_hinweis: Gebaut aus werkzeuge\eden_rise\ereignisse_*.py - dort aendern, dann ereignisse_basis.py laufen lassen.

kein_gras_an_bord.label: No weed on board
kein_gras_an_bord.wirkt: Lola a little annoyed every evening; no inspection risk with Elsa over the weed

gras_nur_nach_dienst.label: Weed only off duty, never on deck
gras_nur_nach_dienst.wirkt: Lola's evening event stays possible; Holm/Chiara events with weed on deck drop out

drei_minuten_dusche.label: Three-minute showers
drei_minuten_dusche.wirkt: Rosi +2 trust every evening: her batteries can breathe

essen_geteilt.label: Food is shared, not hoarded
essen_geteilt.wirkt: Crew Mood +1 every evening, two fewer goods in Totò's locker

kamera_aus_22.label: Cameras off after 10 pm
kamera_aus_22.wirkt: Siri +2 trust in the evening; Yasin's content missions only during the day

kombuese_ordnung.label: Galley order
kombuese_ordnung.wirkt: Chiara +2; Lola's galley gags happen less often

gaestebereich.label: The guest area stays the guest area
gaestebereich.wirkt: −50 € every evening, Megan's pressure events are milder

kein_alkohol_deck.label: No alcohol on deck
kein_alkohol_deck.wirkt: Backing +1 every evening; Alva's bar deliveries to the boat drop out

nachtruhe.label: Lights out at midnight
nachtruhe.wirkt: Energy +1 in the morning; fewer phone events at night

lolas_pesto.label: Lola's “Special Pesto”
lolas_pesto.text: A jar of green pesto. Very green. It lifts the mood, Lola says.

muschelkrone.label: Festa Shell Crown
muschelkrone.text: Glitter, shells and dignity. Visible in the epilogue.

muschelkette_kinder.label: Homemade Shell Necklace with Beads
muschelkette_kinder.text: A thank-you from the village kids. Siri loves it.

frischer_fang.label: Frischer Fang
frischer_fang.text: A bucket of fish. Lola turns it into a feast.

siris_karte.label: Siris Dankeskarte
siris_karte.text: “Thank you for my first birthday without a camera.” Visible in the epilogue.

netzknoten.label: Petrus Netzknoten
netzknoten.text: Once a day: advantage on Empathy.

bauchnabelpiercing.label: Belly Button Piercing with a Shell
bauchnabelpiercing.text: Alva puts it on your tab for Lola. Lola loves it.

rosis_foto.label: A Photo You Shouldn't Delete
rosis_foto.text: Rosi knows you have it. Visible in the epilogue.

eden_cap.label: Eden-Group-Kappe
eden_cap.text: White, with a golden anchor. Totò loves it, Siri hates it.

lolas_gewuerz.label: Lola's Spice Mix
lolas_gewuerz.text: A jar of “Ocean Glitter”. Rosi loves it.

megan_screenshot.label: Wrong Chat
megan_screenshot.text: She says it was a mistake. Megan McAllister doesn't make mistakes. Once a day: advantage on Charm with Megan.

elsas_abzeichen.label: Gendarmerie Maritime Badge
elsas_abzeichen.text: Elsa tossed it to you. Once a day: advantage on Courage.

holms_foto.label: Foto von Holms erstem Kommando
holms_foto.text: A rusty freighter off Bergen, a young woman in a cap.

drohnen_propeller.label: Propeller von Megans Drohne
drohnen_propeller.text: A trophy. Megan wants it back. Never.

ducs_gedicht.label: Duc's Poem About the Sea
ducs_gedicht.text: Rhymes sea with me. Chiara loves it, secretly.

petrus_messer.label: Petrus altes Fischermesser
petrus_messer.text: Once a day: advantage on Perception.

goldfisch.label: Goldfish in a Water Bag
goldfisch.text: Casanova gives it to “the heroine of the bay”. Lea loves it, Chiara hates it.

siris_haarband.label: Siris Haarband
siris_haarband.text: She tucked it into your hair while you were dancing. Visible in the epilogue.

alvas_rose.label: Alvas Rose
alvas_rose.text: A red rose from Alva's hair. Lola and Siri love it.

leas_taucherbrille.label: Leas alte Taucherbrille
leas_taucherbrille.text: +1 Perception while carried. Smells of salt and sun cream.

rosis_handschuhe.label: Rosis Werkstatthandschuhe
rosis_handschuhe.text: +1 Cunning while carried. Too small, but she wanted you to have them.

plektrum.label: Lolas Plektrum
plektrum.text: Once a day: advantage on Charm.

messing_anker.label: Brass Anchor Keyring
messing_anker.text: Rusty, fished out of the bay. Holm would love it.

seeglas.label: Green Sea Glass
seeglas.text: Worn smooth by the sea. Siri loves it.

alvas_schluessel.label: Key to Alva's Back Room
alvas_schluessel.text: On a red cord. Opens the bar's back room, also for quiet talks without witnesses.

rose_festa.label: The Mayor's Rose
rose_festa.text: From Madame Casanova's hair, after the flamenco. Used once: desire +6 with all the women.

control_chip.label: Control Chip
control_chip.text: A small black chip, grown into the lion's collar. Engraved: “A.V. Estates – Behaviour Control Unit”.

alva_selfie_3.label: Last Round
alva_selfie_3.text: careful. say things like that and i start believing them. keep it 🍷

alva_selfie_5.label: Nobody's Mine
alva_selfie_5.text: …ok. that one counts. keep it. keep me a bit too 🌙

alva_selfie_4.label: On the House
alva_selfie_4.text: the whole village is asleep. no excuses then 💋

bibi_selfie_3.label: No Animals
bibi_selfie_3.text: ...ok that's the nicest thing anyone's said to me. keep it. don't show danzel

bibi_selfie_5.label: The Door's Shut
bibi_selfie_5.text: you don't have to walk. you just have to come. keep this one, it's only for you

bibi_selfie_4.label: Washed for You
bibi_selfie_4.text: stop. you're making me laugh at 1am and the hyena is judging me. keep it 🖤

chiara_selfie_3.label: Out of Ten
chiara_selfie_3.text: Eleven isn't on the scale. …Okay. Keep it. Don't you dare show anyone 🔥

chiara_selfie_5.label: Off the Scale
chiara_selfie_5.text: …Nobody ever says that. Keep it. Keep the quiet one too.

chiara_selfie_4.label: No Number
chiara_selfie_4.text: Winning feels better than I thought. Keep it. And come up.

elsa_selfie_3.label: Status Report
elsa_selfie_3.text: Noted. Filed. Not deleted. You may keep the evidence.

elsa_selfie_5.label: Case Closed
elsa_selfie_5.text: I'll write that down. In my private file. Keep this. Don't lose it.

elsa_selfie_4.label: For the File
elsa_selfie_4.text: …That's not a fact. It's an opinion. I'll allow it. Keep it.

isabelle_selfie_3.label: Lavender
isabelle_selfie_3.text: nobody has ever said that to me. I'll keep that. you keep this 🌿

isabelle_selfie_5.label: Confession
isabelle_selfie_5.text: …then I won't ask for forgiveness. only for you. keep it 🕯️

isabelle_selfie_4.label: Patience
isabelle_selfie_4.text: I don't feel brave. I feel like jelly. but thank you. keep it

jana_selfie_3.label: Wrong Photo
jana_selfie_3.text: really?? Jessas. okay. I'm keeping this message forever. you keep the photo 🥺

jana_selfie_5.label: Slip Knot
jana_selfie_5.text: okay. okay. now I'm saying sorry to my pillow because I'm so happy. keep it 🥺

jana_selfie_4.label: Brave
jana_selfie_4.text: me?? brave?? …okay. I'll try to believe it. keep it, Sir

lea_selfie_3.label: For Science
lea_selfie_3.text: better than the whole ocean?? …okay. keep it. I'm going to scream into my pillow now 🙈

lea_selfie_5.label: No Fact for This
lea_selfie_5.text: …okay. then no facts. just you and me. keep it, Duc

lea_selfie_4.label: Nervous Colours
lea_selfie_4.text: really? like octopus nervous? okay. good. keep it 💙

lola_selfie_3.label: Rate the Chef
lola_selfie_3.text: okay okay okay. keep it. don't show Rosi, Rosi tells everyone 😂

lola_selfie_4.label: Not the Bao
lola_selfie_4.text: …oh. okay. that's. I'm not crying, it's the onions. keep it 🥺

megan_selfie_3.label: Third Quarter
megan_selfie_3.text: I know. That's precisely why I sent it. Keep it, Duc.

megan_selfie_5.label: No Conditions
megan_selfie_5.text: Then I won't. …Keep it. Keep me, if you're brave enough.

megan_selfie_4.label: Your Move
megan_selfie_4.text: …Nobody has ever said that and meant it. Keep it.

rosi_selfie_3.label: Proof Attached
rosi_selfie_3.text: a draw. fine. I'll take a draw. keep it, Officer 😏

rosi_selfie_5.label: Tactical Surrender
rosi_selfie_5.text: that's the dumbest thing anyone has ever said to me. keep it. …Captain.

rosi_selfie_4.label: Draw
rosi_selfie_4.text: …okay. don't make me soft, Officer. keep it

siri_selfie_3.label: Not the Camera Voice
siri_selfie_3.text: real. nobody says that to me. keep it. it's yours 🤍

siri_selfie_5.label: No Filter
siri_selfie_5.text: …okay, I'm crying a bit. good crying. keep it

siri_selfie_4.label: Just for One
siri_selfie_4.text: it's me. huh. keep it, Duc. I like being me with you

sophia_selfie_3.label: Research Material
sophia_selfie_3.text: Oh. That's going in. Word for word. You keep the photo, I keep the line.

sophia_selfie_5.label: No Bet Tonight
sophia_selfie_5.text: So am I. Keep it. And keep asking me, would you?

sophia_selfie_4.label: The Forfeit
sophia_selfie_4.text: …Darling. That was dangerously accurate. Keep it.

laetitia_scarf.label: Laetitia's Red Scarf
laetitia_scarf.text: A faded red scarf, still damp from the lake. It smells of woodsmoke and of a girl who left in a hurry.

av_radio.label: A.V. Estates Radio
av_radio.text: A black field radio with a small white logo: A.V. Estates. The last channel used is still set.

ir_controller.label: Collar Controller
ir_controller.text: A grey handset with an infrared lamp and a dial. Every blinking collar on the mountain answers to it.

ghjuvan_knife.label: Ghjuvan's Father's Knife
ghjuvan_knife.text: A shepherd's knife with a horn handle worn smooth by three generations of the same thumb.

foreign_part.label: The Part That Isn't Ours
foreign_part.text: A small black module, warm to the touch, with a stamped code and a tiny white logo. Rosi pulled it out of Unit-01's control board. It doesn't belong to anything on this boat.

gennaro_drawing.label: Giulia's Drawing
gennaro_drawing.text: A child's drawing of a man with a big moustache in a boat. Underneath, in crooked letters: PAPÀ.

collar_crate.label: The Crate from Antibes
collar_crate.text: A heavy plastic crate with a stamped code and a small white logo. Inside, in foam, forty new collars and a box of control chips. You saw this crate before, in a hangar in Antibes.

ghjacumu_medal.label: Ghjacumu's Medal
ghjacumu_medal.text: A small tin medal of Saint Erasmus, patron of sailors, on a green string. The string has been chewed.

bastien_ring.label: A Ring in a Velvet Box
bastien_ring.text: A ring with a tiny blue stone. The receipt is still in the box. Marseille, March.

treasure_notes.label: Chloé's Notes
treasure_notes.text: A waterproof folder: photos of an old schooner, sonar printouts, and a map of the bay with a red circle on it.

lea_chart_page.label: Page Forty
lea_chart_page.text: A page torn from Lea's chart book: her grandfather's pencil marks, a bay, a cross, and a date from 1924. In the margin, in older pencil: “She sings at the pool when the tide is in.”

babel_badge.label: Employee Badge
babel_badge.text: A staff badge with the logo taped over. Only one word is left to read: BABEL. Whoever taped it did it neatly.

postcard_bibi.label: Postcard from a Zoo
postcard_bibi.text: Giraffes and a French stamp, in big fast handwriting: “I finally went. They have a lion who snores. I'm okay. I think.” No address to write back to.

postcard_charly.label: Postcard from Paris
postcard_charly.text: No sender, postmarked Paris, a very ugly statue on the front. On the back there is only “2/10”. You can't tell if she means the statue.

fish_sauce.label: Fish Sauce
fish_sauce.text: Amber, salty, and a smell that gets into your shirt and stays until Christmas. It comes from a cousin in Marseille, and she won't say which cousin. Everybody says it stinks. Everybody comes back.

kl_post.label: Three Weeks of Post
kl_post.text: A bundle of letters in a rubber band, three weeks thick. Mina couldn't get past the bridge. Some of them are for people you still have to find.

old_camel_coat.label: Old Camel Coat
old_camel_coat.text: Heavy camel wool from the thirties, with an English tailor's mark worn nearly smooth. It has been lost at cards at least twice. Both times, someone was very upset.

events.lage: Clearing out the galley freezer to save power, Rosi found a kilo of weed. Neatly vacuum-packed and labelled “BASIL ♥”. She drops the bag on the table in front of you and folds her arms.

zeilen.text: Found this behind the fish. Holm's gone, so it's your crew now, Officer. Let's see what you do with it.
Overboard, tonight. If the coast guard finds that, we lose the boat and every licence we've got.
Comandante, overboard is a crime against nature. I keep it safe, nobody knows, and Lola stays happy. Everybody wins.

optionen.text: “Chiara's right. The bag goes overboard tonight.”
Pushes the bag over to Totò. “Keep it safe, and nobody knows.”
Ship's rule: only after duty, never on deck.

zeile.text: Hm. Diplomatic. Holm would have thrown it at the moon. We'll see if your rule holds.

optionen.text: Promise to Chiara: “From tomorrow I'll check the galley myself.”

events.lage: The watermaker can't keep up with thirteen people. Sophia has drawn a shower schedule on a napkin. At the bottom there's a sad face.

zeilen.text: Thirteen people, one watermaker. Someone's going to cry in a cold shower tomorrow, darling. We just have to decide who.
Three minutes each, on a schedule, and guests go first. That's the job.
Give my minutes to the crew. Honestly, it's fine. I can wash my hair in the sea, I grew up doing that.

optionen.text: Ship's rule: the three-minute shower.
Takes Siri's side. “The guests give their shower minutes to the crew.”
Lea builds a saltwater shower on the swim platform.

events.lage: Megan has written: the guest cabins are to be stripped and the minibars counted. Today. Chiara reads the message out without moving a muscle in her face.

zeilen.text: Megan wants the guest cabins stripped and the minibars counted tonight. She calls it cost discipline, and I call it humiliating.
Do half, darling. Count the minibars, leave the cabins. She gets her numbers and nobody loses face.
I'm still sleeping in one of those cabins. Just so everyone remembers that.

optionen.text: “Count the minibars and leave the cabins, like Sophia says.”
“No stripping and no counting. The guest cabins stay as they are.”
Ship's rule: the guest area stays the guest area.
Picks up the phone. “I'll call Megan myself.”

events.lage: Yasin is offering five hundred euros if the crew plays along in his video tomorrow. “Stranded with an Influencer”, with laughs, drama and bikinis. Sophia puts the envelope on the table.

zeilen.text: Five hundred euros in cash, darling. He wants the crew in his video tomorrow, with smiles, drama and swimwear.
It's free publicity, bro. My people love a shipwreck. You'll be famous. Small famous, but famous.
We are not his props. We work here, and some of us would like to keep working here.

optionen.text: Takes the envelope. “Everyone plays along in Yasin's video tomorrow.”
Pushes the envelope back. “We are not your props, Yasin.”
“Whoever wants to be in the video can be. Nobody has to.”
Ship's rule: cameras off after ten.

events.titel: The Crew as a Festa Attraction
events.lage: Madame Casanova wants the crew on a stage at the festa, in sailor costumes, with a song. Rosi holds up the letter and can't stop laughing.

zeilen.text: The mayor wants us on stage in sailor costumes, singing, and she drew a picture, Officer. There's an actual picture.
Yes! Yes yes yes. I can do the dance. I already know a dance, I've known it for years.
Absolutely not. We are a professional crew, not a cruise-ship cabaret.

optionen.text: “We'll do the mayor's show. Costumes, song, everything.”
“Thank the mayor for us, and tell her no.”
“Nobody else has to do it. I'll sing for the mayor, alone.”

zeile.text: Oh no. Oh, this I have to see.

events.lage: Someone has to watch the anchor until sunrise. Rosi has barely slept, but she says she can do it. Lea volunteers so fast she nearly falls off her chair.

zeilen.text: Someone has to watch the anchor until sunrise, and Rosi has slept four hours since we got here.
I'm fine, I'm Sicilian. We don't sleep, we just close our eyes angrily for a while.
Me! Let me. I've never done a real night watch. I'll be so awake. Look how awake I am already.

optionen.text: Gives the night watch to Rosi. “You're Sicilian. Close your eyes angrily up there.”
Gives the night watch to Lea. “Stay awake, and wake me if the anchor moves.”
Keeps the night watch himself. “Go to bed, both of you.”
Ship's rule: quiet hours from midnight, and a watch rota.

events.lage: Petru will take two of the crew fishing at dawn. Whoever goes is gone until noon. Lea already has her boots on.

zeilen.text: Petru's taking two of us fishing at dawn. Real fishing! With nets! I'm going. Who else?
And he says if we catch enough, Alva buys the rest. Money and dinner, Duc!
I need hands here tomorrow, not on a fishing boat. But fine, go on, abandon me.

optionen.text: Goes with Lea and Petru at dawn. “Back by noon, Rosi.”
“Nobody goes, Lea. Rosi needs every hand here tomorrow.”
“Lea and Totò go with Petru. I stay here.”

events.lage: Lieutenant Ferrandi has announced an inspection for tomorrow. Totò goes pale and glances towards the storeroom. Chiara sees it.

zeilen.text: Lieutenant Ferrandi inspects us tomorrow at ten. She asked, very politely, whether we have anything to declare.
Comandante, a few boxes take a little boat trip tonight, and they're back tomorrow evening. Nobody sees nothing.
Or we declare everything and stop being a floating flea market.

optionen.text: Nods at Totò. “Take the crates out tonight, and have them back tomorrow evening.”
Sides with Chiara. “We declare everything to Elsa.”
Call Elsa today and talk to her honestly.

events.lage: Every day three kids from the village row out to the yacht and stare. Today they held up a sign: “Tour please?” Lea took a photo of it.

zeilen.text: They made a sign, Duc. A sign! “Tour please.” With a drawing of us. I'm the one with the big hair.
Children on a superyacht with no power? The insurance would die, and then I would die.
Let them come. I'll show them the sea turtles on my phone. They don't care about the gold taps anyway.

optionen.text: “Chiara's right. No kids on board, it's too risky.”
“Let the kids come for a tour in the afternoon.”
Lea only shows them the swim platform, in life jackets.

events.lage: Lola found Siri's passport in the laundry. It's her birthday tomorrow, and she hasn't told anyone. Yasin knew, but he has other plans.

zeilen.text: It's Siri's birthday tomorrow and she didn't tell anyone. That's the saddest thing I've ever heard, mate.
Something small, breakfast on the foredeck with no cameras, just us. I'll organise it.
Bro, I have a whole concept. Drone shot, champagne, a sponsored cake. It's content. She loves content.

optionen.text: “Sophia organises a small breakfast on the foredeck, with no cameras.”

zeile.text: Thank you for my first birthday without a camera. I mean it. Don't make it weird.

optionen.text: Lets Yasin have his way. “Drone, champagne, sponsored cake. Do it.”
Lola bakes something, and only the crew sings.

events.titel: Yacht Stuff for the Crew Fund?
events.lage: Totò has made a list. Two crates of champagne, four bathrobes, a spare propeller. All Eden Group property, all easy to sell.

zeilen.text: Totò made a list of things nobody would miss. It's a long list. It's a very confident list.
Two crates of champagne, Comandante. The Group writes it off as breakage, and we eat for a week.
That is theft, with a list, in handwriting.

optionen.text: Nods at Totò's list. “Sell it all. We have to eat.”
Hands the list back to Totò. “No. That's stealing from the Group.”
“Sell the champagne, but only to Alva. The rest stays on board.”

events.lage: Lola is lying in her bunk with sunstroke, mumbling recipes. So someone else cooks tomorrow. Rosi has already tied on an apron. That scares everyone.

zeilen.text: Lola has sunstroke and is reciting risotto in her sleep. Someone else cooks tomorrow.
I'll cook, how hard can it be? It's just chemistry with garlic.
Or we order from Alva, darling, and nobody gets poisoned. Just a thought.

optionen.text: “All right, Rosi. You cook tomorrow.”

zeile.text: If anyone says the word “burnt”, they sleep on deck.

optionen.text: Sides with Sophia. “We order from Alva, and nobody gets poisoned.”
Takes the apron off Rosi. “I'll cook tomorrow.”

events.lage: Kevin the seagull has built a nest on the solar deck. Right on top of a panel. He makes a mess of anything he doesn't like. He doesn't like anything.

zeilen.text: Kevin built a nest on panel four. Panel four now makes eight percent less power and one hundred percent more poop.
You can't move a nest! What if there are eggs? What if Kevin's a mum?
In Napoli we have a word for a fat seagull, Comandante. The word is dinner.

optionen.text: “Leave the nest. Kevin can stay on panel four.”
“The nest goes, and so does Kevin. Sorry, Lea.”

zeile.text: I will never forgive you. Ever. Maybe tomorrow.

optionen.text: Move the nest carefully to the railing.

events.lage: Lola wants to sing on the aft deck tomorrow night. Just a guitar, candles and everyone. Siri would sing along, but only if nobody films it. Yasin has already unpacked his tripod.

zeilen.text: Tomorrow night: candles, my guitar, everyone sings. No speakers, no power, just vibes.
I'd sing, really, I would, but only if nobody films it. Not one second.
Babe, unplugged content performs insane. It's authentic. I'll just film a little bit.

optionen.text: Takes Siri's side. “No phones and no cameras tomorrow night. That means you, Yasin.”
Yasin can film. He pays for the footage.
Ship's rule: cameras off after ten.

events.lage: Until now the guests have eaten in the salon and the crew in the mess. Lola thinks that's silly now that everyone's in the same boat. Chiara doesn't think etiquette is silly.

zeilen.text: Guests in the salon, crew in the mess. Lola wants one table for everyone. Chiara wants a word with Lola.
There are rules for a reason. Guests pay for distance, even stranded guests.
We're all stuck in the same bay, mate, so let's eat like a family. A weird family, with a seagull.

optionen.text: “Chiara's right. Guests in the salon, crew in the mess.”
Sides with Lola. “One table for everyone, guests and crew.”
“One evening a week, we all eat together.”

events.lage: Megan lands tomorrow by helicopter. Chiara wants to polish all night. Rosi wants to show Megan how broken everything is, with a sign.

zeilen.text: Megan lands tomorrow, and I want this boat to shine, every brass handle and every glass.
If she sees one fingerprint, she'll mention it in front of everyone. Slowly.
Or we let her see the truth. I'll make a sign that says broken, in three languages.

optionen.text: “Chiara's right. We polish the whole boat tonight, every handle and every glass.”
“Make your sign, Rosi. Let Megan see the truth.”

zeile.text: Broken, kaputt, rotto, and a little drawing underneath. She'll love it.

optionen.text: “We polish the salon and nothing else.”

events.lage: Lea and Siri went skinny dipping last night. Elsa's patrol boat came past at exactly that moment. With a searchlight.

zeilen.text: So. Lea and Siri went skinny dipping. And Lieutenant Ferrandi's patrol boat has a searchlight. A very good one.
It was romantic! The plankton was glowing! And then a boat was glowing. At us.
The coast guard has now seen half our crew naked, so I need a rule. I need several rules.

optionen.text: Shrugs at Chiara. “Nothing happened, really. Two people went for a swim.”
“Chiara gets her rule. From now on, swimwear only.”
Send Elsa a letter of apology, with Lola's cake.

events.lage: For three days Rosi has worked more than sixteen hours a day. Today she fell asleep standing up in the engine room. Chiara wants you to forbid it.

zeilen.text: Rosi fell asleep standing up today, darling. With a screwdriver in her mouth.
I'm fine. One more day, then I sleep. Promise. Maybe. Don't look at me like that.
Order her to rest. She won't listen to me, but she listens to you, apparently.

optionen.text: “All right, Rosi. One more day, then you sleep.”
“You take tomorrow off, Rosi. That's an order.”

zeile.text: Fine. Fine! I'll rest. Aggressively.

optionen.text: Promise to Rosi: “I'll take your late shift tomorrow.”

events.lage: Petru won't take money for his fish. He wants something else: tomorrow morning two of the crew mend his nets. Three hours, in the sun, with an old man who doesn't talk.

zeilen.text: Petru won't take money for the fish. He wants two of us to mend his nets tomorrow. Three hours.
Three hours I don't have. Pay the man in euros, like a normal person.
He said euros are for tourists, nets are for friends. I think that's beautiful, honestly.

optionen.text: Sides with Rosi. “We pay Petru in euros for the fish.”
“Lea and I will mend his nets tomorrow.”
“Send Totò to Petru instead, with a bottle of wine.”

events.lage: Siri asked Sophia whether there's a free bunk in one of the crew cabins. Just for a few nights. Yasin has found out, and now he's standing in the corridor.

zeilen.text: Siri asked if a crew bunk is free, just for a few nights. Yasin found out, and now he's in the corridor.
I just need a bit of space. To sleep. To think. That's all. Please don't make this a thing.
Bro, she's my girlfriend. She sleeps in the VIP cabin. With me. That's not a crew decision.

optionen.text: “Give Siri the crew bunk, Sophia. That's my decision, Yasin.”

zeile.text: Thank you. Really. You didn't have to.

optionen.text: Stays out of it. “You two sort this out yourselves.”
“It's Siri's choice. If she moves, the crew helps her.”

events.lage: Yasin gave Lea an envelope with two hundred and fifty euros in it. “For you, sweetheart. You can thank me later.” Lea holds it between two fingers, as if it were wet.

zeilen.text: Yasin gave me this. Two hundred and fifty euros. He said I could thank him later. I don't want to thank him later.
I just want to give it back. But then he'll be weird about it. Weirder.
Two-fifty is two-fifty, cara. Put it in the crew box. He can thank himself in the mirror.

optionen.text: Takes the envelope from Lea. “I'll give it back and talk to Yasin.”
“Totò's right, Lea. Put it in the crew box.”
Back to Yasin, in front of everyone at breakfast.

events.lage: Madame Casanova wants to make you an honorary citizen at the festa. With a sash, a crown of shells and a speech. She has already made the crown. Rosi has a photo.

zeilen.text: The mayor made you a crown out of shells, Officer. There's glitter on it. So much glitter.
You have to! You'd be a prince! A shell prince! I'll carry your train!
The First Officer will not wear a shell crown in public. I forbid it on behalf of the uniform.

optionen.text: “Tell the mayor yes. I'll wear the crown.”
Sides with Chiara. “No shell crown for me. Thank the mayor kindly.”
Accept, but Chiara gives the speech.

events.lage: Megan is on board and wants to host a dinner for two investors tomorrow. On the dead yacht, by candlelight. The crew is to serve as if everything were normal.

zeilen.text: Megan wants a dinner tomorrow, darling, with two investors, eight courses and candles, on our dead boat. With a smile.
A stranded yacht is a story, First Officer, and I sell stories. Your crew will serve. Beautifully. Or else.
We have rice, tins and one bottle of champagne, and my people are exhausted. This is madness.

optionen.text: Nods to Megan. “Eight courses and candles, as you want it. The crew will serve.”
Looks at Megan. “No dinner. This crew is exhausted.”
Lola cooks, and the crew eats at the table too.

zeile.text: The crew at the table, with my investors. You're either a genius or insane, and I'm intrigued.

events.lage: Tomorrow everything gets decided. Lola wants a party tonight. Chiara wants everyone asleep. They're both a little bit right.

zeilen.text: Whatever happens tomorrow, tonight we dance, barefoot on the aft deck, and that means everyone.
I saved a bottle and a cake, and a joint, but that's just for me. Mostly.
Tomorrow we need clear heads, so everyone's in their bunk by midnight. Please.

optionen.text: Sides with Lola. “We dance tonight, and that means everyone.”
“Chiara's right. Everyone in their bunk by midnight.”
“We dance until midnight, then I send everyone to bed.”

events.lage: Alva calls from the bar. Behind her, Lola is dancing barefoot on the counter. The fishermen are clapping.

zeilen.text: O figliolu, your cook is teaching my fishermen to twerk. It's very educational.
Come and get her. Or don't. Bring nothing but yourself.
BOSS! The universe says hi!

optionen.text: Takes the tender over.
“Let her dance. Put it on my tab.”
Has Chiara call her.

events.lage: At 02:13 Sophia texts: “Are you awake?” Then she calls. She's lying in the dark, her face lit only by the screen. The notebook rests on her chest, and the duvet has slipped a long way down.

zeilen.text: I wrote something about you. I want to read it to you before I lose my nerve.
He listens like it costs him nothing, and that is the most expensive thing I've ever been given.
Okay. That's all. Unless you want to tell me what you'd do if you were here. Slowly.
You already know how this one ends, darling. You were there. I'm only writing it down.

optionen.text: “Read it again.”
Quietly tells her what he'd do.

zeile.text: Keep talking. Don't stop. I'm… my hand is already… God, Duc. Don't stop.

optionen.text: Just “Good night, Sophia.”
Doesn't pick up.

events.nachklang_text: You hardly slept. Her voice at 02:13 is still there, very close to your ear.

events.lage: Holm is lying in a hospital bed with tubes in her arm, her hair down for once. She looks pale, and very angry that she isn't on board.

zeilen.text: They took my appendix and my boat on the same day. Only one of them I want back. How is she?
And don't lie to me, Frankfurt. I can hear it in your voice when you lie. You get polite.

optionen.text: Tells her honestly how bad it is.

zeile.text: Good. Now I know you'll tell me the truth when it matters.

optionen.text: Reassures her: “Everything's under control.”
Asks for her advice.

zeile.text: Trust your engineer. Feed your crew. And never let them see you guess.

events.lage: Holm calls in the middle of the night. The painkillers have made her talkative. She tells you about her first command, a rusty freighter out of Bergen.

zeilen.text: My first command was a rust bucket out of Bergen. Thirty-one, terrified, and nobody listened to me for a month.
Then one night I said, I don't know, let's find out together. After that they listened. Funny, hm?

optionen.text: Listens until she falls asleep.
Tells her about himself.
“Get some sleep, Captain.”

events.lage: Megan calls at 23:40. She's still at the office, shoes off, a glass of whisky in her hand. Behind her the harbour glitters.

zeilen.text: Everyone in this building is afraid of me. It's very boring. Entertain me, First Officer.
And don't mention the boat. I know about the boat. Tell me something nobody tells me.

optionen.text: Tells her something personal.
Flirts with her.

zeile.text: Careful. I bite. Contractually.

optionen.text: “Go home, Megan.”

zeile.text: Nobody tells me to go home. …Fine. You first.

events.lage: Megan has decided that someone from the crew gets fired. You're to name them. Now.

zeilen.text: I've decided someone gets fired. For morale. Pick a name. You have ten seconds.
Nine. Eight. I'm counting in my head, it's more threatening.

optionen.text: Gives her no name.

zeile.text: Correct answer. It was a test. Nobody ever passes. Ahaha— don't tell anyone I laughed.

optionen.text: “Then fire me.”
Suggests Totò, as a joke.

events.lage: Elsa calls from the harbour. She's speaking quietly. Tomorrow morning there'll be a raid for smuggling in the bay. She isn't saying it as a police officer.

zeilen.text: I never called you. Tomorrow, seven o'clock, we search every boat in the bay. Every locker.
If your bosun has something he shouldn't, tonight would be a good night for swimming lessons.

optionen.text: “Thank you, Elsa.” Warns Totò.
Doesn't warn Totò.
“Why are you helping me?”

zeile.text: Because you didn't try to bribe me. People always try. You just asked questions.

events.lage: Elsa needs help. A small sailboat is drifting off the bay with two tourists on board and a dead engine. Her patrol boat is too far away.

zeilen.text: A little sailboat is drifting at the mouth of the bay. Two Germans, no engine, a lot of shouting.
My boat is twenty minutes out. Your tender is two. Can you help?

optionen.text: Lea takes the tender.
Duc goes himself.
“No time, sorry.”

events.lage: A message from an unknown number: “Gennaro here. Parcel comes tonight. Tell Salvatore the goat is coming too 🐐” Totò is Salvatore. Totò is reading over your shoulder, and he goes pale.

zeilen.text: Comandante. That message. It's a wrong number. Gennaro is a very common name. Very common. Goats too.
Okay. Okay. My cousin brings a small parcel tonight. And maybe a small goat. It's a long story.

optionen.text: “No goat on board.”
“How small is the goat?”

zeile.text: Small! Medium. A medium goat. She's very polite.

optionen.text: Tips off Elsa.

events.lage: Lola calls from ashore. She was only supposed to buy lemons. Now she's standing in Petru's workshop with a goat on a lead and no idea how that happened.

zeilen.text: Boss. Don't be mad. I went for lemons, and now I have a goat. Her name's Fiona. She chose me.
Petru says she eats everything. I said, same, girl. We bonded.

optionen.text: “Fiona comes with us.”
“Take her back. And bring the lemons.”
Asks Petru what's going on.

zeile.text: He just pointed at the goat and then at me. Very poetic, mate.

events.lage: Rosi sends a photo of the spare part she's looking for. It isn't a spare part. It's a mirror selfie in a towel, fresh out of the shower. Thirty seconds later she calls.

zeilen.text: DELETE THAT. That was the wrong photo. The part is the other photo. Why aren't you deleting it?
…Unless you liked it. Did you like it? Say something, you idiot, I'm dying here.
…Officer, you've seen more than that anyway. So why am I this red?

optionen.text: “I'll delete it. Right after I save it.”

zeile.text: You're the worst. Keep it. I'll send you a better one when I'm brave.

optionen.text: Tells her how much he liked it.

zeile.text: Okay. Okay. Then this one's on purpose. Don't show Totò.

optionen.text: Really deletes it, the perfect gentleman.

events.nachklang_text: A steamed-up mirror, a towel, Rosi's grin. At breakfast she asks, too loudly, whether anyone has seen a spare part.

events.lage: Lea calls from the swim platform. She's holding the phone in the water. Every movement makes the plankton glow blue. She whispers as if she were in a church.

zeilen.text: Look. Look look look. Every time I move my hand, the sea lights up. Like it's happy to see me.
I didn't want to see this alone. Come down? Just for a minute. I'll be quiet. I'll try.
You've been down here with me before, so you know how this goes. I'll talk, and you'll stay.

optionen.text: Goes down.

zeile.text: Give me your hand. In the water. See? Now we're both glowing.

optionen.text: Swims with her.
“Send me a video.”

events.nachklang_text: Blue light between your fingers. In the morning Lea has salt in her hair and smiles at you as if you shared a secret.

events.lage: Siri calls from the foredeck. No make-up, hair tied back, an old jumper. She says it's the first time in years she's called anyone without a filter.

zeilen.text: No ring light, no filter. This is just my face. It's the first time in two years I've called someone like this.
Say something nice. Or say something true. I can't tell which one I need.
You've seen this face with a lot less on it. I don't know why a phone still makes me nervous. Sorry.

optionen.text: Says something true.
Says something kind.
Asks her to switch the camera off and just talk.

events.nachklang_text: Her face without a filter, her laugh without an audience. At breakfast she's wearing make-up again, but she winks at you.

events.lage: Megan wants a tour, live by video, right now. You walk through the yacht with the phone, and she comments on everything.

zeilen.text: Walk me through my boat. Now. And hold the phone straight, I get seasick through screens.
Why is there a goat. No, don't explain. Show me the engineer. Is she working? She looks like she's working.

optionen.text: Shows Rosi at work.

zeile.text: Hello, Mrs Boss. Everything is broken. Lovely to meet you.

optionen.text: Shows Lola's galley.

zeile.text: Hiii! Want a cookie? It's a normal cookie. Mostly.

optionen.text: “No signal!” Hangs up.

events.lage: Alva has one canister of diesel left. She won't sell it, but she'll trade it for a dance, tonight, on her bar, in front of the whole village.

zeilen.text: One canister. Not for money. For a dance. Tonight. On my bar. In front of everyone.
Don't make that face. You'll be wonderful. And if not, you'll be funny. Both sell drinks.

optionen.text: Dances.
Sends Lola.
“I'd rather pay.”

events.lage: Sophia sends a short message: Chiara has been sitting alone in the pantry for an hour, staring at a cup. Maybe someone could bring her a fresh coffee.

zeilen.text: Chiara has been staring at one cup for an hour. I'd go, but she'd pretend to be fine for me. Not for you. ☕
Two sugars. She'll say she doesn't take sugar. She takes two. 🙄

optionen.text: Brings her a coffee.
Thanks Sophia, goes later.
“Why don't you go?”

zeile.text: Because I organise people, darling. You actually see them. 😘

events.lage: Lola calls from the galley, her face covered in flour. She's invented something and needs a taster right now. Behind her a pot is smoking, but in a good way.

zeilen.text: Boss, emergency. I invented a dish. It's either the best thing ever or a crime. I need a mouth. Yours.
It's got fish, lemon, fennel and a secret. The secret is love. And chilli. Mostly the chilli.
And don't look at me like that, Boss. I know what that mouth's good for, that's why I rang.

optionen.text: Runs straight over to taste it.

zeile.text: Your face! Is that a good face? That's a good face. I'm crying.

optionen.text: Sends Rosi.
“I trust you. Just go for it.”

events.lage: Holm calls on the evening before the hearing. She's sitting up straight in bed, wearing her captain's cap, just for this call.

zeilen.text: Tomorrow it gets decided, one way or another. I wanted you to hear it from me before it does.
She's your boat now, Frankfurt. Whatever you choose, choose it out loud. They'll follow that.

optionen.text: “Thank you, Captain.”
“She'll come back to you.”

zeile.text: Good. Then take care of her for me. Both of you.

optionen.text: Asks her for one last order.

zeile.text: Sleep. That's the order. Heroes who don't sleep make bad decisions.

events.lage: Twenty to midnight. A photo from the private number, no text. A tall mirror in a bedroom above Port Hercule, the harbour lights behind her, and Megan in nothing but a thin gold chain with a small anchor. Forty seconds later, a second message.

zeilen.text: That was meant for a different chat. I'd think very carefully about what you do next, First Officer.
Delete it. Or don't. But if anyone on that boat ever sees it, I'll know exactly whose phone it came from. ⚓

optionen.text: Deletes it and says nothing.

zeile.text: Hm. A gentleman. How disappointing. 🙄 Goodnight, Duc.

optionen.text: Keeps it.

zeile.text: There is no other chat, is there. Goodnight, Duc. Delete nothing. 🖤

optionen.text: Sends back a photo of the radar screen.

zeile.text: A radar screen. 📡 How... romantic. Go to sleep, First Officer.

events.lage: Totò calls in a panic, whispering. Someone is in his locker. He can hear rustling and crunching. He doesn't dare open the door.

zeilen.text: Comandante. Someone is in my locker. I hear rustling. Crunching. Come quick, and bring something heavy.
Oh. Oh no. It has wings. It has wings and it's eating my cigars.

optionen.text: Heads over with a broom.

zeile.text: Kevin. Of course it's Kevin. He took a cigar. He looks happier than me.

optionen.text: Sends Lea.
Laughs out loud.

events.lage: Lola has baked a pancake portrait of everyone on board, and she was obviously high while doing it. Rosi's pancake is beautiful. Chiara's face is a slightly burnt circle with a syrup frown.

zeilen.text: I made all of you, out of love and flour! Chiara, yours is very accurate, actually.
Is that supposed to be my face?

optionen.text: Praises Chiara's pancake.
Eats his own portrait first.

zeile.text: You ate my heart, Boss. Literally.

optionen.text: Asks Lola for a second portrait of Chiara.

events.lage: A black Eden Group drone is flying an inspection. Megan's voice comes out of its speaker. The drone is chasing Totò, because he ran off with a crate.

zeilen.text: Mister Esposito. What's in the box? No, don't run. Running is a confession.
It's FISH, signora! Confidential fish!

optionen.text: Covers for Totò: “It's fish.”
Lea catches the drone with the landing net.

zeile.text: Impressive. Give that girl a raise, but not a big one.

optionen.text: Shows the drone what's in the crate.

events.lage: Rosi is stuck head first in a service hatch. The zip of her coverall has caught. As she crawls back out, the coverall slides down to her hips. Underneath she's only wearing an old sports bra, and it's sitting crooked.

zeilen.text: Don't say anything, just pull me out. By the hips. No, the HIPS, Officer.
You're staring, and that's good, because I was starting to think you only liked the engine.
Comandante, I bring the coffee and— ah. I bring nothing. I was never here.

optionen.text: Pulls her coverall back up, the perfect gentleman.
Sends everyone out, shuts the door and fixes the zip.

zeile.text: It's fixed? Good, then leave it, because I don't think I'm putting it back on. Come here.

optionen.text: “I didn't see a thing.” With a look.

klatsch.was: Duc and Rosi in the generator room

events.nachklang_text: Oil on your fingers, her laugh in the generator room. At breakfast Rosi is wearing a new coverall and grinning into her coffee.

events.lage: Unit-01 coughed. In front of Totò. Rosi gives the housing one loving whack with her ring spanner. Unit-01 coughs back: a black cloud of soot through the ventilation shaft, straight into the galley. Lea is standing there covered in soot, holding half a cake.

zeilen.text: Unit-01 coughed at me. COUGHED, in front of Totò, so now this is personal.
Um. Rosi? There's soot. On me. On the cake. The cake is a chimney now.

optionen.text: “Again. Harder.”
Takes the spanner off her.

zeile.text: Fine. But she started it.

optionen.text: Wipes the soot off Lea and rescues the cake.

events.lage: Rosi has changed tactics. She's singing Unit-01 a Sicilian lullaby, one hand on the housing. She claims machines listen.

zeilen.text: My nonna sang this to tractors, and those tractors never died. Shh, she's listening.
Can I join in? I know the tune. I don't know the words. I'll make up the words.

optionen.text: Sings along.
Keeps a straight face and doesn't disturb Rosi.
Takes Totò's phone before he can film this.

zeile.text: Thank you. If that video exists, Totò, you'll be sleeping in the anchor locker.

events.lage: Lea gave the butter to a fat seagull. The last butter. The seagull is now sitting on the railing, checking whether there's more.

zeilen.text: He looked so hungry! And now he loves me. Look at him. I'm calling him Kevin.
That was the LAST butter, and now Kevin is eating my croissants. Kevin is dead to me.

optionen.text: “Kevin's part of the crew now.”
Buys more butter at the village shop.
Shoos Kevin away.

zeile.text: He'll be back. He knows where we live now.

events.lage: Seven in the morning. A fishing boat pulls up alongside the yacht. On it stands Madame Casanova with the village brass band. They're playing the anthem of Cala d'Orsu. Loudly.

zeilen.text: Good morning, heroes of the sea! A welcome song! All four verses! Maestro, again from the top!
It's seven. It's seven in the morning, and I will throw that tuba into the sea.

optionen.text: Applauds.
Sings along, badly but loudly.
Politely asks for a shorter version.

events.lage: Fiona the goat is eating Chiara's uniform cap. Totò is standing next to her, trying to distract her with a croissant. It isn't working. Fiona wants the cap.

zeilen.text: Fiona, cara, look, a croissant! Butter! Leave the hat! The hat is not food, the hat is a uniform!
That goat is eating my career.

optionen.text: Pulls the cap out of Fiona's mouth.
Promises Chiara a new cap.

versprechen.text: Duc gets Chiara a new cap

optionen.text: Lets Fiona eat the cap.

events.lage: Yasin is asleep. Siri has put on some music and is teaching the crew a dance. No camera. She laughs out loud, the way nobody has heard her laugh before.

zeilen.text: Left, left, turn, shoulder. Rosi, the other left. No, the other other left.
My feet are Sicilian. They don't take orders from Norway.

optionen.text: Dances along.
Helps Rosi find her other left.
Pays Siri a compliment when she laughs.
Films it for Yasin's channel. He pays well.

events.lage: Chiara is inspecting the crew cabins in white gloves. She has reached your cabin, and she has found something under the pillow.

zeilen.text: Crew cabin inspection, and that includes officers. Especially officers. What's this under your pillow?
Is this poetry? Did you write poetry about the sea? You rhymed sea with me.

optionen.text: “That's not mine.”
“Read it out loud, if you dare.”

zeile.text: The sea is wide, the sea is free, and someone should come back to me. Oh no. That's actually sweet.

optionen.text: Hands her the poem from under the pillow.

events.lage: Totò is baking Neapolitan pizza on the grill. Lola has brought a pineapple. Totò is shielding the grill with his body.

zeilen.text: Over my dead body. Over my cold, dead, Neapolitan body. No pineapple touches this dough.
It's sweet and salty, mate, so it's balance, like yin and yang. Like you and a shower.

optionen.text: “Totò's right, Lola. No pineapple on his dough.”
A pineapple pizza for Lola, in secret.
“Bake two pizzas, one each, and let a jury decide.”

events.lage: Yasin has set out candles in a heart shape on the sun deck. He's filming live. He wants to tell Siri in front of his followers how much he loves her. Siri stands there and doesn't move.

zeilen.text: Babe, look at the camera. Two hundred thousand people are watching us. Say you love me back.
Yasin. Please. Not like this. Can we just… turn it off?

optionen.text: Steps between Siri and the camera.

zeile.text: Thank you. I couldn't move.

optionen.text: Does nothing; that's their business.
Gives Siri a way out: “Siri, Chiara needs you in the pantry.”

events.lage: Elsa's patrol boat comes alongside. Totò and Lea are out in the tender. Without life jackets. Elsa holds up her ticket book and smiles thinly.

zeilen.text: Two people, one tender, zero life jackets. That's either a crime or a very small miracle.
Lieutenant, the jackets are in our hearts. Spiritually, we are wearing them.

optionen.text: Pays the fine.
Offers Elsa a coffee and talks to her.
Announces a ship's rule: life jackets are mandatory.

events.lage: Petru comes alongside in his boat and, without a word, throws a tuna onto the deck. A big one. Then he points at you, and at a knife. He wants you to gut it.

zeilen.text: You. Take the knife. I show you once.
A whole tuna. A WHOLE TUNA. Petru, I love you, marry me. Or just come for dinner.

optionen.text: Guts the tuna himself, with Petru watching.

zeile.text: Good. Not good. But good.

optionen.text: Hands the knife to Lola.
Offers Petru money.

zeile.text: Money is for tourists.

events.lage: Since Holm left, Chiara acts as if she runs the place. She tosses you the keys to the tender. You're to reverse it into the garage, in front of the crew and without help. She folds her arms and waits.

zeilen.text: Holm made me do this on my first day. Now it's your turn. Back her in, no help, everybody watching.
You've got this! Probably! I'll hold the line. Mostly.

optionen.text: Takes the keys and reverses the tender in, calm and slow.

zeile.text: Hm. Not bad. Holm would have said that too. Then she'd have found a scratch anyway.

optionen.text: Asks Lea to guide him in.

zeile.text: Asking for help in front of the crew. Holm would have liked that, and so do I.

optionen.text: Throws the keys back: “Show me, Chiara.”

events.lage: Holm stands on the bridge with two mugs and hands you one. For a long time she says nothing. She looks out at the water. Her hand rests on her stomach, as if it hurts.

zeilen.text: Thirty years at sea. You learn to hear a boat. This one sounds tired.
You're good with people, Frankfurt. Be careful. Being liked is not the same as being followed.

optionen.text: “What would you do differently?”
Drinks the coffee in silence.
“You don't look well, Captain.”

zeile.text: Mind your boat, not my stomach. …Takk.

events.lage: Rosi turned off the hot water to save power. Siri was in the shower at the time. The scream echoes through the whole yacht.

zeilen.text: Hot water costs power and power is life, but cold water builds character. You're welcome.
ROSI! I had conditioner in! I have conditioner in my soul now!

optionen.text: Hot water on for five minutes.
“Rosi's right, Siri. Cold water it is.”
Brings Siri a towel and tea.

events.lage: For the first time, Chiara takes a break. She dives off the stern in a white swimsuit. When she climbs back up, half the crew is staring. She only notices one of them.

zeilen.text: What? Officers are allowed to swim. Stop staring, all of you. Not you. You can stare.
Chiara has legs. Who knew. Somebody write this down.

optionen.text: Dives in after her.

zeile.text: Race you to the buoy, and the loser gets dunked. I don't lose.

optionen.text: Holds her towel and looks her in the eye.
Tells the crew to get back to work.

events.nachklang_text: Water on her skin, her laugh at the buoy. At breakfast Chiara asks, far too matter-of-factly, whether you slept well.

events.lage: Siri comes to breakfast in a grey jumper that's far too big for her. It's your jumper. She took it off the chair last night and acts as if that were normal.

zeilen.text: It was cold and it was on the chair, and it smells like the sea and coffee. So I'm keeping it.
Interesting choice of knitwear, darling. Very… officer-adjacent.

optionen.text: “It looks better on you than on me.”
Acts as if nothing's up.
“I want that back. In person.”

zeile.text: Come and get it, then. Tonight. If you dare.

events.nachklang_text: Your jumper on her. All day you keep finding grey wool fluff on your sleeve, and you smile about it.

events.lage: Lola has found a loose page from Sophia's notebook and is reading it out to the crew in her most dramatic voice. A love scene. A strict officer and a first officer on a stranded yacht. It gets very hot, very fast. Halfway through, Sophia walks in.

zeilen.text: “She pushed him against the chart table. The charts slid to the floor. Nobody cared.” Oh my god. Who wrote this?
Stop reading, stop reading right now. Why does the officer have my haircut?

optionen.text: “Keep reading.”
Takes the page from Lola and gives it back to Sophia.
Later, alone with Sophia: “How does it end?”

zeile.text: Badly for the charts, and very well for everyone else. …It's nothing, darling, just ideas. Come by later, and I'll read you the ending.

events.lage: The Eden Group helicopter lands on the sun deck. The downdraught rips the towel off Lola, the hairdo off Chiara and very nearly the shorts off Totò. Megan steps out. Not one hair moves.

zeilen.text: Good afternoon. I see the welcome committee is wearing less than expected. Charming.
My towel! My towel's in Sardinia now! Hi, I'm Lola, I'm the cook, I'm naked.

optionen.text: Greets Megan formally.
Gives Lola his jacket.

zeile.text: A gentleman. How rare. I'll write it in my diary— no, I won't. Ahaha.

optionen.text: “Welcome to the most beautiful dead yacht in the fleet.”

events.lage: Megan sets up a glass chessboard in the salon and challenges you. The crew gathers. Megan has never lost. She says so three times.

zeilen.text: Chess. You and me. If you win, I owe you a favour. If I win, you owe me one. I always win.
Check. No, wait. Not check. You're cleverer than you look. I hate that. I love that.

optionen.text: Plays Megan and tries to win.
Plays Megan and loses on purpose.

zeile.text: You let me win. Never do that again, I want to beat you properly.

optionen.text: Offers his seat to Sophia.

events.lage: Totò's cousin comes alongside at night in a rubber dinghy with no lights and starts unloading crates. On the shore something flashes: Elsa's binoculars.

zeilen.text: Gennaro, piano, piano! Quiet! The whole bay can hear you. And put the goat down, it's not part of the delivery!
Is this smuggling? Is this real smuggling? Can I carry something?

optionen.text: Stows the crates below deck, fast.
Sends the cousin away.
Flashes a torch back at Elsa.

zeile.text: Why are you signalling the police? Are you flirting with the police? Comandante!

events.lage: Lola is cooking breakfast in sunglasses. Indoors. She's moving very slowly and speaking very quietly. The omelette is oversalted. Very.

zeilen.text: Shhh. Everything is loud, the eggs are loud, your face is loud. I love you all. Quietly.
This omelette has more salt than the Mediterranean.

optionen.text: Gives Lola water and quiet, and cooks breakfast himself.
Bravely eats the omelette.

zeile.text: You ate it, you're a hero. I'll name a sauce after you.

optionen.text: “If you party, you still cook.”

betroffen.was: wants to weld something right now

events.lage: Day eight. For a week Rosi has welded, sanded and sworn behind a tarpaulin. This morning the tarpaulin is gone. The workshop door stands open, the benches are clean, and on the door there's a strip of red tape with crooked letters on it: “Open. Mostly.” She holds out a key to you and acts as if it were nothing.

zeilen.text: It works again, Officer. Every bench, every light, every drawer. The fire took the old one, so I built a better one. Don't touch the drawers.
I only stored a few boxes in there, Comandante. Temporarily. For years. They're out now. Mostly.
And those strange chips you brought back from the harbour, give them here. …See that? There's a transmitter in every one. Somebody wanted to steer those animals from very far away.
Not any more. I've cut the transmitters out, so now they only listen to you, and you can pull them out whenever you like. That part matters to me.
One more thing. I rebuilt one of the collar senders. It doesn't give orders any more, it eavesdrops. It's in your jacket now, so out there you'll know who's waiting before they know you're coming.
Bring me your jacket, your weapons and the chips, one piece a night, and I'll text you when it's done. And if you want to say thank you, say it fast. I hate it.

optionen.text: Takes the key and thanks her, fast.

zeile.text: Good, fast is good. Now go away, I have a bench to christen.

optionen.text: Leaves the key with her: “You rebuilt it. It's yours.”

zeile.text: …Idiot. Thank you. Now bring me something to fix, I'm already bored.

optionen.text: Helps Totò carry his crates out.

zeile.text: Comandante, careful, that one is fragile. And that one. They are all fragile. Don't ask.

events.lage: Chiara has labelled everything in the galley. Overnight, Lola relabelled every single jar. The salt is now called “ocean glitter”, the flour “cloud dust”.

zeilen.text: Where is the salt, Lola. Where. Is. The. Salt.
It's ocean glitter, Chi, second shelf. It's all about energy.

optionen.text: Sides with Chiara. “Salt is called salt. Change them back.”
Sides with Lola. “Ocean glitter stays. I like it.”
“You two are cooking together today.”
Sits down with popcorn and watches them argue.

events.lage: Alva has one canister of diesel left, and she'll only part with it if someone beats her at poker. They're playing for clothes. Three rounds in, Alva has lost her scarf and Sophia her blouse. Sophia hasn't blinked once all night. Both of them look at you.

zeilen.text: O figliolu, your concierge cheats like a Corsican. I like her. I still win.
I never cheat, darling. Two years in the wings of a West End theatre teaches you to watch faces. Duc, tell her which card she's hiding under her garter.
This is the best night of my LIFE.

optionen.text: Helps Sophia: gives away Alva's card.
Warns Alva. “She's reading your face.”

zeile.text: Alva remembers who helps her, o figliolu. Here. A rose, and the canister stays mine.

optionen.text: Sits down and joins the game.

klatsch.was: Duc lost his shirt at poker in Alva's bar

optionen.text: Leaves the table.

zeile.text: Boooo.

events.lage: Kevin the seagull is sitting on the railing between Lea and Totò, calmly eating a croissant. Lea wants to save him. Totò wants to catch him and auction him off to tourists.

zeilen.text: He's family now! You can't sell family! Kevin, come to mummy!
A seagull that steals butter? On Instagram that's money. I catch, we auction, everybody eats.

optionen.text: Sides with Lea. “Nobody sells Kevin.”
Helps Totò catch Kevin for the auction.
Dives for Kevin himself.

zeile.text: He's in the water. Kevin is dry. Kevin won.

optionen.text: Sits down with popcorn and watches the chase.

events.lage: Chiara assigned Rosi's people to interior duty. Rosi took them back without asking. Now the two of them are standing in the corridor, and neither will step aside.

zeilen.text: The interior crew is mine and I assign it. You don't just take my people because you need hands.
Without my hands there is no interior. There's a dark, warm box that smells of fish. Your choice.

optionen.text: “Chiara's right, Rosi. The interior crew is hers to assign.”
“Rosi needs those hands more, Chiara. The repairs come first.”
“You two make a plan together, right here, right now.”

events.lage: At dinner Yasin filmed Siri without asking, with her mouth full. Siri stands up. For the first time, she says no out loud in front of everyone.

zeilen.text: Delete it. Now. I'm not your content when I'm eating. I'm not your content when I'm crying. I'm a person.
Babe, relax, it's cute. People love real moments. You love real moments.

optionen.text: Stands next to Siri and says nothing.

zeile.text: Thank you. I needed someone to just stand there, that's all.

optionen.text: Mediates: “Not at dinner.”
Stays quiet and lets Siri decide.

events.lage: Lola claims her arancini are the best in the Mediterranean. Alva has opinions about that. The whole village is watching. You're the jury.

zeilen.text: Mine have a secret ingredient, and it's love and three kinds of cheese. Mostly the cheese.
Mine have my grandmother's recipe. My grandmother would spit on your love.

optionen.text: Raises Lola's hand. “Lola's arancini win.”
“Alva wins. You can taste forty years of this bar.”
“A draw. I need more samples.”

zeile.text: A draw! A diplomatic triumph! I declare a festival!

events.lage: Sophia wants an afternoon off for the crew. Megan wants results. They sit across the table from each other, smiling as if each were about to poison the other.

zeilen.text: One afternoon off, because the crew works better rested. It's in all the studies. I'll send you the studies.
Darling, I invented the studies. They get half a day, and they wear Eden caps while they relax.

optionen.text: Sides with Sophia. “They get the afternoon off.”
Sides with Megan. “No afternoon off. We need results.”
“A whole day, and I'll wear the cap.”

events.lage: Elsa wants to look inside Totò's locker. Totò stands in front of it with his arms spread wide, like a goalkeeper facing a penalty.

zeilen.text: Lieutenant, this locker is my bedroom. My church. My grandmother is in there. Spiritually.
Then your grandmother won't mind if I say hello. Step aside, Mister Esposito.

optionen.text: Stands beside Totò. “That locker is private, Lieutenant.”
Steps aside. “Go ahead, Lieutenant, open it.”
Waves Lola over to distract Elsa with cake.

zeile.text: Lieutenant! Cake! It's a normal cake! Please eat it before I explain it.

events.lage: Siri wants to lend Chiara a dress for the festa. Silver, backless, very expensive. Chiara wants to go in uniform. Siri holds up the dress and won't let it go.

zeilen.text: You have the shoulders for this. I've wanted to say that for days. Try it on. Five minutes.
I'm an officer. Officers don't wear silver. Officers wear navy and responsibility.

optionen.text: Sides with Siri. “Try it on, Chiara.”

zeile.text: Fine. Five minutes. Nobody look. Okay, you can look. Is it too much? It's too much.

optionen.text: Sides with Chiara. “The uniform is fine.”
“You look good in anything, but this…”

events.titel: The Mayor Wants to Come Aboard
events.lage: Madame Casanova wants to board the yacht ceremonially, with a sash and a photographer. Chiara is standing at the gangway and isn't letting anyone past. The mayor already has one foot on the ladder.

zeilen.text: Mademoiselle! The village welcomes you! With speeches! Three speeches! May I come aboard?
No. Our captain is in hospital and this boat is not a stage. Come back when we're not sinking quite so politely.

optionen.text: Holds the ladder for Madame Casanova.
Stands with Chiara. “Not today, Madame.”
Lets the mayor give one short speech on the jetty.

events.lage: Totò claimed that women can't arm-wrestle. Rosi has rolled up her sleeves. The crew is drumming on the table.

zeilen.text: Say it again, Totò. Say it again while I break your wrist.
Rosi, cara, it was a joke, a Neapolitan joke. We say it to everyone, even to men.

optionen.text: Bets on Rosi.
Bets on Totò.
Takes on the winner.

zeile.text: Don't you dare let me win. I'll know.

events.lage: The tender's outboard is sputtering. Petru wants to fix it with a hammer and a feel for it. Rosi wants a multimeter and a laptop. Each thinks the other one's method is superstition.

zeilen.text: Listen. The engine talks. The hammer answers.
The engine does not talk, Petru. The engine has a fault code. I'm reading it. Please put the hammer down.

optionen.text: Nods at the hammer. “Go on, Petru. Let's hear what the engine says.”
“Put the hammer down, Petru. Rosi reads the fault code.”
Rosi measures first, then Petru's hammer.

zeile.text: Good. Science first, then the hammer. Like my father did.

events.lage: While snorkelling, Lea found a small octopus and brought it back. Siri wants to return it to the sea at once. She knows a surprising amount about octopuses.

zeilen.text: Look at him! He held my finger! Can we keep him? Just for today? In the ice bucket?
He's scared, Lea. They're smarter than half of Instagram. He needs a dark rock, not an ice bucket.

optionen.text: Sides with Lea. “He can stay in the ice bucket, just for today.”
Sides with Siri. “He goes back in the sea, Lea.”
Takes him back together, with Siri explaining.

zeile.text: Three hearts and blue blood. He'll remember you, Lea, because they remember faces.

events.lage: Madame Casanova wants to turn Alva's bar into a VIP lounge for the festa, with a velvet rope. Alva wants her bar to stay the way it is: loud, full, and for everyone. Behind them Pascal walks along the wall with a tape measure, his hat pushed back.

zeilen.text: A velvet rope! Gold chairs! A VIP list! With the yacht crew as the main VIPs!
My bar has had one rule for forty years: everybody drinks, fishermen, mayors and dogs. No rope.
Four metres eighty, Madame. It's for the rope, Alva, only the rope. Don't look at me like that, I just hold the tape.

optionen.text: Sides with Casanova. “One velvet rope, just for the festa.”
Sides with Alva. “Her bar stays as it is.”
“Fine, a VIP lounge. All the fishermen are VIPs.”

zeile.text: A VIP list where everyone is a VIP. Very Corsican. I approve.

events.lage: Megan runs a white glove along the bar in the salon and holds her finger up to Chiara. A tiny grey smudge. Chiara goes red, then white.

zeilen.text: Dust, on my bar, on my boat. Explain it to me as if I were an investor.
We have no power, no water and no sleep. We have dust. I accept the dust. I will not apologise for it.

optionen.text: Nods at Megan. “Not good enough, Chiara.”
Stands next to Chiara. “This ship is clean, Megan.”
Takes the glove and wipes the smudge off himself.

zeile.text: The First Officer cleans. Interesting. Ahaha— don't look at me.

events.lage: Lola holds out a cookie to Megan. Megan doesn't eat cookies. Megan hasn't eaten sugar since 2019. Lola just keeps holding out the cookie and smiling.

zeilen.text: It's a normal cookie, ninety percent normal. Just one, love, you look like you need a hug in food form.
I don't eat cookies. I don't eat joy. I eat results. …Is that chocolate?

optionen.text: Smiles at Megan. “Just one bite. It won't kill you.”

zeile.text: Oh no. That's good. That's very good. Why is the room warm. Why am I happy.

optionen.text: Gently lowers Lola's hand. “She said no, Lola.”
Takes a cookie himself, so Lola isn't left standing there.

events.lage: Lea and Rosi had a fight. Now both of them are baking a peace cake to apologise, at the same time, in the same galley. It escalates.

zeilen.text: Mine has strawberries. Because I'm sorry. And because strawberries are sorry too.
Mine has Sicilian almonds in it, which means I'm more sorry. Scientifically.

optionen.text: Tries Lea's cake first.
Tries Rosi's cake first.
Puts both cakes on one plate and eats them together.

zeile.text: Strawberry almond! You two just invented a cake, and I'm crying.

events.lage: Elsa is sitting at Alva's bar, drinking an espresso. Under the counter stand four diesel canisters. Everyone knows. Elsa looks at Alva for a long time.

zeilen.text: Alva. That smell. Is it diesel, or is it your perfume?
It's my perfume, Lieutenant. It's called Fisherman's Dream. Very exclusive. Another espresso?

optionen.text: Sniffs the air. “That's diesel, Alva.”
Leans on the bar. “Nice perfume, Alva. Very exclusive.”
Buys a canister from Alva, with a receipt.

zeile.text: An official purchase with a receipt, in this village. I might frame it.

events.lage: The crew needs outfits for the festa. Chiara wants matching white shirts. Sophia wants everyone to wear what she finds beautiful. The pile of clothes in the corridor keeps growing.

zeilen.text: White shirts and navy trousers, because we represent the yacht. We look like a crew, not a festival.
It IS a festival, darling, so let them shine. Rosi has a dress she's never worn. Let her wear it.

optionen.text: “Chiara's right. White shirts and navy trousers for everyone.”
Sides with Sophia. “Let them shine. Everyone wears what they like.”
“One matching detail, and the rest is up to you.”

zeile.text: A red flower for everyone! I'll nick them from the mayor.

events.lage: Chiara has pinned a new rota to the mess door. Double shifts for everyone until Megan's inspection. Sophia has crossed out tomorrow afternoon in red and written FREE across it.

zeilen.text: Megan does not care that we're tired. Megan cares that the brass shines. Two shifts. Everyone.
Darling, they've polished brass for a week. One afternoon in the sea, or I start hearing mutiny in the walls.

optionen.text: Takes Chiara's side. “The rota stays.”
Takes Sophia's side. “Tomorrow afternoon is free.”
“Mornings Chiara's way, afternoons free.”

zeile.text: Free afternoon! I'm getting my fins before anybody changes their mind.

events.lage: The village left tips after Lola's dinner on the quay. Three hundred euros in a jam jar. Lola wants to split it. Rosi wants a new fuel pump.

zeilen.text: Split it six ways, Boss, and everyone buys something stupid. That's the whole point of tips.
Something stupid like a fuel pump? The old one is held together with prayers and my hairband.

optionen.text: “The money goes to Rosi's fuel pump.”
“Lola's right. Split it six ways.”
“It goes in the ship's account, for emergencies.”

events.lage: Lea has put a speaker on the foredeck, and three people are dancing around it. It's half past one. Chiara is standing in the hatch in her dressing gown. She has the early watch.

zeilen.text: Some of us are on the bridge at five, so turn it off, Lea. Now, please.
It's one song! Okay, it was four songs. But this one's really good, Chiara, listen-

optionen.text: “Lights out. Chiara's right.”
“Let them dance, Chiara. One more song.”
Buys everyone headphones in the village tomorrow.

events.lage: There's a spare crew cabin by the laundry. It has a real porthole and a door that locks. Sophia has put her books on the bunk. Lola has put her pillow on top of the books.

zeilen.text: I need quiet to write, darling. Lola needs quiet like a fish needs a bicycle.
I snore, Boss, everyone knows I snore, so a door that shuts is basically charity.

optionen.text: Gives the cabin to Sophia. “You need the quiet to write.”
“The cabin is Lola's. We all need a door between us and that snoring.”
Yasin wants it for his camera gear. He pays.
Holds out his hat. “You two draw lots.”

zeile.text: Lola wins! Lola always wins. Sophia, you can visit, but bring biscuits.

events.lage: It's Sunday, if anyone is counting. Lea has packed towels and a cool box for the cove. Rosi has packed a toolbox. Both bags are on the mess table, waiting.

zeilen.text: One day, Officer. One beach, one swim. Then we fix the whole world on Monday, promise.
The batteries don't know it's Sunday. If we stop now, she cools down and we start from zero.

optionen.text: “Everyone works. Rosi's right.”
“Beach day. Everyone.”
“Work till noon, then the cove.”

zeile.text: Fine, noon. But if the cove has a generator, I'm fixing it.

events.lage: Lola has written a shopping list for the village. It's two pages long and has saffron on it. Chiara has written a shorter one. It says: tins.

zeilen.text: You can't feed a crew on tins, Chi, that's how mutinies start. I read about it.
We have a budget, Lola, and the budget does not include saffron. The budget barely includes us.

optionen.text: Takes Chiara's list. “Tins. We stay on budget.”
Takes Lola's two pages. “Buy all of it, saffron too.”
Goes fishing with Petru instead.

zeile.text: Look at that, fresh fish and no saffron needed! Boss, you're a genius. A smelly genius.

events.lage: Just after midnight there's a knock. Lola is standing in the doorway, barefoot, in a T-shirt far too big for her, her eyes glassy and happy. She smells of the sea and sweet smoke. She leans against the door frame and grins.

zeilen.text: Hiii. I was smoking on the stern and the stars told me to come here. The stars are very bossy tonight.
Can I come in? I'm not that high, I'm medium high. High enough to say I've wanted you since the galley.
You can say no, Boss, and I'll just go back and tell the stars they were wrong. They'll get over it.

optionen.text: Lets her in.

szene_intim.hinweis: Lola is high, giggly and very forward, and she leads. Playful, dirty, warm; she checks in with a laugh and means it.

zeile.text: Oh, thank god. Lie down and let me show you what the stars had in mind.

optionen.text: Lets her in, but talks first.

zeile.text: Talking first? You're so sweet it hurts. Okay, talk to me, then maybe kiss me, then maybe more.

optionen.text: “Not tonight, Lola. Come back when you're clear-headed.”

zeile.text: Respect. Annoying, but respect. I'll come back sober and twice as dangerous.

events.nachklang_text: Smoke, salt, Lola's laugh in the dark. At breakfast you're the only one who gets a heart-shaped pancake.

events.lage: A message from Lola: a photo of her bare back in the moonlight, and underneath, a single word: “Again?” She lets you choose the place. The night is long, she writes.

zeilen.text: Again? You choose where. I'll be there before you've finished reading this. I'm fast when I want something.
No pressure, Boss. If you're tired, send me a heart and I'll dream about you instead. Loudly.

optionen.text: Chooses a place to meet.

szene_intim.hinweis: Lola chose this, again. Familiar now, bolder, laughing, filthy and tender.

zeile.text: On my way, so leave the light off. I know the way by heart now.

optionen.text: Sends a heart.

zeile.text: Dreaming about you, out loud. Sorry, Rosi.

events.lage: The last fishermen have gone. Alva turns the sign to “Chiuso” and locks the door. She goes into the back room and comes back in something black with ruffles that hardly covers anything. There's a rose in her curls.

zeilen.text: For forty years this bar has been open to everybody. Tonight it's open to one man. Sit, o figliolu.
My grandmother danced flamenco in Seville. I only learned the parts that end on a table.
You can walk out, you know. The door is right there. But you won't.

optionen.text: Stays with her.

szene_intim.hinweis: Alva is in charge in her own bar: slow, teasing, experienced, very sure of what she wants; she dances first.

zeile.text: Good. Now watch. Don't touch. Not yet. I'll tell you when.

optionen.text: Dances with her, very slowly.

zeile.text: You dance like a sailor. Hold me closer. There. Now you dance like a man who stays.

optionen.text: “Not tonight, Alva.”

zeile.text: Then I'll leave the dress on the chair. It's patient. I'm not.

events.nachklang_text: Black ruffles on a bar stool, a rose on the floor. You can still smell her as you row back to the boat in the morning.

events.lage: Alva calls. She's wearing something black with white polka dots and swinging a small key on a red cord in front of the camera. The key to her back room.

zeilen.text: I had a key made for the back room, for you. Nobody else has one, not even my accountant.
Tonight or whenever you want, and wherever you want. I'll bring the fan. You know what the fan is for.

optionen.text: Chooses a place to meet.

szene_intim.hinweis: Alva again, playful and possessive, a little jealous, very skilled.

zeile.text: Perfect. Don't eat. I'll feed you after.

optionen.text: “Tomorrow. I promise.”

events.lage: Lola has heard that you can cook. Now she's standing in front of the stove with her arms folded. Two burners, one hour, the crew as the jury. Lola already has a spoon in her hand and is pointing it at you.

zeilen.text: Right. My galley, my rules. One hour, one plate each, the crew votes. Loser does the dishes for a week.
I put twenty euros on the Comandante. Don't look at me like that, Lola, it's business.
Boss, I once made a whole dinner party out of a tin of beans and a lime. Bring it.

optionen.text: Cooks his best dish, and cooks to win.

klatsch.was: Duc beat Lola in her own galley

zeile.text: Okay. OKAY. That's annoyingly good, so rematch tomorrow, and you're still doing the dishes.

optionen.text: “Let's cook one dish together.”

zeile.text: Together? That's not a showdown, that's a date with knives. I love it.

optionen.text: Lets her win.

zeile.text: You let me win, I saw that. I'm keeping the trophy anyway.

events.lage: Alva has pushed the tables together. On one side stand her fiadone and her wild boar pâté, on the other your street kitchen of two camping stoves. Half the village is here. Madame Casanova has brought a microphone.

zeilen.text: Mesdames et messieurs! Corsica against Saigon! Forty years of tradition against one handsome sailor!
In this bar, o figliolu, the food is older than your country's flag. Cook. Impress me.
Hm.

optionen.text: Puts his thịt kho up against her pâté.

klatsch.was: The First Officer beat Alva at cooking

zeile.text: Sweet pork and eggs, like a grandmother made it. Which grandmother, eh? You'll tell me one day.

optionen.text: Puts both dishes on one plate, half Corsican and half Vietnamese.

klatsch.was: Duc's fusion cooking confused the village

zeile.text: Brocciu with fish sauce. I hate that I like it. Don't tell my grandmother. She's in Seville and she'd still find out.

optionen.text: Lets the village decide who wins.

zeile.text: Democracy! The village votes for everyone! Nobody loses, everybody eats, and I give a speech!

events.lage: Totò has a pot of ragù on that has been simmering for six hours. He claims the recipe is older than Naples itself. You have a clay pot of caramelised pork belly. Rosi is handing out forks like weapons.

zeilen.text: Comandante, this is my nonna's ragù, six hours on the fire. If you lose, you say on camera that Napoli is the centre of the world.
And if the Officer wins, you say Sicily is better than Napoli, on camera. Yasin, film it.
Already rolling. This is going to do numbers.

optionen.text: Sets his thịt kho down next to Totò's ragù. “Forks ready, Rosi.”

zeile.text: Caramel and pork and egg. Madonna. My nonna would have married you. Don't tell Rosi I said Sicily.

optionen.text: “Let's swap recipes.”

zeile.text: A recipe swap? You know what that's worth in Naples? Everything. Here's my cousin's fish, fresh. Don't ask.

optionen.text: Gives him the win and praises Naples.

zeile.text: Traitor. You'll sleep in the engine room with Unit-01.

events.titel: Lola's Down: You Cook for Thirteen
events.lage: Lola ate a bad mussel and is lying green in her bunk. Tomorrow thirteen people need feeding. Chiara is staring at the empty meal plan. Rosi wants tins and to save power. Sophia wants it to look like a yacht anyway.

zeilen.text: Lola is out. Thirteen people, one galley, zero cooks. Somebody has to stand at that stove tomorrow.
Cold tins, and that's all. No oven and no hotplate marathon, because every kilowatt goes to the batteries and not to a soufflé.
If the guests eat beans out of a tin, they'll talk about it for a year. One proper meal, darling. That's all I ask.

optionen.text: “Rosi's right. Cold tins tomorrow, and we save the power.”
Sides with Sophia. “One proper meal. I'll cook it.”
A third way: bún riêu in one big pot. One course, little power.

zeile.text: One pot for thirteen. If that works, I'll write it on the whiteboard in gold.

optionen.text: Promise: tomorrow Lola gets the first bowl of soup, in bed.

versprechen.text: Duc bringt Lola Suppe ans Bett

events.lage: Lola's blender is dead. Rosi has cleared two workbenches and set up a stopwatch. Whoever gets it running first gets the first glass of Lola's mango smoothie. Lola is standing by with a glass as if it were a trophy.

zeilen.text: One blender, two engineers, one stopwatch. If you beat me in my own workshop, I'll call you Maestro for a day.
Whoever wins gets the first smoothie. The loser gets the one with the bits.
I'm timing! Ready, steady, wait, which button is start, okay, GO!

optionen.text: Races Rosi against the stopwatch to fix the blender.

zeile.text: Maestro. Ugh. For one day only, so don't get used to it. Okay, maybe a little.

optionen.text: Fixes the blender with Rosi, her right hand and his left.

zeile.text: Your left hand, my right hand. It works. It shouldn't work. Don't look at me like that.

optionen.text: Lets Rosi win and hands her the smoothie.

zeile.text: You let me win. That's stupid, but it's sweet. Drink half.

events.lage: Two dismantled spearguns are lying on towels. Chiara has started a bet. Whoever assembles theirs faster and hits the buoy decides who does the washing-up tonight. She ties her hair up and smiles at you.

zeilen.text: Eight parts, one buoy, thirty metres. I've done this blindfolded on a charter in Phuket. You're going down, First Officer.
Can you two do this in slow motion? For the algorithm. Chiara, hair flip, please.
Yasin, one more word and the buoy is you.

optionen.text: Builds his speargun as fast as he can and shoots at the buoy.

klatsch.was: Duc beat Chiara in the speargun race

zeile.text: Okay, that was fast. That was annoyingly hot and fast. The dishes are mine, so don't gloat.

optionen.text: Helps Chiara with the last part so they finish together.

zeile.text: A tie. You planned that, and nobody plans a tie. Who are you?

optionen.text: Nudges Yasin's camera into the water, discreetly.

zeile.text: My GoPro! That's a business expense! Siri, stop laughing!
