events.lage: Lea has brought her field guide up on deck. The game: she describes a sea creature, you have to guess it. Then the other way round. Siri keeps score. Petru sits on the railing mending a net and pretends not to listen.

zeilen.text: Okay! It's got eight arms, three hearts, blue blood, and it can taste with its skin. Go!
I'm keeping score. Lea's winning, but only because she reads under the blanket at night.
Too easy.

optionen.text: Guesses cleverly, then sets her a hard one.

zeile.text: A sea pig? That's a real thing? You're making that up. Petru, is he making that up?

optionen.text: Guesses as badly as he can, on purpose. “A seagull?”

zeile.text: A seagull is NOT a fish, Duc. Kevin would be so offended.

optionen.text: Turns to the railing. “Petru, you know this sea. Your turn.”

zeile.text: A big grouper under the harbour wall, fifty years old. I call him Napoleon.

events.lage: You've set up a quiz night. Two teams, a bell from the galley, you as the host. After three rounds it's a draw. Totò is suspiciously often right, and there's a search engine glowing on his phone.

zeilen.text: The capital of Mongolia? Ulaanbaatar, obviously. I know these things. I am a cultured man.
Duc. Darling. His phone is under the table and it's glowing. I'm not saying anything. I'm just noticing.
CHEATER! Ring the bell! Ring the cheating bell!

optionen.text: Rings the bell. “Phone under the table, Totò. You're disqualified.”

zeile.text: Disqualified? In Naples this is called research!

optionen.text: Gives Totò a penalty round: a question about his nonna.

zeile.text: My nonna's birthday? The fourth of March. You see? Some things I don't need a phone for.

optionen.text: “Bonus question, and only the host knows the answer.”

klatsch.was: The quizmaster didn't know the answer to his own question

zeile.text: A question only the host can answer. That's clever, and I'm keeping that one.

events.lage: Sophia has called a poetry slam. Lola drew the topic out of a hat: her fridge. Sophia went first, four verses, and Chiara cried laughing. Now it's your turn. Sophia looks at you over her glass.

zeilen.text: O fridge, cold keeper of Lola's sins, you hum all night like a lover who knows too much. Your turn, Duc.
That's my fridge she's talking about! It's a good fridge, it's emotionally available!
Make me feel something for an appliance, darling. I dare you.

optionen.text: Stands up and reads a cheeky, warm poem about the fridge.

zeile.text: That last line. You didn't write that about a fridge. Did you.

optionen.text: Reads a poem about the fridge that only Sophia will understand.

zeile.text: Everyone else heard a fridge. I heard something else. Walk me to my cabin later. Just walk.

optionen.text: Speaks as the fridge, in the fridge's own voice.

zeile.text: He did the VOICE. He did the fridge's VOICE, I'm going to cry.

events.nachklang_text: Sophia copied your poem onto a napkin. In the morning the napkin is folded in your jacket pocket.

events.lage: Alva found a nineties karaoke machine in her cellar. The microphone crackles, the lyrics scroll across an old tube TV. Half the crew is here. Madame Casanova has already signed up for three songs. Then Alva calls your name.

zeilen.text: Next on stage, the First Officer! He sings, or he buys a round for the whole bar. Those are the rules. I just made them up.
A duet! He must sing a duet! I volunteer! I have already volunteered!
Pick someone who can't sing, it's more fun. Pick Chiara.

optionen.text: Holds out the second microphone and picks a partner.

zeile.text: A duet, good. Everyone in Corsica falls in love during a duet. It's the law.

optionen.text: Takes the microphone alone and gives it everything.

klatsch.was: Duc sang at Alva's. Loudly. Very loudly.

zeile.text: Comandante! Like Pavarotti, if Pavarotti had been hit by a boat! Bravo!

optionen.text: Gives Madame Casanova her duet.

zeile.text: Mon capitaine! Hold my hand for the high note! There is no high note! I'll make one!

events.lage: It's warm, and there's just enough power for a single string of fairy lights. You've fetched the old guitar from the salon. At first only Lea is sitting there, then Rosi and Lola come with blankets. Siri stops at the top of the stairs, and then comes closer after all.

zeilen.text: Play something everyone knows! Or something nobody knows! Either! Both!
Can you play something quiet? Something that isn't for a camera.
I brought Tim Tams for the vibes. Don't ask where I hid them.

optionen.text: Plays something everyone can sing along to.

zeile.text: Okay, I'm singing, but nobody films this, and I mean it. Yasin, I mean you, wherever you are.

optionen.text: Plays something quiet, just for Siri.

zeile.text: My dad used to play like that. Badly, and with his whole heart. Don't stop.

optionen.text: Passes the guitar on.

zeile.text: Rosi can play? Rosi can PLAY? Why does nobody on this boat tell me anything?

events.nachklang_text: The fairy lights flicker, the guitar leans against the railing. For a while Siri rested her head on your shoulder.

events.lage: No power for music, just candles on the aft deck. Someone asked where you actually come from. It goes quiet. Everyone waits. Nobody pushes. Lola holds out a mug of tea to you.

zeilen.text: You don't have to, Boss. But if you want to, we're all here and nobody's going anywhere. Literally, we're stranded.
You always ask about us, but you never talk about you. Where does the First Officer come from?

optionen.text: Tells his story: family, flight, the long way up.

szene_gespraech.hinweis: Duc tells the crew where he comes from, in his own words: his parents fled Vietnam after the war and built a new life in Germany; he grew up in a migrant working-class family and worked his way up. Do not invent details he has not said. The women listen and react in character, each in her own way: questions, silence, a hand on his arm. No one turns it into pity.

zeile.text: Take your time. We've got all night and nowhere to be.

optionen.text: Tells only one person, later, in private.

szene_gespraech.hinweis: Later, alone with one person of Duc's choice, he tells her where he comes from, in his own words. Do not invent details. She listens, asks honest questions, and keeps it between them.

zeile.text: Okay. Whoever he picks, the rest of us are going to bed and absolutely not listening at the door.

optionen.text: Waves it off: “Another time.”

zeile.text: Okay, the offer stays open. That's how it works on a boat.

betroffen.was: her boat is lost in the fog

events.lage: Madame Casanova is rehearsing her festa entrance. In a flamenco dress, on a fishing boat, with a hired fog machine. The fog is thicker than planned. The whole harbour has gone white. Somewhere in it, Elsa's patrol boat is sounding its horn.

zeilen.text: Behold! The mayor rises from the mists of Corsica! …Is it working? I can't see anything. Perfect.
Madame. I can't see my own bow. Turn. It. Off.
Front row in the fog, ten euros! Second row, five! You see nothing, but you see nothing first!
Lieutenant, this is my fault, please write it down. I ordered the small machine. This is the small machine.
Then I'll need a form, Monsieur Leca. The same kind as the one for my antenna, I suppose. It's been eleven months.
Almost through, Elsa. I promise you, almost.

optionen.text: Fixes the fog machine so it doses properly.

zeile.text: A gentle mist! A mysterious mist! You have given me the gift of drama, Monsieur!

optionen.text: Applauds loudly until she bows.

zeile.text: The people love me! Even the ones I cannot see!

optionen.text: Guides Elsa back to her boat.

zeile.text: …Thank you. Tell her the fog machine is now evidence.

events.lage: Petru left a bucket on board when he made his delivery. In the bucket was an octopus he's been feeding for weeks and calls Bastianu. Now the bucket is empty. Lola is standing in the galley with a wooden spoon, swearing she only had a look. An arm waves from the sink.

zeilen.text: Okay, so, in my defence, he looked hungry. And then he looked at the garlic. And then he was GONE.
Bastianu. Come here.
Comandante, think about it. The garlic is already here. Destiny is calling.

optionen.text: Gently coaxes Bastianu back into the bucket.

zeile.text: …Grazie. He likes you. He never likes anybody.

optionen.text: Makes it clear to Totò: you don't eat friends.

zeile.text: Fine! Fine. I will eat my feelings. Also not octopus.

optionen.text: Lets Lola draw the octopus until Petru collects him.

zeile.text: Look, I gave him eyebrows. He's thrilled. He's not thrilled. He's an octopus.

events.lage: Elsa has stopped one of Totò's crates on the quay. The crate says “Potatoes”. The crate meows. Totò claims they're very young potatoes. Elsa has already pulled out her notebook.

zeilen.text: Monsieur Esposito. Potatoes do not purr.
Corsican potatoes, Lieutenant. Very emotional. It's the soil.
Open it. If it's a cat, I'm keeping it. If it's potatoes, I'm keeping those too.

optionen.text: Backs Elsa: open it.

zeile.text: A kitten. Three kittens. Esposito, you are smuggling kittens.

optionen.text: Covers for Totò: “Those are my potatoes.”

zeile.text: Comandante! A man of honour! …They are kittens, by the way. For my nonna.

optionen.text: Suggests giving the kittens to the village.

zeile.text: The official cats of the festa! I declare it! Somebody write it down!

events.lage: Megan calls during the crew dinner and demands to be put on a chair. “Team building.” Lola puts a napkin in front of the laptop and serves Megan a plate of pasta that nobody will eat.

zeilen.text: Put me at the head of the table. Yes. There. Now everyone may look at me while they eat.
Mwahaha. That was a laugh. I'm told laughing builds trust. Is it working?

optionen.text: Raises a toast to Megan.

zeile.text: To me. How thoughtful. I'm writing it in your file. The nice part of your file.

optionen.text: Lets her “taste” the pasta.

zeile.text: …Don't tell anyone I laughed. If this leaks, I'll know it was you.

optionen.text: Politely hangs up so the crew can eat in peace.

events.lage: The piazza is empty, the festa lights still strung up. Madame Casanova stands by the fountain in a red flamenco dress, an old portable radio at her feet. She summoned you “for a lesson on behalf of the municipality”. Then she switches on the radio and stops being the mayor.

zeilen.text: Tonight there is no mayor. No festa. No speeches. …Well. Maybe one speech. A short one.
Flamenco is not dancing, Monsieur. It is a conversation where nobody is allowed to lie.
Give me your hand. If you want to stop, you stop. If you don't… we'll see where the music goes.

optionen.text: Takes her hand and lets her lead.

szene_intim.hinweis: Madame Casanova drops the act: no poses, no speeches. She leads the dance, slow and proud, and it turns intimate between two adults who both want it. She checks in, laughs at herself, means every step.

zeile.text: Good. Now listen to the guitar. Your feet will lie. Your hands won't.

optionen.text: Dances with her, just dances.

zeile.text: Only dancing. Yes. That is also a conversation. A beautiful one.

optionen.text: “Not tonight, Madame.”

zeile.text: Then the music waits. The way the whole village waits for me. Patiently. Dramatically.

events.nachklang_text: A rose from her hair lies in your hand as you walk to the tender. The next morning she greets you at the harbour as if nothing had happened. Her eyes say otherwise.

events.lage: A voice message, 23:58. In the background, the office in Monaco: every light switched off except hers.

zeilen.text: First Officer. It is midnight. I am still in the office. Do you know why? Because my yacht is sitting in a bay with no engine and no explanation.
And before you check your account: probation rate, First Officer. Half the fee, until you prove you're worth the other half.
Five days. Then I want a name. Goodnight. I won't sleep. Neither should you.

optionen.text: Texts back: “Understood.”
Plays it to Rosi.

zeile.text: No engine. She said no engine. It's an inverter! Somebody tell Monaco it's an inverter!

optionen.text: Deletes it and goes to bed.

events.lage: A voice message, 06:02. Megan has been up since four. You can hear it.

zeilen.text: Good morning. I made a spreadsheet. It has one column. The column says: who.
It is empty, First Officer. EMPTY. Four days.

optionen.text: Texts back: “The column is filling up.”
Sends her a photo of the sunrise.

zeile.text: Is that a sunrise? Did you send me a SUNRISE? I am adding a second column.

optionen.text: Doesn't answer.

events.lage: A voice message, 07:15. Megan has just come out of a board meeting. In the background, a coffee machine rattles very loudly.

zeilen.text: I just told the board the Eden Bay Weekend is still a success. I said it with a smile. My face still hurts.
Three days. And tell your cook to stop sending me pictures of breakfast. They look good. It is unacceptable.

optionen.text: Passes it on to Lola.

zeile.text: She said they look good? Boss, she said they look GOOD. I'm framing this.

optionen.text: Texts back: “You'll get your name.”
Texts back: “You'll get the truth.”

events.lage: A voice message, 07:40. Rotor noise. Megan is shouting over a helicopter.

zeilen.text: I am in a helicopter. I hate helicopters. I hate them less than your reports.
Landing at eleven. I want coffee, a clean deck, and nobody smiling at me. Two days.

optionen.text: Lets Chiara know.

zeile.text: Eleven. Coffee. Clean deck. No smiling. I can do three of those.

optionen.text: Lets Maxwell know.

zeile.text: A helicopter? Mr. Maximum will greet it. From behind the anchor locker. Very respectfully.

optionen.text: Texts back: “Coffee will be ready.”

events.lage: A voice message, 06:30. Sender: the VIP cabin. One deck above you.

zeilen.text: I am one deck above you. This is a voice message because if I walk down those stairs, I will fire someone on the way.
Tomorrow. Eleven o'clock. The salon. Bring proof. Not feelings.

optionen.text: Goes up the stairs and knocks.

zeile.text: You came up. Nobody comes up. …Sit. You have four minutes.

optionen.text: Texts back: “Eleven o'clock.”
Plays the message to Totò.

zeile.text: Comandante, I run a book. Odds she fires somebody before lunch: two to one. You want in?

events.lage: A voice message, 07:00. No shouting. That's worse.

zeilen.text: Good morning. Today I listen. Only today.
Make it count, First Officer.

optionen.text: Takes a deep breath.
Texts back: “I will.”

events.lage: Maxwell stands at the top of the sun deck with towels over his shoulders, waving you up. Half the crew is hanging over the railing to watch.

zeilen.text: Number One! The sea took our engine, brother, but not our muscles. Mr. Maximum is going to teach you to fight, and lesson one starts right now!
Two to one on the gigante. Comandante, please don't make me rich.

optionen.text: “Show me, Mr. Maximum.”

zeile.text: MAXIMUM! That's the spirit, brother!

optionen.text: Joins his warm-up push-ups first.

zeile.text: Ten for you, twenty for Mr. Maximum! Now we fight!

events.lage: Your tenth win against Maxwell. Down at the railing stands Jana with two bottles of water, forgetting that one of them was meant for Maxwell. She turns red when you look at her.

zeilen.text: Sorry, I– that was really– you just– I brought water. For you. Both. Both are for you.
Mr. Maximum sees everything, little sister. Mr. Maximum also sees that Mr. Maximum gets no water.

optionen.text: Takes a bottle and winks at her.

zeile.text: Na geh… okay. Okay. I'm going to go and stand somewhere else now.

optionen.text: Offers to let her join the next training session.

zeile.text: Me? Fighting? …Will you show me how to stand like that?

optionen.text: Gives Maxwell the second bottle.

zeile.text: THANK you, brother. Jana, Mr. Maximum forgives you.

events.lage: Your third defeat. You're lying on the teak, looking up at the sky. A shadow falls over you: Chiara, arms folded, uniform immaculate. She saw everything.

zeilen.text: First Officer. You are aware that he's on our side? He was going easy on you. I could tell.
Mr. Maximum was NOT going easy. Mr. Maximum was going… medium.

optionen.text: “Then you show me how it's done.”

zeile.text: In this uniform? Absolutely not. …Tomorrow at seven, and don't be late.

optionen.text: Stays lying there and laughs along.

zeile.text: …Fine, that was funny. Now get up, you're lying on my clean deck.

optionen.text: Gets up, offended.

zeile.text: Oh no. I hurt the First Officer's feelings. I'll put it in the log.

events.lage: Lola holds out a spoon to you before the food goes out. There's a sticker on the cooker hood: NO TWEEZERS. She looks at you as if a verdict were about to fall.

zeilen.text: Okay, Boss. Taste. Be honest. No, don't be honest. Yes, be honest.
Mr. Maximum volunteers as second taster. Mr. Maximum is very brave.

optionen.text: Praises it loudly in front of the whole crew.

zeile.text: Did you hear that? Everybody hear that? Okay. Okay. I'm fine. I'm not crying, it's the onions.

optionen.text: Quietly: “That's really good.”

zeile.text: …Yeah? Okay. Okay, cool. Cool cool cool.

optionen.text: Critiques it like a star chef.

zeile.text: Yes, Chef. …Sorry. Habit. Old kitchen. Forget it.

events.lage: Megan claps her hands in the galley: dinner for four, right now, like in a restaurant. Someone shouts “Service!” Lola stands still, the spoon in her hand. She isn't breathing.

zeilen.text: Service! Four plates, now. Chop chop. This is a yacht, not a hippie commune.
Yes, Chef. Yes, Chef. Yes, Chef.

optionen.text: “I'll take over.”

zeile.text: …Thanks, Boss. I just need a minute. Just a minute.

optionen.text: “Lola, pull yourself together.”

zeile.text: Yes, Chef.

optionen.text: “Everybody out. Lola, breathe.”

zeile.text: …Sydney. It was a kitchen in Sydney. Nobody ever said it was good. Not once. Can I tell you later? When she's gone?

events.lage: On the chart table lies a sheet of paper covered in tiny writing: angles, times, and one circled word – Polaris. Chiara's handwriting. Lola leans over to you.

zeilen.text: Psst. Light on the bridge wing, two in the morning, every night. Somebody's studying. You didn't hear it from me.
That's mine. That's nothing. That's… a shopping list.

optionen.text: Hands the page back without asking.

zeile.text: …Thank you.

optionen.text: “A shopping list with Polaris on it?”

zeile.text: Polaris is a very popular brand of… rice. Goodbye.

events.lage: Two in the morning. A torch is burning on the bridge wing. Chiara is measuring the sky with an old sextant, her lips moving. She hasn't seen you yet.

zeilen.text: Thirty-nine… no. Forty-one. Again.
How long have you been standing there? Don't answer that.

optionen.text: “I didn't see anything.”

zeile.text: Good. Neither did I. Goodnight, First Officer.

optionen.text: “Do you want some help?”

zeile.text: I don't need help. I need… nothing. Goodnight.

optionen.text: “Will you show me how you do that?”

zeile.text: …You want to learn? From me? Fine. That's Polaris. And I failed the theory exam in April. Don't tell anyone.

events.nachklang_text: In the morning the page of stars is lying at your place in the mess. At the bottom she has added something: “Night 2?”

events.lage: Jana is wringing out lines on the swim platform in her red-white-red bikini, the tip of her tongue between her teeth. Two decks up, Yamamoto-san is hanging over the railing with a camera whose lens is as long as a forearm. He has binoculars and a notebook too, and he's being very busy.

zeilen.text: Officer-san. Shhh. A very rare bird. Only visible at the swim platform. Between ten and noon.
Sir! Hi! Sorry, am I in the way? I'm only doing the lines. Jessas, the water is cold.

optionen.text: Asks Yamamoto what kind of bird it is.

zeile.text: Latin name: Avis kitsune. Very shy. Very red and white. So sorry, I cannot say more.

optionen.text: Brings Jana a jumper.
Watches quietly to see what happens.

events.lage: Yamamoto is lying on the sun deck, just about to take a picture. Suddenly it goes dark. Behind him stands Maxwell, two metres wide, arms folded, casting a shadow like a wardrobe.

zeilen.text: Mr. Maximum sees a rare bird too. The bird is on the camera's side of the lens. Mr. Maximum has a question.
So sorry. The bird is gone now. Very fast bird.

optionen.text: Lets Maxwell handle it.
Covers for Yamamoto: “He's photographing clouds.”

zeile.text: Yes. Clouds. Beautiful clouds. Very low clouds. Very red clouds.

optionen.text: Invites them both for an iced tea.

events.lage: On the swim platform, Maxwell has dressed a dummy made of towels in a red-white-red bikini and tied it to a deckchair with a line. He's hiding behind the fenders and waving you over. Two decks up, the clicking starts.

zeilen.text: Number One, Mr. Maximum has a plan. The towel is the bait. The bird always comes back.
Ah. Beautiful. Very still bird. Finally, a bird that does not fly away.

optionen.text: Stays quiet and lets the trap work.
Warns Yamamoto.
Fetches Jana so she can see the dummy.

zeile.text: Sorry, why am I made of towels? Is it a surprise? Jessas, it's a good bikini.

events.lage: Jana has finally worked out what's clicking up there. She goes red and waves up anyway. Then she strikes a pose, too loud and a step too far. Yamamoto bows so deeply that the camera slips out of his hands and sails towards the water.

zeilen.text: Hallo, Yamamoto-san! Sorry! I'm the bird! Servus! Is this the good side? Jessas, this is so embarrassing.
So sorry, so sorry. The bird is very beautiful. The camera is very wet.

optionen.text: Fishes the camera out of the water.
Praises Jana: “That was brave.”

zeile.text: I was brave? Sorry. I mean, thank you. I didn't know I could be brave in a bikini.

optionen.text: Hands Yamamoto a towel.

events.lage: This time Yamamoto is sitting on the foredeck with his lens trained on the swim platform. Maxwell comes up silently behind him, takes him by the collar and lifts him a hand's breadth off the deck. Jana stands by with her hands over her mouth.

zeilen.text: Caught! Mr. Maximum catches the bird! Number One, what happens to a bird that gets caught?
So sorry. I am a quiet bird. I only look. I never touch. This is my promise.

optionen.text: Lets Maxwell decide: the photos get deleted.
“He deletes them, but he keeps one photo.”
“Ten push-ups for the bird, and we forget it.”

zeile.text: For the joke! Ten push-ups! Mr. Maximum counts in Zulu! Kunye, kubili, kuthathu!

events.titel: The Last Item on the List
events.lage: Yamamoto has opened his notebook: a list of things he wants to do once in his life. The last item reads: photograph a real bird. Maxwell reads along, and so does Jana. Then Maxwell sets him on the mat, and Jana hands him a towel.

zeilen.text: Mr. Maximum signs the list. Mr. Maximum will take you to a real bird. After push-ups. Many push-ups.
A bird, and a friend with a very large hand. Thirty years of overtime, and this is my holiday.
I'll draw the tick, Yamamoto-san. And a little bird next to it. Sorry, a very little bird.

optionen.text: Joins them on the mat.
Ticks the item off himself.
Takes a photo of all three of them.

events.lage: Half past six on the aft deck. Maxwell, in his neon-orange training top, stands in front of Jana, hair in a plait, still half asleep. Totò sits on a bollard and watches, his coffee mug held like a ticket.

zeilen.text: Mr. Maximum does not say good morning. Mr. Maximum says: burpees! One joke, one burpee. Go!
Sorry, sorry. Is it already time? Na geh. Okay. One. Two. Servus, legs.

optionen.text: Joins the training.
Cheers Jana on.

zeile.text: Thank you, Sir. I can do ten. Maybe six. Okay, three.

optionen.text: Steals Totò's coffee and watches.

events.lage: Jana is holding a plank, her arms trembling, her face bright red. Maxwell crouches in front of her, calm as a rock. Lea comes past with two mugs and joins in counting.

zeilen.text: Mr. Maximum does not hear “I can't”. Mr. Maximum hears “not yet”. Say it with Mr. Maximum.
Not… yet. Not yet. Jessas. Not yet! Sorry, my arms are shaking.

optionen.text: Counts with her.
Reins Maxwell in: “That's enough.”
Lets Maxwell handle it.

betroffen.was: cries with pride and calls it an allergy

events.lage: Jana is in the starting position. Maxwell counts without blinking. At five she's shaking, at seven she swears in Viennese, at ten she collapses onto the mat, beaming. Maxwell turns away and wipes his face.

zeilen.text: Ten! TEN! Did you see? Servus, Sir! Sorry! I did ten!
Mr. Maximum has no tears. Mr. Maximum has an allergy. To very good push-ups. Number One, look away.

optionen.text: Gives Jana a hand and pulls her up.
Hands Maxwell a tissue.

zeile.text: Thank you, Number One. This is not a tissue. This is a push-up towel.

optionen.text: Invites everyone to breakfast.

events.lage: The hangar doors stand open. Pallets, low sun, and outside the white bow of the Eden Rise. A black stretch limousine rolls into the hall, and the loading stops.

zeilen.text: Number One has arrived! Mr. Maximum salutes the limousine!
Madonna, six windows. Comandante, I like you already. I've already put money on you.
Is that a real limo? Can I sit in it? Not now, obviously. Later? Please?
That's the founder of Eden Consulting, darlings. Be charming. Not you, Lea. Me.
Great. A consultant, and he came in a hearse.
Six windows. We're thirteen people with no budget for napkins, and he has six windows.
Mate. Who turns up to a boat in a limo?

optionen.text: “Morning, everyone. I'll carry my own bag.”

zeile.text: …Noted. That's a first.

optionen.text: “The CEO insisted on the car. I'd have taken the bus.”

zeile.text: The bus. Sure you would, Boss. Alright, I like you a little.

optionen.text: “Hi. I'm Duc.”
“Careful with the bags, they're Louis Vuitton.”

zeile.text: See? I told you. A hearse.

events.lage: A woman with a clipboard walks out of the glare. Ten years, and she still walks the same way.

zeilen.text: Duc.

optionen.text: “It's good to see you, Meg.”

zeile.text: …It's Megan now. Fleet Director Megan.

optionen.text: “Fleet Director? Did you yell your way to the top?”

zeile.text: I did. And I'll yell you right back down if I have to.

optionen.text: “And you still look so gorgeous, Mac. It feels like time didn't pass.”

zeile.text: …Time passed, Duc. The gangway's that way.

optionen.text: “Ms McAllister.”

zeile.text: First Officer. Good. Let's keep it like that.

events.lage: Megan leads you to the gangway. At the top stands a woman with a mug of cold coffee, looking at you the way she would look at the weather. For a second her hand goes to her side. Then back to the coffee.

zeilen.text: Captain Marit Holm. Eleven seasons on this boat. She doesn't like consultants. She doesn't like anyone, really.
So you're the CEO's consultant. Can you tie a bowline?

optionen.text: Ties a bowline one-handed. “Behind my back, if you like.”

zeile.text: …Hm. Takk. Don't let it go to your head.

optionen.text: “I can tie a tie. Does that count?”

zeile.text: On my bridge, no. At the party, maybe.

optionen.text: “I have my Yachtmaster. It's in the papers.”

zeile.text: Papers don't float, Frankfurt.

optionen.text: “Can't the crew do the knots?”

zeile.text: The crew does what I do. My coffee's cold, and so is this conversation.

events.lage: At the foot of the gangway: a uniform without a single crease, a clipboard, and a look that finds dust.

zeilen.text: Chiara Sonnberg, Chief Stew. The best in the fleet. Chiara, have you eaten?
Yes.
Liar.
Welcome aboard, First Officer. Your cabin is ready. It used to be mine.

optionen.text: “Then you know what's wrong with it. What would you change?”

zeile.text: …The shower, and that bell. Thank you for asking. Nobody ever asks.

optionen.text: “Then I'll take good care of it. And of the one who had it before.”

zeile.text: …That was almost charming. Don't do it on duty.

optionen.text: “Thank you.”

zeile.text: You're welcome. Breakfast is at seven, and I mean seven.

optionen.text: “Great. Is there a bigger one?”

zeile.text: No, First Officer. There's a smaller one. Mine. As of now.

events.lage: Two legs in work trousers stick out from under the stern. Next to them, a small diesel generator hums away happily.

zeilen.text: Rosi Scuderi, our ETO. Brilliant. She bites.
If you're here to look at the motor, don't touch anything.

optionen.text: “It's not a motor. It's an inverter.”

zeile.text: …Okay. Fine. You can touch one thing.

optionen.text: “I'm here to look at the engineer.”

zeile.text: Wow, that was cheesy. Here, hold this rag, and don't drop it.

optionen.text: “I won't.”

zeile.text: Good. Then we'll get along.

optionen.text: “Can't we just call a mechanic?”

zeile.text: I AM the mechanic, Officer!

events.lage: A man lifts an entire pallet over his head. Then a helicopter thunders over the hangar roof, and he vanishes behind the pallet in a flash.

zeilen.text: Maxwell, steward and trainer. Don't challenge him to anything.
Number One! Mr. Maximum has heard of you! Do you lift?
Mr. Maximum was just checking the pallet. The pallet is fine. Everything is fine.

optionen.text: “Show me. Tomorrow, six thirty.”

zeile.text: A MAN OF HONOUR! Six thirty! Mr. Maximum will cry, but quietly.

optionen.text: “Only my expectations.”

zeile.text: Ha! One push-up for that joke, brother!

optionen.text: “A little.”

zeile.text: A little is the beginning of a lot, brother!

optionen.text: “I have a personal trainer in Frankfurt.”

zeile.text: …Mr. Maximum will be very professional now.

events.lage: A man with a gold-tooth grin is carrying a small crate himself, although there are pallets everywhere.

zeilen.text: Totò, our bosun. If something goes missing, it was Totò. If it comes back, that was also Totò.
Comandante! Welcome, welcome! Don't mind this. Potatoes. Very small potatoes.

optionen.text: “Let me help you carry that.”

zeile.text: No, no! Heavy potatoes. I mean light. Very light. I've got it.

optionen.text: “What are the odds I survive the week?”

zeile.text: Ten to one. Against. But I love a long shot, Comandante.

optionen.text: “Morning.”

zeile.text: Buongiorno, Comandante!

optionen.text: “Shouldn't those potatoes be inspected?”

zeile.text: Inspected? By who? Elsa?! …I mean, yes. Of course. Later.

events.lage: In a corner of the hangar, a bamboo steamer puffs away on a camping stove. She's barefoot, with flour on her cheek.

zeilen.text: Lola, our cook. Don't ask what's in the oregano.
Alright, Boss. You look like a bloke who eats with tweezers. Go on, prove me wrong.

optionen.text: “One day I'll cook for you. Pho, my mother's recipe.”

zeile.text: …A man who cooks? Okay. Now I'm listening.

optionen.text: “That's the best thing I've had in years. Who taught you this?”

zeile.text: Nobody! That's the whole point, mate.

optionen.text: “Maybe later.”

zeile.text: Later is how people starve, Boss.

optionen.text: “Is it gluten-free?”

zeile.text: It's free. That's all it is, mate.

events.lage: Megan checks her watch. The tide doesn't wait.

zeilen.text: Where to first? You've got five minutes.

optionen.text: Visits the Moore sisters at the dive tanks
Visits Jana, the new deckhand
Visits Siri and Yasin, the guests
Visits Yamamoto-san, the guest in the owner's suite

events.lage: Megan taps her clipboard. One more stop.

zeilen.text: One more, and then we sail.

optionen.text: Visits Jana, the new deckhand
Visits Siri and Yasin, the guests
Visits Yamamoto-san, the guest in the owner's suite
Goes back to the gangway

events.lage: Between the dive tanks stand two sisters, one with a notebook, one with wet hair.

zeilen.text: The Moore sisters. One plans everything, the other plans nothing.
Did you see the sea last night? It glowed. I swear it glowed, proper glowing!

optionen.text: “Bioluminescence. Noctiluca, probably.”

zeile.text: You know Noctiluca? YOU KNOW NOCTILUCA?

optionen.text: “Show me tonight.”

zeile.text: It's a date! A science date. Obviously.

optionen.text: “I was in Frankfurt.”

zeile.text: Frankfurt doesn't glow, though, does it?

optionen.text: “Probably pollution.”

zeile.text: And that, darling, is how you lose her.

events.lage: Sophia offers you her hand as if she had rehearsed this moment. Maybe she has.

zeilen.text: Sophia Moore. I read your interview, darling. You said sustainability is a question of hospitality.

optionen.text: “Then you're the expert on board. What would you change?”

zeile.text: …Nobody ever asks the concierge. Thank you.

optionen.text: “I wrote that for exactly one reader. Didn't know it was you.”

zeile.text: Nice line. I might steal it.

optionen.text: “Did I say that?”

zeile.text: You did. Page three, second column.

optionen.text: “I don't usually give interviews to staff.”

zeile.text: Of course not. How silly of me.

events.lage: A young deckhand walks backwards into a door and apologises to it. Next to her stands a crate. The crate meows.

zeilen.text: Jana, first season. She apologises to furniture.
Sorry, sorry – oh! Sorry, Sir. Not you. I meant the door.

optionen.text: “I didn't hear anything.”

zeile.text: …Thank you, Sir. Really.

optionen.text: “Your potatoes are meowing.”

zeile.text: Very small potatoes! Like Totò's!

optionen.text: “Morning.”

zeile.text: Morning, Sir! Servus!

optionen.text: “Megan, there's a cat in that box.”

zeile.text: There is no cat, First Officer.

events.lage: A convertible, two pairs of sunglasses, and a camera that's already rolling before anyone says hello.

zeilen.text: Our guests. Smile, please. She has nearly three million followers, and he has opinions.
The sustainability guy! Say something green, my man!
Hi. Sorry – sorry about him.

optionen.text: Holds a hand over the lens. “Not before coffee, Yasin.”

zeile.text: …Thank you. Really.

optionen.text: “Something green? Your eyes.”

zeile.text: …They're blue, actually. But nice try.

optionen.text: Waves into the camera.

zeile.text: Content! That's content, bro!

optionen.text: “Tag Eden Consulting, please.”

zeile.text: Sure! Smile for the camera!

events.lage: A small gentleman in a Hawaiian shirt bows deeply. Then his camera clicks. He's photographing a seagull. Or not.

zeilen.text: Mr. Yamamoto. Owner's suite, four weeks. He tips like a king.
Officer-san. Very honoured.

optionen.text: Bows, exactly deep enough. “Yamamoto-san. The honour is mine.”

zeile.text: …You know the bow. Very interesting.

optionen.text: “Bird photography?”

zeile.text: Very rare bird. So sorry.

optionen.text: “Welcome aboard.”

zeile.text: Thank you. Please take care of me.

optionen.text: “Can someone take his luggage?”

zeile.text: I carry my own luggage. Thirty years, Officer-san.

events.lage: The helicopter waits on the apron. Maxwell has disappeared. She touches your arm, just briefly.

zeilen.text: See you at the end of the season, Duc. Don't sink my boat.

optionen.text: Watches her go
Heads for the gangway

events.lage: The helicopter waits on the apron. Maxwell has disappeared. She gives you a crooked grin.

zeilen.text: See you at the end of the season. Don't sink my boat, and don't call me.

optionen.text: Watches her go
Heads for the gangway

events.lage: The helicopter waits on the apron. Maxwell has disappeared. She hesitates at the helicopter door. Very quietly:

zeilen.text: Mac. Nobody's called me that in ten years. Don't sink my boat, Duc.

optionen.text: Watches her go
Heads for the gangway

events.lage: The helicopter waits on the apron. Maxwell has disappeared. A handshake. Firm. Short.

zeilen.text: First Officer. Don't sink my boat.

optionen.text: Watches her go
Heads for the gangway

events.lage: The tender hasn't even touched the quay when you hear it. Not one scream, but a whole village of them, and under the screaming a sound like rain on tin. Rats. Hundreds of them, pouring over the fish crates.

zeilen.text: Madonna. Comandante, that is not a welcome committee.
They're not running from anything. They're running at everything. That's not how rats work, I promise you that's not how rats work.

optionen.text: Looks around for something to fight with.

zeile.text: Go! I'll keep the engine running!

optionen.text: “Lesson one, Mr. Maximum.” Takes a deep breath.

zeile.text: Two to one on the Comandante. Today I'm feeling generous.

events.lage: Rosi jumps off the tender behind you, soot still on her cheek from the workshop fire, a baseball bat over her shoulder. She throws it to you without a word. *He was the only one who knew what an inverter was. If I give it to anyone, it's him.*

zeilen.text: Officer, you can't go out there with your bare hands. The workshop's gone, the whole thing burned, and this is the only thing I got out.
His name's Terremoto. I put a weight in the barrel, so when you hit something, it really feels like an earthquake. Go on, I'm right behind you.

optionen.text: Catches it and runs at the rats.
“Thanks, Rosi.” Then charges.

events.lage: Rosi whistles through her fingers. When you turn round, the bat is already flying at you. *Don't grin. Don't you dare grin. Now I'm grinning.*

zeilen.text: Hey, Officer! Since you like looking at engineers so much, here's something an engineer made for you. Catch!
That's Terremoto. There's a weighted core inside, I built it myself, so try not to drop it. And stop looking at me, the rats are over there!

optionen.text: Catches it and runs at the rats.
“Thanks, Rosi.” Then charges.

events.lage: Rosi pushes through the people on the quay and tosses you a baseball bat without asking. *Let's see what he can do with it.*

zeilen.text: You'll need something to fight with, Officer. That's all I could save from the workshop.
It's called Terremoto, like the earthquake. There's a weight in the barrel, so just swing it and let it do the work. Leave the thinking to me, okay?

optionen.text: Catches it and runs at the rats.
“Thanks, Rosi.” Then charges.

events.lage: Rosi throws you a baseball bat, a little too hard, and it almost slips through your hands. *The only thing I got out of the fire, and of all people, he gets it.* Then her voice drops.

zeilen.text: Here you go, Officer. Compliments of the mechanic.
His name's Terremoto. Papa would love him. So please don't make me regret this, alright?

optionen.text: Catches it and runs at the rats.
“Thanks, Rosi.” Then charges.

events.lage: Rosi has caught up with you. She looks you over the way she looks at a bad weld, then she starts pulling things out of her tool bag.

zeilen.text: You're only swinging at them, Officer. You have special moves, so use them. That's what they're for.
Take these three plasters. They heal a little, and using one doesn't cost you your turn.
These two grenades are mine, so be nice to them. Throw the water one first, so the animal is wet. Then throw the shock one at the same animal.
Wet plus shock makes a short circuit. It hurts, and the animal loses its next turn. That's physics, not luck.

optionen.text: Takes everything. “Thanks, Rosi.”

zeile.text: Don't thank me. Just win this time.

optionen.text: “I had it under control.”

zeile.text: You were lying on the ground, Officer. Take the grenades.

zeile.text: Don't thank me. Just win this time.

zeile.text: You were lying on the ground, Officer. Take the grenades.
