zeile.text: You were lying on the ground, Officer. Take the grenades.

events.lage: The last rats spill into the alleys. On the blue boat an old man is standing on his workbench with a boat hook in both hands. He has been holding the gangway for twenty minutes. Not a single one got aboard.

zeilen.text: Hm.
My wife painted that boat. They were not getting on it.
Alva's bar is up the lane. Listen. Go. I will hold the quay.

optionen.text: Holds out a hand from the quay wall. “Come down. I've got you.”

zeile.text: …Hm. Your hand is steady. Good.

optionen.text: “Twenty minutes with a boat hook? You should be on my crew.”

zeile.text: I was on crews before your father was born.

optionen.text: Just nods and moves on.

zeile.text: Hm.

optionen.text: “You could have just run, you know.”

zeile.text: And you could have stayed on your yacht.

events.lage: Barking up the lane, and a door being hit, again and again. The pack has the bar surrounded. Through the gap in the shutters you see a woman with a broom handle and a bottle of grappa, and she looks like she's choosing which one to use first.

optionen.text: Puts himself between the dogs and the door.

events.lage: The last dog slinks off down the lane. The door opens a crack, then all the way. She looks at the claw marks in the wood. Then at you.

zeilen.text: Alva. That's my bar you just defended. So don't expect me to thank you properly. Just come back when there's music.
Everybody's welcome here, o figliolu. Even the ones who arrive by yacht.
Hear that trumpet up the hill? That's the mayor. …Go on. She'll never forgive me if you're late.

optionen.text: Picks up her bar stool and sets it back at the counter. “Open tomorrow?”

zeile.text: For you, I'll open tonight.

optionen.text: “I fought a pack of dogs for you. I think that's worth a drink.”

zeile.text: Careful. I remember who helps me. And who flirts with me.

optionen.text: “Are you hurt?”

zeile.text: Only my pride. And the door.

optionen.text: “Grappa as a weapon? Bold.”

zeile.text: It's the cheap one. I'm not an animal.

events.lage: Up the hill a church bell starts ringing, wrong, far too fast. Then a trumpet. Then something that sounds like a confetti cannon going off in fear. On the piazza a boar the size of a small car is pacing at the foot of the town hall steps. At the top, in a red dress, a woman holds the confetti cannon like a rifle. The boar is covered in glitter and very angry about it.

optionen.text: Walks out into the middle of the piazza. “Over here!”

events.lage: The boar snorts, turns, and trots back into the macchia as if it had an appointment. At the top of the stairs the woman lowers the confetti cannon for the first time.

zeilen.text: Monsieur! You arrive exactly at the climax. That is either destiny or excellent timing, and I accept both.
…My father built these steps. I wasn't going to let a pig have them.

optionen.text: Climbs the stairs and takes the confetti cannon from her. “I think you've won, Madame.”

zeile.text: We won, Monsieur. Write it down. History is watching.

optionen.text: “You shot a boar with glitter.”

zeile.text: And it will never look serious again. That's strategy.

optionen.text: “Is anyone hurt?”

zeile.text: Only the festa decorations. A tragedy, but not a fatal one.

optionen.text: “Next time, maybe hide?”

zeile.text: A mayor does not hide, Monsieur. A mayor poses.

events.lage: The sun goes down over a harbour that looks like a party nobody enjoyed. Someone has rolled out a barrel. Petru brings bread, Alva brings the cheap grappa. Elsa arrives last, in uniform, with her notebook already open. Alva and the mayor end up standing at the same barrel. Neither of them says anything. Then Casanova pushes her glass a few centimetres towards Alva, and Alva pours without looking.

zeilen.text: Lieutenant Ferrandi, coast guard. I'll need statements from everyone. TOTÒ, I can see you behind that crate.
I am also a victim, Lieutenant!
He fights like a sailor. Not like a tourist.
First round's on the house. Second round you pay. Third round, we'll see.
People of Cala d'Orsu! Tonight a stranger from a broken yacht defended our quay, our bar and our town hall. Tomorrow we clean up.
And the day after tomorrow, Monsieur, you come to my office. There is something I need to ask you, and it is not a thing one asks over grappa.

optionen.text: “Rats, dogs, a boar. Nobody hurt. The yacht's still dark.”

zeile.text: …Finally, someone who can count. Thank you.

optionen.text: “Statement: I'm a consultant who owns a baseball bat now.”

zeile.text: Noted. Badly noted. Unofficially? Thank you.

optionen.text: Raises his glass to her and says nothing.

zeile.text: Officially, you were never here.

optionen.text: “Where was the coast guard an hour ago?”

zeile.text: On the other side of the bay with one boat and two men, First Officer. Where were you?

events.lage: You're walking back to the tender when something stops you. On the stone wall above the quay stands a goat, perfectly calm, as if the day had nothing to do with her. Around her neck is a collar, and on the collar a small red light is blinking, slowly, like a heartbeat. Then she turns and climbs the wall, and the macchia swallows her whole. For a moment Casanova's eyes follow her up to the dark line of the mountains.

optionen.text: Watches the mountains for a long moment. Then goes back to the boat.

events.lage: Late on the sun deck. For once Yamamoto has put his camera away. He's holding a small glass of whisky he isn't drinking, and he asks you something nobody on this boat has asked yet.

zeilen.text: Officer-san. Thirty years in a bank, and I never asked anyone this. So I ask you now. How was your life? Before the yachts. Before the suits.

optionen.text: Tells him the whole story: parents who fled Vietnam after the war, a small flat in Germany, night shifts, and a son who was supposed to have it better.

zeile.text: My father was a fisherman in Noto. He smelled of the sea until the day he died, and he never once complained. …I think our fathers would have understood each other, Officer-san.

optionen.text: “Short version: rice, homework, and a mother who checked both.”

zeile.text: Ha. My mother checked the rice. Homework was my father's war. Very interesting.

optionen.text: “It was fine. It's a long story.”

zeile.text: Long stories are the best kind. Another evening, then.

optionen.text: “I'm a self-made man. Nobody helped me.”

zeile.text: Nobody? Hm. In my experience, a self-made man has usually forgotten who made the tea. So sorry.

betroffen.was: is snoring in the galley next door

events.lage: The crew mess, after midnight. Chiara is sitting with a cup of tea and a stack of checklists she is re-laminating for no reason. She looks up when you come in, and for once she doesn't hand you a job.

zeilen.text: Can I ask you something? Not as the Chief Stew. You've got a company, a sabbatical, a limousine with six windows. How did you get there? Who believed in you?

optionen.text: Tells her about his parents' flight from Vietnam, the years of night shifts, and that nobody expected him to get this far.

zeile.text: My grandfather had a captain's licence and a whole wall of photos. Everyone expected my brother to get one too. Nobody ever asked me. …Thank you for telling me. I won't make it a story. It's yours.

optionen.text: “My mother believed in me. Loudly. In front of the whole street.”

zeile.text: …I like her already. Loud women raise people who get things done. I'd know.

optionen.text: “It's a long story. Another night.”

zeile.text: Okay. I'm holding you to that. Another night.

optionen.text: “Hard work. Anyone can do it if they really want to.”

zeile.text: Anyone? Some of us were told what we're allowed to want before we could spell it. Goodnight, First Officer.

events.lage: Past midnight your phone lights up. Chiara, on video, out on the bridge wing in her grandfather's old jacket. She holds the phone as if it might bite.

zeilen.text: Sorry, were you asleep? Don't answer that. My brother just sent the family a photo. Jonas. Four stripes on his shoulders, his own ship, a feeder out of Hamburg.
Everyone's sending fireworks. I've typed congratulations nine times and deleted it nine times. What do I write?
You're the only one I'm ringing, Duc. You've seen me without my lists, so you may as well see this.

optionen.text: “Write congratulations. Then tell me what you'd write if nobody else could read it.”

zeile.text: That I'm proud of him. And that it should have been me first, and I hate that I even think that. …Okay. He gets the first part. You get the rest.

optionen.text: Looks at her, not at the phone. “Write: congratulations, keep the bridge warm, I'm coming for it.”

zeile.text: Ha! He'll hate it. He'll frame it and hate it. Sending. …Thank you, Duc.

optionen.text: “Send him a thumbs up. It's half past one.”

zeile.text: A thumbs up. Right. Goodnight, First Officer.

events.lage: After midnight. Alva, on video, behind her dark bar. The chairs are up on the tables. Her phone lies face down next to a full glass she hasn't touched.

zeilen.text: My mother rang. From Seville. She does it every year when the season ends. The bar has had you for thirteen years, Alva, when do I get you back?
I told her the bar needs me. That's what I always tell her. So, o figliolu. Tell me something that isn't about the bar.
You've seen this bar with the chairs up and me with my shoes off, so don't ask me if I'm fine. Just talk.

optionen.text: Leans closer to the screen. “Then let me be the thing that isn't about the bar. Tomorrow night, after closing.”
“What would you do in Seville, if you went?”

zeile.text: Dance. Badly at first. My grandmother's way, until the floor shakes. …Nobody has asked me that in thirteen years.

optionen.text: “Alva, it's half past one.”

zeile.text: So it is. Sleep well, Officer.

events.lage: A photo from Alva: the chalkboard behind her bar, smudged with forty years of chalk. Next to every name in the village, what they order. Underneath, a message.

zeilen.text: My father kept this board for forty years. The whole village is on it. Do you want to know what the people you're trying to impress actually eat? The first lesson is free. 🍷

optionen.text: “Tell me.”

zeile.text: Petru, fish pie, every week since his Marie died, and every week he says it isn't as good as hers. Madame Casanova, bouillabaisse, as long as she thinks nobody's counting the saffron.

optionen.text: “And what does it say next to my name?”

zeile.text: Nothing yet. That's the interesting part. 😏

optionen.text: “I'd rather find out myself.”

events.lage: One in the morning. Your phone buzzes: Megan, video. You answer. She isn't looking at the camera. Behind her a laptop is playing an anime with the sound off, and her eyes are wet.

zeilen.text: This is a pocket call. I'm hanging up. …Why are you still there?
It's an allergy. Monaco is full of pollen. If you tell a single living soul, First Officer, I will have you reassigned to a pedalo.

optionen.text: “Which episode? No, really. Which one does that to you?”

zeile.text: The last one. The robot finally gets to see the sea. …Don't. Don't you dare smile, Duc.

optionen.text: “I didn't see a thing. Goodnight, Mac.”

zeile.text: It's Megan now. …Goodnight.

optionen.text: “Pollen. At one in the morning. In an office.”

zeile.text: Pedalo, First Officer. Pink one. With a swan's head.

optionen.text: Hangs up at once.

events.lage: Yasin, on video from the sun deck, sunglasses on, very excited. Behind him Siri sits on a lounger reading something on her phone. She doesn't look excited at all.

zeilen.text: First Officer! Big one. Siri's management closed a deal. Nordic salmon, premium farms, huge budget. You're the sustainability guy, so ten seconds on camera: this is the future of fish. Easy.
Yasin, my dad fights those farms. On the island council, every single winter. Did you even read the caption? I didn't write it. I never write them.

optionen.text: “I don't put my name on fish farms. Not for anyone.”
Takes part, but keeps Siri out of the shot.

zeile.text: That's business, bro. And you get my satellite data pack, all week. Winners help winners.

optionen.text: “Siri, write your own caption. I'll check every word with you.”

zeile.text: My own? …I don't think I've written one in six years. Okay. Okay, give me a minute. Sorry. Give me ten.

events.lage: Megan, on video, in the lobby of the Eden Group. She holds a framed photograph at arm's length, as if it were evidence.

zeilen.text: Marketing is making an anniversary book. They found this in the archive. A young stewardess with a silver tray and a very unfortunate haircut. Guess.

I had a degree in naval architecture and a navigation certificate, and they gave me a tray. I carried it for four years. I learned more about ships in the pantry than on the bridge. Don't repeat that.

optionen.text: “Put it in the book. Big. Front page.”

zeile.text: Front page. Of course you'd say that. …I'll consider page two.

optionen.text: “Does Chiara know?”

zeile.text: Nobody on that boat knows, and that's how it stays. She'd be insufferable about it. She'd also be right.

optionen.text: “The haircut really is unfortunate.”

zeile.text: It was a very windy year. Goodbye, First Officer.

events.lage: Madame Casanova, on video from the piazza. Behind her stands a confetti cannon the size of a small car. She holds a remote in one hand and an envelope in the other.

zeilen.text: Monsieur! The Eden Rise is officially invited to the festa of Cala d'Orsu. And I want to do this properly. With ceremony. Three. Two.
…It is not supposed to do that. It is not supposed to point at me. Monsieur, I need a moment. And a broom.
I have the broom, Madame. I brought two. It went much better at eleven o'clock, Duc, you should have seen it.

optionen.text: “We accept. With ceremony.”
Applauds slowly. “Again, please. With the cannon facing the other way.”

zeile.text: Again! Yes! THIS. IS. THE. FESTA! …Everybody duck.

events.lage: Rosi has worked it out on a napkin. With the power you have, the satellite link holds for about forty minutes tomorrow, and tomorrow is Sunday. Lola rings her Nan every Sunday. Jana rings her mum every Sunday. Both calls tend to run long.

zeilen.text: Forty minutes, Officer, not one more, or Unit-01 starts coughing. I'm not splitting it. You are.
Nan's ninety-one, Boss. If I don't ring, she rings the coast guard. She's done it before. Ask anyone in my family, they still talk about it.
It's fine, Sir, honestly. I only tell Mama that everything is super. That takes two minutes. …Maybe twenty. She asks a lot of questions.

optionen.text: Gives the long call to Lola. “Ring your Nan. Jana, you'll have to keep yours short.”
“Take the long call, Jana, your mama has questions. Lola, keep yours short.”
Twenty minutes each, and he takes Unit-01 down to half load himself.

zeile.text: Fine. Twenty and twenty. If Unit-01 so much as sneezes, I'm hanging up on both grannies.

events.lage: For once Totò has a request that isn't about a crate. Jana wants to take the tender into the harbour tomorrow, alone, for the first time. Chiara says no before he has finished the sentence.

zeilen.text: Comandante, the piccola ties a better bowline than me now. Don't tell anybody. One day she wants my job, and I'm getting old, so let her start.
Only to the harbour and back, Sir. Four hundred metres. I've counted. I've counted them a lot, actually.
She's had her boat licence for six weeks. If she scratches the tender, it's my inventory. If she scratches herself, it's my fault. No.

optionen.text: “Take the tender, Jana. Alone, to the harbour and back.”
Sides with Chiara. “Not yet, Jana. Six weeks is too short.”
Sits in the bow himself and keeps his hands in his pockets the whole way.

zeile.text: You didn't touch anything. Not once. Sir, did you see the docking? Did you see it?

events.lage: Elsa's patrol boat runs to Ajaccio in the morning, and she has offered to take a parcel for the Captain. The mess table is covered in candidates. Siri has pushed a small envelope to the very edge, as if it might not count.

zeilen.text: Thermos of coffee, Boss. Hot. Don't look at me like that. She pours it cold to look tough, but I've seen her drink the hot one when she thinks the galley's empty.
She'll want the watch lists, because she always signs them. She'll want to sign them.
And this is, sorry, it's nothing. A card. I wrote two words on it in Norwegian. It's silly. She might not even want it.

optionen.text: Puts Lola's thermos of hot coffee on top of the parcel.
Puts Chiara's watch lists on top of the parcel. “She'll want to sign them.”
Puts Siri's card on top and asks her to sign it with her whole name.

zeile.text: My whole name? Then she'll know it was me. …Okay. Okay, good. She should know.

events.lage: Petru has fixed the davit, two hinges and Lola's blender, and he won't take a cent. Lola wants to thank him with his favourite dish. Chiara has heard what his favourite dish is.

zeilen.text: Fish pie, Boss, a proper one with mash on top, all crispy. He'll cry, in a good way, I reckon. Mostly the crust.
Do it. A man alone eats standing at the sink. I know. Feed him sitting down.
His wife made that pie for forty years. You don't walk into a widower's kitchen with his wife's pie.

optionen.text: “Bake the fish pie, Lola. Petru should eat sitting down for once.”
Sides with Chiara. “Not his wife's pie, Lola. Cook him something else.”
Walks down to the harbour and asks Petru himself, quietly.

zeile.text: Hm. She put the bay leaf in the milk. Nobody knows that. …Now you know.

optionen.text: Ship's rule: whoever helps us eats with us. Food is shared, not hoarded.

events.lage: Totò stands at the head of the mess table with a form from the town hall. A market stall on the quay, all legal. He has filled in every box but one: the yacht has to agree. Lola has already promised him a crate of chilli jam and two bottles of Alva's myrtle liqueur.

zeilen.text: Comandante, in Napoli my whole family sells things. Nobody ever sold anything with a stamp. I want a stamp. One table, market day, Lola's jars, Rosi's radios. Nothing from a truck.
People queue for my chilli jam, Boss! Well. Totò queues. But he'd be queueing in public.
The Eden Rise is not a flea market. If a guest sees our bosun selling liqueur on the quay, it's in a review by lunch.

optionen.text: Signs the form for Totò. “One table, on market day.”
Pushes the form back. “Not under the yacht's name, Totò.”
Signs it for Eden Consulting, not for the Eden Rise.

zeile.text: A stamp. A real one, with a name on it. Madonna, Comandante. My mother will think I'm in trouble.

optionen.text: Ship's rule: no alcohol on deck. The stall sells jam, not liqueur.

events.lage: Chiara has called a short meeting. The subject: since Antibes, Jana has been carrying Siri's towels, sun cream and water bottle around. Nobody asked her to. Siri still calls her Jenna.

zeilen.text: She's crew. Crew are not a guest's personal assistant. If she carries one more towel for Siri instead of coiling lines, I'm laminating a sign.
I don't mind, Sir! Honestly. I've followed her since I was sixteen. It's like carrying towels for a lighthouse.
I never asked her, I promise. Sorry, Jenna. Jana! Jana. Sorry. I'm so bad with names, it's not you, it's my whole brain.

optionen.text: “Jana can carry what she likes, Chiara. It's her choice.”
“Chiara's right, Jana. Crew is crew, so no more towels for Siri.”
“Siri, tomorrow you coil one of Jana's lines. Then you're even.”

zeile.text: Me? A rope? …Okay. Yes. Jana, show me. I'll learn the knot and your name, both.

betroffen.was: recognises the box from ten metres

events.lage: Alva comes alongside in a borrowed dinghy with a cardboard box on her lap. It has come from Australia, by three ferries and a cousin. Lola recognises it from ten metres and makes a sound you have never heard a person make.

zeilen.text: Tim Tams, two packets. And one jar of the black stuff, which I refuse to name. Your cook has been ordering it through my bar for weeks. Alva remembers who drinks her coffee.
Vegemite! Boss, real Vegemite! I'm going to cry, I'm already crying. Mostly the Tim Tams.
That smells like a ship's engine, and it's going in my galley fridge?

optionen.text: Helps Alva aboard and carries the box himself.
Lets Lola teach him the Tim Tam slam, right there on the platform.

zeile.text: Bite both ends, suck the coffee through, and then you've got about two seconds before – yes! Yes! He's one of us now!

optionen.text: Finds the jar a shelf of its own, far away from Chiara.

zeile.text: Bottom shelf, behind the fish sauce, with the lid taped. Merci.

events.lage: Past midnight a searchlight sweeps across the swim platform. Elsa's patrol boat idles twenty metres off. In the beam, a single snorkel. Lea surfaces, sees the light, and salutes.

zeilen.text: First Officer. Your deckhand is diving alone, at night, without a dive computer. I'm not writing that down. I'm telling you, so that I never have to write it down.
Only six metres! There were squid, Duc. Proper glowing ones, the little ones that only come up at night – okay. I can hear it. I'm coming out.

optionen.text: “Out. Now. We'll talk in the morning.”
Kicks off his shoes. “Next time, wake me. I'll hold the torch.”

zeile.text: You'd come? At night? …Okay. Deal. I'll knock. Quietly. I'm very good at quiet.

optionen.text: “Lieutenant, would you check her gear once a week?”

zeile.text: Once a week. I'll bring figs. And TOTÒ, I can see your cigarette from here.

betroffen.was: has never been to a theatre

events.lage: Dinner on the aft deck. Lea mentions, very casually, that her sister spent two years in the West End. Every head turns. Sophia keeps buttering her bread as if nobody had spoken.

zeilen.text: Two years! Understudy for the lead. She knew every single line. I used to test her on the train home.
Darling, an understudy learns every line and then catches the last train home. Two years. Not one night on stage. Pass the salt, would you.

optionen.text: “One line. Just one. For us.”

zeile.text: …The last train has gone, and I find I don't mind at all. There. Act two. Nobody ever heard it. Now you have.

optionen.text: Changes the subject before anyone can ask again.

zeile.text: Thank you. …You're dangerous, you know. You notice things.

optionen.text: “Two years and never once on? That's rough.”

zeile.text: Isn't it. Salt, darling.

events.titel: The Most Mended Net in Corsica
events.lage: Late afternoon at Petru's workshop. The radio is playing Corsican football. Petru is mending a net. You can't see a single hole in it. He has been mending it since you arrived.

zeilen.text: Comandante, don't say anything. That net is perfect. He mends it every afternoon, since Marie. Five years. It's the most mended net in Corsica.
Hm. The sea doesn't hurry.

optionen.text: Sits down beside him and takes the other end of the net.

zeile.text: Hm. Not like that. …Like that. Yes.

optionen.text: “Petru, there's no hole in that net.”

zeile.text: No. Not in the net.

optionen.text: Fetches two coffees from Alva's and says nothing at all.

betroffen.was: wants to know about the wiring

events.lage: Early morning on the foredeck. Lola sits cross-legged with a coffee and a napkin, drawing. A shack, a counter, a sign. She hides it when she sees you, then decides not to.

zeilen.text: Don't laugh, it's a kitchen on a beach. Four stools, one stove and no head chef, and nobody yells. If somebody yells, they're out.
Got a name and everything. Well, half a name. I keep crossing it out.

optionen.text: Takes her pen and draws a fifth stool.

zeile.text: That one's a bit close to the stove, Boss. …I'll move it. Just for you.

optionen.text: “Where's the steamer for the bao?”

zeile.text: You'd know about the steamer. Right here, next to the stove. Nobody's ever asked about the steamer.

optionen.text: “Nice. Shouldn't breakfast be on by now?”

events.lage: Evening in the crew mess. Lola puts a warm plate in front of Lea, who has just come up from a dive. Then she announces her theory to the whole table.

zeilen.text: Every evening, same dolphin, same spot off the point, and she comes back all pink and smiley. I'm not saying it's love. I'm saying I've seen less obvious on Bondi Beach.
He's a bottlenose! He's a research subject! You can't fall in love with a research subject, that's the first rule of marine biology!
What's his name?
…Gerald. Shut up. All of you.

optionen.text: Backs Lola's theory with a straight face.
“Lea is the only one on this boat doing actual science.”
Asks Lea to introduce him to Gerald tomorrow.

zeile.text: You want to meet Gerald? …He's very shy. Bring a fish. A fresh one, he's got standards.

betroffen.was: polishes the railing in the background

events.lage: Yamamoto is on the foredeck with a tablet at arm's length. His daughter Hana is on video from Tokyo, and she has asked to see his bird photographs. He is scrolling very, very slowly.

zeilen.text: Hana-chan, this is a seagull. A very rare seagull. …Yes. It does look like a large man. The light was difficult.
Officer-san. Please. My daughter booked this voyage because my heart made a small complaint. If she thinks I only follow Maxwell-san with a camera, she will book another one. Help me.

optionen.text: Takes the tablet and tells Hana her father has made a lot of friends on board.
Waves Maxwell over to say hello.

zeile.text: Howzit, Hana! Mr. Maximum is the bird! Mr. Maximum is a very rare bird!

optionen.text: Points the tablet at the sky, just as a cormorant flies past.

events.lage: Elsa's patrol jacket lies on a bollard. Next to it, face down, a paperback with a shirtless pirate on the cover. Totò has seen it. Elsa has seen Totò see it.

zeilen.text: Comandante, look. The law of Cala d'Orsu reads The Captain's Forbidden Treasure. Chapter twelve. I am a witness. I am a free man now.
That's evidence. I confiscated it from a tourist. This morning. Totò, if that photo goes anywhere, you get a ticket for every crate in your locker, and I have counted them.

optionen.text: Picks up the book and reads the back cover aloud.

zeile.text: Chapter twelve is the good one, for the record. TOTÒ, PUT THE PHONE AWAY.

optionen.text: Hands it back with a straight face. “Confiscated evidence, Lieutenant. Very dangerous.”

zeile.text: Thank you, First Officer. I'll file it under pending, for a while.

optionen.text: “I've got one like that too. Mine has a lighthouse keeper.”

zeile.text: A lighthouse keeper. …Does he brood? He has to brood. Never mind, I'm not asking. Lend it to me.

events.lage: Lea is sitting cross-legged in front of Unit-01 with her sketchbook, drawing. The old generator has a face now, and tentacles. Rosi has just seen the tentacles.

zeilen.text: Look, she's got a face! The intake's the mouth and the exhaust is, okay, I gave her tentacles. Sea monsters need tentacles. That's basically biology.
She is not a monster. She's thirty-one years old, she's survived two owners and one explosion, and she has never once had tentacles. Draw her properly or don't draw her.

optionen.text: “The tentacles stay.”
“Rosi's right. No tentacles.”
“Draw her as a sea monster that guards the ship.”

zeile.text: A guardian. With tentacles. Fine. Give her the amber eye and I'll hang it in the workshop when it's rebuilt. Don't tell anyone I said that.

events.lage: The festa is in full swing when Jana steps onto the piazza in a red dress. It fits her almost perfectly. It's Chiara's. Chiara is standing right next to you, holding a glass of wine very, very still.

zeilen.text: Sir! Do I look – sorry. Hello. I didn't ask. I was going to ask. Then it was eight o'clock and the dress was just hanging there, looking at me.
That's my dress. That's my dress, and she's doing my walk. Duc. She's doing my walk.

optionen.text: “It suits her, Chiara. Let her have tonight.”
“Jana. Back to the boat, change, then come back and dance.”
Raises his glass to both of them. “Two women in red. Cala d'Orsu won't survive it.”

zeile.text: …Fine. She keeps the dress for tonight. But she gives back the walk.

events.lage: There's a bet on the foredeck. The stake is a week of washing up. The subject is the Captain. Years ago, so the story goes, up north: a bear, one kilometre, one shot.

zeilen.text: One shot, Comandante. One kilometre. The Capitana told it to a harbour master in Monaco, he told my cousin, and my cousin never lies about bears.
Eish, brother. Mr. Maximum respects the Captain. Mr. Maximum also respects physics. One kilometre is very far for a bear, and very far for a bullet.

optionen.text: Bets with Totò: she made that shot.
Bets with Maxwell: nobody makes that shot.
“Ask yourselves why she never tells it herself.”

zeile.text: Maybe because it was two kilometres. Sorry. I'm only saying. She's very modest.

events.lage: Chiara has decided to order in Italian tonight. Loudly and proudly. Alva has decided to answer only in Corsican. The whole bar is listening.

zeilen.text: Buonasera! Vorrei un bicchiere di vino rosso, per favore, and also – how do you say olives? Olivas. Olivetti!
Olivetti is a typewriter, cara. You've just ordered a glass of red and a typewriter. I could help. I'm enjoying this far too much to help.

optionen.text: “She wants olives, Alva. A lot of olives.”
“I'll take a typewriter too, Alva.”
Orders the next round in French, just as badly.

zeile.text: Oh no. There's two of them now. Somebody call the language police.

events.lage: Closing time at Alva's. Yasin wants one more shot inside, golden hour but at night. Alva has said no. Maxwell has quietly taken up position in the doorway with his arms folded. He is exactly as wide as the door.

zeilen.text: Bro. Bro, one minute. Thirty seconds. Do you know who I am? Four hundred thousand followers.
Mr. Maximum stood at the door of the loudest club in Cape Town for six years, my friend. Mr. Maximum has met four hundred thousand people. Not one of them got in after closing.

optionen.text: Stands next to Maxwell. “Closing time, Yasin.”
Backs Yasin: one shot, then out.
“Yasin, film the door. Turned away by the strongest man in Corsica. That's content.”

zeile.text: Mr. Maximum approves of this content. Mr. Maximum would like his left side, please.

events.lage: Seven in the morning. For the third day running Siri knocks at the power room with a coffee for Rosi. For the third day running Rosi pretends she doesn't drink coffee.

zeilen.text: Sorry, it's me again. Sorry. Oat milk, one sugar, I asked Lola. You said I was useless, so I thought, okay, then I'll be useful at seven.
I said useless on day one. Day one doesn't count, everybody's useless on day one. I don't need a coffee. …Is that cardamom?

optionen.text: “Take the coffee, Rosi.”
“Rosi drinks it when she wants to.”
Takes the cup, sips, and hands it to Rosi. “Not poisoned. Good, actually.”

zeile.text: Fine. Fine! Tomorrow, same time. Not because I like it, but because the generator likes it when I'm awake.

events.lage: A parcel from Falmouth has made it all the way to Cala d'Orsu. Inside, wrapped in a Cornish newspaper, is a small seascape: a grey harbour, a red boat, a sky that took four tries. Their mother painted it. Lea wants it on the wall of the mess. Sophia wants it in a drawer.

zeilen.text: It's Falmouth! That's Grandad's boat, the red one, see? Mum did it from memory. It belongs where everyone can see it, proper.
Mum painted that instead of paying the electricity, darling. Twice. I'll keep it safe. Somewhere dark, where it can't cost anyone anything.

optionen.text: “It goes on the wall.”
“It goes in Sophia's drawer.”
“On the wall, but Sophia picks the spot.”

zeile.text: By the door, then. Where you see it last, not first. …It's a good sky. She always got the sky right.

events.lage: Lea is hopping on one foot on the swim platform, half into her wetsuit, one arm twisted behind her back. The zip is stuck exactly where she can't reach it.

zeilen.text: Duc! Help. Emergency. Not a real emergency. A zip emergency. Could you – the back, it's stuck.
Did you know octopuses can reach every part of their own body? I'd make a terrible octopus.

optionen.text: Pulls the zip up slowly, one tooth at a time.

zeile.text: That was – yes. Thank you. That was very thorough. Proper thorough. I'm going in the water now. Immediately.

optionen.text: Does it quickly, like a professional.

zeile.text: Thanks! You're very efficient. That's – yeah. That's good. Efficient is good.

optionen.text: “For the record, I think you'd make a lovely octopus.”

zeile.text: Eight arms and three hearts. Two of them would be going very fast right now.

betroffen.was: is singing in the galley and hears nothing

events.lage: Lea has fallen asleep over her logbook on the aft deck. The wind turns a page. Fish, a crab, a jellyfish with a face. And on page forty-one, very carefully drawn: you, at the helm. She wakes up exactly now.

zeilen.text: Don't – that's a fish. That's a very big fish. With a jaw. Okay, it's you. It's research.

optionen.text: Sits down next to her. “Show me how you did the eyes.”

zeile.text: You look at things like the sea's about to tell you a secret. That's the hard part. I had to watch you for ages. Oh no. I said that out loud.

optionen.text: “It's good. You should draw the whole crew.”

zeile.text: The whole crew. Right. Yes. Good idea. Very… crew.

optionen.text: Takes the pencil and adds a small octopus on his shoulder.

zeile.text: Now it's a portrait of two of my favourite things. I mean – octopuses. Two octopuses.

events.lage: A message from Lea, sent at 00:47. Then a second one at 00:48. Then a third at 00:48.

zeilen.text: Fact of the night: some fish only glow when someone else is looking. 🐟✨ Unrelated. Goodnight.
That wasn't about anyone. It was about fish. Proper fish facts. 🐠 Goodnight properly now. 🙈
also, fact: you snore. very small snore. like a sea otter 🦦 goodnight for real

optionen.text: “Then I'll keep looking.”

zeile.text: Okay. Okay okay okay. 🫣 I'm putting my phone under the pillow now. It's glowing. ✨

optionen.text: Sends a fish emoji.

zeile.text: It's a clownfish. You sent me a clownfish. 🐠 I'm choosing to find that romantic. 🥹

optionen.text: “Sleep, Lea. Early start.”

betroffen.was: is coiling lines and pretending not to notice

events.lage: Since yesterday, Lea salutes every time you walk past. On the foredeck, at breakfast, once from inside the tender. This morning she salutes, drops her coffee and salutes again.

zeilen.text: Morning, sir! Duc. Sorry. Morning, Duc. I don't know why my hand does that. It just goes up.

optionen.text: Steps closer and lowers her hand gently. “At ease, deckhand.”

zeile.text: At ease. Right. I am so far from at ease. You have no idea.

optionen.text: Salutes back, perfectly straight-faced.

zeile.text: Oh, that's worse. Now I can't stop smiling either.

optionen.text: Fetches her a new coffee.

betroffen.was: is taking bets outside the door and can't see in

events.lage: Two identical faulty relays on the workbench. Rosi slides one over to you and keeps a screwdriver behind her ear like a weapon. The stake, she says, is one minute. Loser does whatever the winner says.

zeilen.text: One minute, Officer, and you do anything I say. Don't look at me like that, I haven't decided yet. I'll decide when I win.

optionen.text: Wins, just. “One minute. Tell me something you've never told anyone on this boat.”

zeile.text: That's not fair, that's a question, not an order. …Fine. I talk to the generator when I'm lonely. And lately I talk about you. Time's up.

optionen.text: Lets her win.

zeile.text: You let me win. I saw it. One minute: stand still and don't say anything. …Okay. That was enough. Go away before I do something stupid.

optionen.text: Calls it even, so nobody won.

zeile.text: A draw, so nobody won. Hm, I like draws. Everyone keeps their minute for later.

betroffen.was: is asleep on the galley bench

events.lage: Unit-01 spits oil. Rosi takes the red bandana off her head without thinking and ties it round your forehead before the next spray. Then she notices how close she's standing.

zeilen.text: There, now you look like you know what you're doing. Don't get used to it, because it's on loan.
…Your eyes are nicer with it on. That's a technical observation.

optionen.text: “Then I'm keeping it.”

zeile.text: You're keeping nothing. You can borrow it, every day, until I say so.

optionen.text: Ties it back on her, carefully.

zeile.text: …Your hands are steady, that's good. Very good. Okay, go, Unit-01 is getting jealous.

optionen.text: Hands it back with a nod.

events.lage: A photo from Rosi: an old green Vespa in a Catania street, her father leaning against it in the sun. Underneath, after a long pause, a message.

zeilen.text: Papa's Vespa. 🛵 If I ever get the workshop back, you get the first ride. On the back. You'll have to hold on. Tight. That's physics. 😏
and yes, I remember what I said about holding on. the other night you held on just fine 😏

optionen.text: “Hold on where, exactly?”

zeile.text: Where I say. I'm in front, I decide. 😤 …Officer, stop smiling at your phone, I can feel it from here.

optionen.text: “Deal. First ride is mine.”
“Your father looks proud.”

zeile.text: He was. Of the Vespa. And me. Mostly the Vespa. 🥲 Goodnight.

events.lage: Past midnight, under Unit-01, two torches, one tight space. Rosi tightens the last bolt, shouts "THIS IS MY DESTINY!" at the ceiling, turns her head, and finds your face ten centimetres from hers.

zeilen.text: That was – I yell that, at bolts. It's not about you. Mostly.
…You're not moving. Why aren't you moving?
I don't know why I'm embarrassed. We've been a lot closer than this, and you know it.

optionen.text: Doesn't move.

zeile.text: Okay, nothing happened. Nothing happened, and I'm keeping score. Now get out before Unit-01 sees us, because she talks.

optionen.text: Slides out first and offers her a hand.

zeile.text: Such a gentleman. Ugh. Fine, thank you.

optionen.text: “Your destiny's got oil on its nose.”

zeile.text: Then wipe it off. …Slowly. That's an order.

betroffen.was: is asleep and will never know

events.lage: One in the morning, dough for tomorrow's bread. Lola laughs at something, flicks flour at you, misses, and hits your face anyway. Then she steps in close to wipe it off with her thumb. Very slowly.

zeilen.text: Oops. Hold still, Boss. You've got a bit – there. And there. And… there was nothing there, I just wanted to do that.
You've got flour on you again. Last time you walked back to your cabin like that, and I laughed for an hour.

optionen.text: Flicks flour back.

zeile.text: Oh, it's on now. Chiara's going to kill us, but it's worth it. Mostly the flour.

optionen.text: Catches her wrist, gently.

zeile.text: Hi. Hello. Okay, the bread can wait. Bread is very patient.

optionen.text: “The bread, Lola.”

zeile.text: The bread, yes. You're no fun. You're a bit of fun.

events.lage: A photo from Lola: her bare feet sticking out of a hammock on the sun deck, a sky full of stars behind them.

zeilen.text: Hammock. 🌌 Stars. ✨ Room for two. Ish. Mostly ish. No pressure, Boss, just letting you know the universe is available. 😇
and you know how it flips, mate, we've done this. mostly the flipping 😇

optionen.text: Goes up to the sun deck.

zeile.text: You came! Careful, careful, it flips – oh, we're in. We're very in. Hi.

optionen.text: “Tell me which stars you can see.”

zeile.text: That one's the Saucepan. That's not its real name. Mostly the Saucepan. 🍳 Night, Boss. 🌙

optionen.text: Sends a sleeping emoji.

betroffen.was: is eating the failed ones in the corner

events.lage: Lola is teaching you to pleat bao. You're bad at it. She steps behind you, puts her hands over yours and folds with your fingers. Her chin is almost on your shoulder.

zeilen.text: Pinch, turn, pinch, turn. No, gentle, like you mean it but you're not in a hurry. …You're getting it, so keep going. I'm staying right here.

optionen.text: Keeps going very slowly.

zeile.text: Perfect, that's the best one you've done. I'm not letting go yet, for quality control.

optionen.text: Turns his head. “Like this?”

zeile.text: …Yeah, exactly like that. Jana, out, and take the bao. Take all the bao.

optionen.text: Pleats one perfectly on his own.

zeile.text: Oh, you were faking being bad. You sneaky – that's hot, actually. Annoying and hot.

betroffen.was: is doing push-ups at the far end with his eyes shut

events.lage: Lola is lying on her front on the sun deck, holding a bottle of sun cream over her shoulder in your direction without looking. Her hair is pushed to one side.

zeilen.text: Backs are hard, Boss. I can do arms and I can do legs, but the middle bit is a mystery, so help a girl out.

optionen.text: Takes the bottle and takes his time.

zeile.text: Mmm, you've got good hands. Lower. No, higher. No – yeah, there. Don't stop.

optionen.text: Does it quickly and hands back the bottle.

zeile.text: Speedrun. Respect. Bit rude. Respect.

optionen.text: “Ask Maxwell. He loves a challenge.”

betroffen.was: is filming the sunset at the other end of the deck

events.lage: Golden hour on the foredeck. Siri isn't posing for once. She catches you looking, and instead of the camera smile she gives you the other one, the crooked one. Then she looks away first.

zeilen.text: Sorry. I was – that wasn't a look. It was a… sorry. Do you ever do that, look at someone by accident?

events.lage: Past midnight the wind swings round to the north. The anchor chain groans once, then again. Chiara is already on the bridge wing in her jacket, arms folded, watching the lights on shore drift a little to the left.

zeilen.text: Holm's gone, and I'm not calling Megan about a wind shift, she'd never let me forget it.
So you're the First Officer. Tell me what we do.

optionen.text: Looks at the shore lights, then at her. “No. You've done six seasons here. What would you do?”

zeile.text: Nobody asks me that. They ask me where the good champagne is. Let out more chain, ten metres, and we watch it for an hour. Together, if you're not too tired.

optionen.text: Checks the anchor alarm and makes the call himself. “More chain. I'll take the watch.”

zeile.text: Good call, seven out of ten. I'd have said the same, but you didn't ask, did you?

optionen.text: Yawns. “It'll hold. Get some sleep, Chiara.”

zeile.text: It'll hold, sure. I'll just stand here and make sure of that on my own, then.

events.nachklang_text: An hour on the bridge wing, the chain quiet at last. Chiara rated the night a nine and didn't explain the missing point.

events.lage: Sophia is leaning on the aft rail with two glasses of white wine and that look she gets before a bet. She hands you one without asking if you want it.

zeilen.text: Ten euros says you can't make me laugh. Properly laugh, darling. Not the one I do for harbourmasters.
I've had a lot of practice not laughing. Four seasons of it.

optionen.text: Doesn't try a joke. Tells her, quite seriously, about the time he got locked in a client's walk-in fridge.

zeile.text: Oh, that was a snort. That was a real snort, I haven't done that since I was twelve. Keep the ten euros. I'd rather you remembered the sound.

optionen.text: “I'll take the bet. But if I win, you tell me one true thing.”

zeile.text: One true thing. You're a terrible negotiator, you know. I'd have given you two.

optionen.text: Raises his glass. “I'd lose. Cheers anyway.”

zeile.text: Coward. A charming one, but still. Cheers, Duc.

events.nachklang_text: Sophia laughing at the stern, the real one, a little too loud. She looked around afterwards to see if anyone had heard.

events.lage: The water under the swim platform is glowing blue wherever something moves. Lea is sitting on the edge with her feet in it, kicking slowly, and she pats the teak next to her without looking up.

zeilen.text: Look. Every time I move, it lights up. It's dinoflagellates, they glow when they're disturbed. Which is a bit rude of me, really, disturbing them.
Sit down? You don't have to talk. I mean, I'll probably talk. You can just listen.

optionen.text: Sits down beside her and puts his feet in the glowing water. “Tell me everything.”

zeile.text: Okay, so the light is a chemical reaction, and it might scare off the things that eat them, and – sorry. Your shoulder's warm. I'm just going to rest here for a second.

optionen.text: Sits a little apart and asks her questions about the plankton.

zeile.text: You actually want to know? Nobody wants to know. Right. Okay. Where do I start.

optionen.text: “It's late, Lea. Don't stay out here too long.”

zeile.text: I won't. Five more minutes. Maybe ten. The sea doesn't do this every night, you know.

events.nachklang_text: Lea fell asleep against your shoulder halfway through a sentence about light. The water kept glowing where her feet had been.

events.lage: Unit-01 is idling and the generator room smells of hot oil. Rosi is lying half under the frame with a torch in her teeth. She spits it out when she hears you on the ladder.

zeilen.text: Officer, good, you're here. Hold the torch and don't touch anything, and I mean anything, it's a delicate moment for her.
She's been coughing since Tuesday, and nobody else hears it. I hear it.

optionen.text: Lies down next to her under the frame and holds the torch exactly where she needs it.

zeile.text: Hm. You're not bad at this. Pass me the – yes, that one. Don't look at me like that, I'm talking about the spanner. Mostly.

optionen.text: Holds the torch from the ladder and asks what she's listening for.

zeile.text: The bearing. Hear that little tick, under everything? No? Then you're not listening properly yet. Come back tomorrow.

optionen.text: “It's two in the morning, Rosi. She'll still cough tomorrow.”

zeile.text: She will, and I'll still be here tomorrow. Go to bed, Officer, I've got her.

events.nachklang_text: Two hours under Unit-01, shoulder to shoulder. Rosi called it a draw. On the whiteboard there's a new line at the bottom that she covers with her hand.

events.lage: Siri is sitting cross-legged on the foredeck, scrolling through her camera roll with the brightness turned all the way down. She stops on one picture and turns the phone towards you before she can change her mind.

zeilen.text: This one's not going up, because my manager would hate it. There's no filter, the light's bad, and my hair's doing a thing.
It's from this morning. I was just happy. I don't know when I last took a photo because I was happy. Sorry. That's a weird thing to show someone.

optionen.text: Looks at it for a long moment. “You should write the caption. Your words.”

zeile.text: My words. I don't think I have any. Okay. How about: I was happy, and somebody noticed. Is that stupid? You can say it's stupid.

optionen.text: “It's a good photo. Keep it for yourself.”

zeile.text: For myself. I like that. I don't think I've got anything that's just for myself.

optionen.text: “Your manager's probably right. Bad light.”

zeile.text: Ha. Yes. Probably. Sorry, I'll put it away. Sorry.

events.nachklang_text: Siri's photo stayed in her camera roll, unposted. She showed it to you twice more that evening, as if checking it was still there.

events.lage: The whiteboard in the workshop says ROSI VS. OFFICER in big red letters. Rosi has fourteen ticks. You have three. She's adding a fourth to your side, very slowly, as if it hurts.

zeilen.text: The bilge pump yesterday, that one was yours. I'm a fair person, so I write it down.
Don't get used to it. Fourteen to four is still a massacre, Officer.

optionen.text: Takes the marker from her hand and draws a tiny crown over her fourteen.

zeile.text: A crown. Okay, that's – you can't just be nice in the middle of a rivalry, it's against the rules. Give me the marker.

optionen.text: “Fourteen? I counted twelve.”

zeile.text: You counted wrong, so I'll recount, out loud and with feeling. Sit down, this will take a while.

optionen.text: Nods and leaves her to it.

zeile.text: Hm, no speech. Good, I hate speeches.

events.lage: You sit down for coffee. Rosi takes one look at you, licks her thumb and wipes a streak of grease off your cheekbone before either of you has thought about it. Then her thumb stops halfway.

zeilen.text: That was – a quality check of the cloth. I mean the thumb. It's a very good thumb.

optionen.text: Doesn't move. “Missed a bit.”

zeile.text: Did I. Where. No, don't point, I'll find it myself. Stop smiling, Officer, it's distracting the inspection.

optionen.text: “Thanks. Comes with the job, I suppose.”

zeile.text: It does, everything comes with the job. Drink your coffee.

optionen.text: Laughs and wipes the rest off with a napkin.

zeile.text: Fine, use the napkin. The napkin's never been under a generator, but sure.

events.lage: Sophia's phone buzzes, she glances at the name, and in one smooth movement she hooks her arm through yours and turns you both towards the window, as if you were deep in a very important conversation.

zeilen.text: Harbourmaster. He wants to talk about mooring fees. He's lovely and he never stops. Pretend I'm telling you something fascinating.
There. He's given up. You can have your arm back now, darling.

optionen.text: Doesn't take it back. “Actually, tell me the fascinating thing.”

zeile.text: There isn't one. I made it up. I'll have to think of something now, won't I. Give me a minute. I'm not used to being asked.

optionen.text: “Happy to be a prop. Anytime.”

zeile.text: Careful, I might take you up on that. I go through a lot of props.

optionen.text: Gently frees his arm. “You'll have to call him back eventually.”

zeile.text: Eventually. That's a lovely word. It means not today.

events.lage: At Alva's bar Sophia is writing in her little brown notebook again. Every few lines she looks up at you, then down, and writes a bit more. When she sees you watching, she closes it with one finger.

zeilen.text: Don't ask, it's research. You'd be surprised how much research a person can do at a bar.

optionen.text: “Am I in it?”

zeile.text: You might be, as a minor character. He's tall and asks too many questions, and he's growing on the author, which is very inconvenient.

optionen.text: Doesn't ask, and orders her another drink.

zeile.text: No questions? Darling, you're the first man in four seasons who's let a woman keep her secrets. I may have to write that down too.

optionen.text: Reaches for the notebook, teasing.

zeile.text: Ah-ah. Hands where I can see them. Some things you have to earn.
