events.lage: Siri has bumped into a sun lounger, and she is apologising to it. Quietly and sincerely. Then she notices you.

zeilen.text: Sorry. I mean, sorry to you too. I was saying sorry to the chair. It didn't do anything wrong.
Do you ever do that, or is it just me? Please say it's not just me.

optionen.text: Pats the lounger. “It forgives you. It told me.”

zeile.text: Oh good. That's a relief. It's a very forgiving chair. I like it here.

optionen.text: “I apologise to my car every morning.”

zeile.text: Really? What do you say to it? No, wait, don't tell me, I want to imagine it.

optionen.text: Smiles and walks on.

zeile.text: Okay. Bye. Sorry. Bye.

events.lage: The sun is low and everything on deck is turning gold. Siri holds out her phone so you can take a picture of her. Then, halfway through her pose, she lowers her arms and puts the phone face down on the lounger.

zeilen.text: Actually, no, don't take it, just look. Is that okay? I want one golden hour that nobody else gets.

optionen.text: Puts the phone in his pocket and just looks at her.

zeile.text: You're really looking. Nobody really looks, they look at the screen. Okay. I'm going to go red now. That's allowed too.

optionen.text: “Your golden hour. I'll keep watch.”

zeile.text: Keep watch, like a lighthouse. I like that, you'd make a good lighthouse.

optionen.text: Takes the picture anyway, as a joke.

zeile.text: Oh. Okay. No, it's fine. Delete it later, maybe. It's fine.

events.lage: Evening at the boathouse. Petru is mending a net that isn't torn. On the hook by the door hangs a red hair tie, the kind a girl leaves behind when she means to come back. The radio plays football. He turns it off when he sees you, and that is how you know it's serious.

zeilen.text: Hm.
Laetitia went up to the summer huts. Twelve days ago. She always comes back after three.
In the village they say she was seen with a man in uniform, a soldier, up there by the tower.
I have never asked anyone for anything. Not since Marie died. Bring her down, Officer. Please.

optionen.text: Puts the net down for him. “I'll find her. Tell me the way.”

zeile.text: Through the chestnut woods, up to the old Genoese tower. After that, ask the mountain.

optionen.text: “Did you two argue before she left?”

zeile.text: We don't argue. We say nothing. It's worse.

optionen.text: “Give me a day to get ready.”

zeile.text: Hm. The mountain has waited twelve days. It can wait one more. I'm not sure I can.

events.lage: The path climbs in tight bends through old chestnut trees. In the mud by the first bend there are boot prints, deep and evenly spaced, military soles. Further up, something grunts. A wild sow with four striped piglets stands across the path and has no intention of moving.

optionen.text: Lowers his weapon a little and steps forward slowly.
Reads the boot prints first. “Two men. One of them limps.”
Turns back. “Not today.”

events.lage: An old charcoal pit, a ring of blackened earth, and a fire pit somebody has used recently. The chestnuts here are huge. For a moment the mountain is just a mountain.

optionen.text: Rests a while, then climbs towards the tower.

events.fund: Someone slept here, and not long ago. Two army blankets are folded under a chestnut tree, the corners squared the way only soldiers fold them. One has a dark stain at the edge that has dried brown.

events.lage: The old tower stands on the ridge like a broken tooth. Below it is a camp: three green tents, a radio aerial, men in Legion fatigues cleaning rifles. A sergeant with a grey beard and a black eye patch sees you coming long before you reach him, and waits.

zeilen.text: Halt. This is a military operation. Sergent Kaspar Wolff, Foreign Legion.
You are not a hiker. Hikers have better shoes. Who are you?

optionen.text: Gives his name and his job. “First Officer of the Eden Rise. Down in the bay.”

events.lage: Capra, the goat with the collar, trots past you, straight into the camp, and starts eating a map off the field table. Two legionnaires jump up. Wolff raises one hand and they freeze.

zeilen.text: A goat. On an operation. With a collar.
…May I?
When I was a boy in the Vosges we had one like her. She ate my homework, my shoelaces and once a lieutenant's letter. Good animal.

optionen.text: Lets him scratch Capra behind the ears. “She likes you.”

events.lage: Wolff's sword is long and straight, in a scabbard worn pale at the edges. You don't know anyone who still carries one.

optionen.text: Looks at the sword. “Is that part of the uniform?”

events.lage: He rests one hand on the hilt.

zeilen.text: No. The Legion gave me a rifle, a number and a new name. This one I got from Adjudant Hoffer, who taught me to march.
He called it Parole. His word. When he retired he gave it to me in front of the whole company, and he made me read what is on the blade. Honneur et Fidélité.
He said a rifle does what it is told. With this you have to stand close and look at the man. So I carry it. It is heavy and it is stupid, and I have been told so in nine languages.

optionen.text: Just nods.

events.lage: Wolff pulls a folding stool out for you. He doesn't sit himself. He takes out a notebook, and a pencil he has sharpened with a knife.

zeilen.text: I am looking for a deserter. Caporal Adrien Morel, twenty-eight, wounded. Has anyone in the village spoken of a soldier?

optionen.text: Tells him the truth. “Petru's daughter was seen up here with a man in uniform.”

zeile.text: Thank you. The truth costs nothing, and still most people are too stingy with it.

optionen.text: Shrugs. “Nobody tells a stranger anything down there.”

zeile.text: Hm. That is true of villages everywhere. It may even be true of you.

events.lage: He writes something down. It takes longer than one word should take.

zeilen.text: So. Why does an officer from a yacht climb a mountain in the wrong shoes?

optionen.text: “A father asked me to bring his daughter home.”

zeile.text: Then we want different things from the same mountain. That is not a problem yet.

optionen.text: “The view. I needed a day off the boat.”

zeile.text: The view. Of course. It is a very good view. I have looked at it for nine days.

events.lage: Wolff closes the notebook and puts it in his breast pocket. Now he sits down, on an ammunition crate, so that his one eye is level with yours.

zeilen.text: Last question. If you find him before I do, will you tell me?

optionen.text: Holds his gaze. “I'll hear his side first. Then I'll decide.”

zeile.text: An honest answer that I don't like. I will remember both parts.

optionen.text: “Of course, Sergent.”

zeile.text: Of course. Good. I have written it down.

events.lage: Wolff stands up and points along the ridge with the pencil.

zeilen.text: The deserter is wounded. He will not get far, and he knows it. So I wait. Waiting is half of my job, and the half I am best at.
Go and find your girl, Officer. Take as long as you need. I will be here.

optionen.text: Nods and follows the ridge.

events.lage: The legionnaires nod at you. Wolff is writing in his notebook and does not look up.

zeilen.text: Still looking? Good. So am I.

optionen.text: Takes the ridge path again.
Goes back down to the boat.

events.lage: The path runs along a cliff below the tower. A wolf stands on the ledge ahead, grey and thin, a red light blinking at its throat. There are no wolves on Corsica. This one doesn't know that.

optionen.text: Holds his ground on the narrow path.

events.lage: The lake is so still it looks like a second sky. An ape crouches on the rocks at the shore, collar blinking, and something red floats in the reeds behind it.

optionen.text: Walks along the shore towards the red thing.

events.lage: It's a scarf, soaked through and caught in the reeds. Faded red, like the hair tie on Petru's door. It's the kind a girl ties round her neck when she climbs.

optionen.text: Wrings it out and puts it in his pocket. “I'll give it back to her.”
Leaves it where it is. “She lost it. That's all it means.”

events.titel: An Old Woman at the Water
events.lage: There's a small stone hut at the far end of the lake, herbs drying over the door, a candle in the window in broad daylight. An old woman in black is sitting on the step. She has been watching you the whole time.

zeilen.text: You found the scarf. Of course you did. The mountain wanted you to.

optionen.text: Walks over to her.
Nods to her and keeps climbing. “Later.”

events.fund: A flat rock by the water, warm from the day. Someone has stacked three stones on it, small to big, the way children do. Or the way a woman does when she wants someone to know she was here.

events.lage: A stone fold, a handful of sheep, and a farmhouse that has been patched more often than it has been painted. A shepherd with a shotgun over his shoulder is counting his sheep. He counts them twice. Then a third time.

zeilen.text: Forty. Still forty. Thank God. Who are you? Not one of the men in black, I can see that.

optionen.text: Asks what he's afraid of.
Tells him he's looking for Petru's daughter and moves on.

zeile.text: Laetitia? Up at the bergerie, past the ridge. And if you change your mind, I'll be here. Counting.

events.lage: The fog comes up so fast you can hear it. A man in a black suit steps out of it as if he had been waiting for you. Earpiece, gloves, a pistol he doesn't bother to draw.

optionen.text: “Lost your way to the office?”

events.lage: Two more of them, back to back in the fog. One is talking into a radio. When he sees you he doesn't stop talking, he just says it faster.

optionen.text: Goes for the one with the radio.

events.lage: The radio lies in the wet grass, still hissing. A small white logo on the side: A.V. Estates. Somebody on the other end says a name you know from the hearing, then the line goes dead.

optionen.text: Takes the radio.
Smashes it on a rock.

events.lage: A rope bridge over a gorge so deep the river is only a sound. On the other side a big grey wolf is waiting, and behind it, the smoke of a chimney. The bergerie.

optionen.text: Steps onto the bridge. It sways. So does he.

events.lage: A rifle barrel comes out of the dark before anything else does. Behind it is a young woman with her father's eyes and none of his patience. On a cot by the fire lies a man with a bandaged chest, trying to sit up.

zeilen.text: One more step and I'll find out if this thing still works. Who sent you? The suits or the Legion?
Laetitia. Look at his shoes. He's not either.
Then he's my father's. That's worse.

optionen.text: Holds out the red scarf. “He's worried sick. And you dropped this.”

zeile.text: …You went into the lake for that? Idiot. Thank you.

optionen.text: Raises his hands. “Petru sent me. Nobody else knows I'm here.”

zeile.text: Everybody knows everything on this mountain. That's the whole problem.

events.fund: The bergerie smells of smoke, sheep and iodine. Bandages are drying on a line over the hearth. On the table, next to a camera with a cracked lens, someone has laid out bread for three.

events.lage: Adrien hands you the camera with the cracked lens. The pictures are blurry and terrible and you can't stop looking at them. Cages in a long hall. A bear with a blinking collar. Men in black suits with clipboards.

zeilen.text: My unit was lent out. Officially it was a security contract. An estate in the mountains, a rich man, very nervous.
They were testing the animals. Making them do things. Attack things. I took pictures, and then I ran. Desertion. Five years, if Wolff takes me back.
He's not going back. I don't care what anyone says.

optionen.text: “Then we need a better plan than a rifle and a bergerie.”

zeile.text: They'll come tonight. The suits. They always come at night.

events.lage: The light goes orange, then grey. Then two men in black come up the slope, and behind them a third one, much bigger, who doesn't need a weapon.

zeilen.text: Adrien, stay down. I mean it.

optionen.text: Steps out in front of the door.

events.lage: The light goes orange, then grey. Then two men in black come up the slope, and behind them a third one, much bigger, who doesn't need a weapon. Halfway up the slope something huge and grey bursts out of the alders and throws the big man sideways like a sack of flour. Old Grey, the bear you cut the chip out of, looks at you once. Then she is gone.

zeilen.text: Adrien, stay down. I mean it.

optionen.text: Steps out in front of the door.

events.lage: They come at dusk, and there are more of them than Adrien expected. Three suits and one enormous man who walks like a door that has learned to move. They knew someone was on the mountain.

zeilen.text: Adrien, stay down. I mean it.

optionen.text: Steps out in front of the door.

events.lage: They come at dusk, and there are more of them than Adrien expected. Three suits and one enormous man who walks like a door that has learned to move. They knew someone was on the mountain. Halfway up the slope something huge and grey bursts out of the alders and throws the big man sideways like a sack of flour. Old Grey, the bear you cut the chip out of, looks at you once. Then she is gone.

zeilen.text: Adrien, stay down. I mean it.

optionen.text: Steps out in front of the door.

events.lage: Only one of them comes, the big one, alone. The others never came down from the ridge last night. You heard the screaming. Nobody in the bergerie has slept since.

zeilen.text: Adrien, stay down. I mean it.

optionen.text: Steps out in front of the door.

events.lage: Only one of them comes, the big one, alone. The others never came down from the ridge last night. You heard the screaming. Nobody in the bergerie has slept since. Halfway up the slope something huge and grey bursts out of the alders and throws the big man sideways like a sack of flour. Old Grey, the bear you cut the chip out of, looks at you once. Then she is gone.

zeilen.text: Adrien, stay down. I mean it.

optionen.text: Steps out in front of the door.

events.lage: The last agent drags himself into the dark. In the silence afterwards you hear boots on the path. Wolff, with two legionnaires and a torch. He takes in the bodies, the bandages, the rifle in Laetitia's hands, and he doesn't raise his voice once.

zeilen.text: Caporal Morel. On your feet, if you can.
Sergent. They lent us out. To him. You saw the contract, you know what the estate is.
I know what a contract is. I also know what desertion is.
He was shot running away from a cage full of tortured animals, and you want to put him in one.
Mademoiselle, I didn't write the law. I only carry it up mountains.
Show him the pictures. Please. He won't believe me. Maybe he'll believe you.

optionen.text: Hands Adrien over. “He'll get a fair hearing. That's all I can give him.”
Gets between Wolff and the door. “They're leaving tonight. By sea.”
Hands Wolff the camera. “Look at these first. Then decide.”

events.lage: The last agent drags himself into the dark. In the silence afterwards you hear boots on the path. Wolff, with two legionnaires and a torch. He takes in the bodies, the bandages, the rifle in Laetitia's hands, and he doesn't raise his voice once. Then a second light comes up the path, an old hunting rifle, a man who climbed all night. Petru.

zeilen.text: Caporal Morel. On your feet, if you can.
Sergent. They lent us out. To him. You saw the contract, you know what the estate is.
I know what a contract is. I also know what desertion is.
He was shot running away from a cage full of tortured animals, and you want to put him in one.
Mademoiselle, I didn't write the law. I only carry it up mountains.
Show him the pictures. Please. He won't believe me. Maybe he'll believe you.
Laetitia. Old Dumenica dreamed you dead. I came. I'm here.
Papa? You climbed up here? At night? You can't even climb onto your own boat!

optionen.text: Hands Adrien over. “He'll get a fair hearing. That's all I can give him.”
Gets between Wolff and the door. “They're leaving tonight. By sea.”
Hands Wolff the camera. “Look at these first. Then decide.”

events.lage: You call Totò. He answers on the second ring, and he doesn't let you finish.

zeilen.text: Comandante, I like you. But a deserter, the Legion and the mayor's favourite fisherman's daughter, on my boat, tonight? You don't know me well enough to ask. Not yet.

optionen.text: Hangs up and turns back to Wolff.

events.lage: Adrien doesn't fight. He lets them put the cuffs on and looks at Laetitia the whole time, as if he wanted to remember her exactly. Wolff hands you an envelope and his képi.

zeilen.text: For your trouble. And the képi, because you are the first civilian in nine years who made my job easier. Don't wear it in the village.
I hope you can sleep, Officer. I really do. I won't.
It's all right, Laetitia. He did what the law says. That's not nothing.

optionen.text: Says nothing. Walks down behind them.

events.lage: Totò says one word on the phone, “Midnight,” and hangs up. Wolff looks at you for a long time. Then he looks at the dark where the path goes down to the sea, and he doesn't send anyone after you.

zeilen.text: I will report that the deserter was not found. I will hate writing it.
Tell Papa… no. Don't tell him anything. He'll know.
We'll send a postcard. From somewhere without mountains.

optionen.text: Walks them down to the cove, where Totò's boat waits without lights.

events.lage: Wolff looks at the first picture. Then he puts the camera down very carefully on the wall, as if it might go off, and draws his sword.

zeilen.text: You show me this in front of my men. You know I have to answer it. Defend yourself.

optionen.text: Takes his stance. “Then let's get it over with.”

events.lage: Wolff looks at the pictures, then at you, and his face closes like a door.

zeilen.text: Of course, Sergent, you said to me at the tower. The view, you said. And now you hand me pictures and want me to believe them. Defend yourself, liar.

optionen.text: Takes his stance. He's earned that one.

events.lage: Wolff sits on the wall, breathing hard, and goes through the pictures one by one. When he gets to the bear he stops for a long time. Then he looks at the words on his sword, Honneur et Fidélité, and puts it away.

zeilen.text: We swore an oath. To the Legion. Not to a company, and not to a man who keeps animals in cages.
Caporal Adrien Morel died in action on this mountain. I will write it myself. Tonight.

optionen.text: Gives him a hand up.

events.titel: A Dead Man at the Bergerie
events.lage: Adrien laughs until his bandages hurt. Laetitia doesn't laugh. She sits down next to him and holds his hand, and that is the answer to the question her father will ask.

zeilen.text: A dead man needs a job. I'll keep the bergerie. Come up whenever you need someone who knows the mountain.
I'm staying with him. Tell Papa I'll come down on Sunday. Tell him I said Sunday.

optionen.text: Promises to tell him exactly that.

events.lage: When Wolff came at you, Petru stepped in front of his daughter with his old rifle and caught the blow meant for her on his right hand. Now he sits on the wall with it wrapped in Laetitia's scarf and doesn't complain.

zeilen.text: Hm. It was a good hand. Forty years of nets.
Papa, it's broken. It's completely… why did you do that?
Because the old woman dreamed you. And I'm your father. That's all.

optionen.text: Splints the hand as well as he can.

events.lage: Laetitia walks past the boathouse without looking in. Petru watches her go up to the house. Then he turns to you.

zeilen.text: She's home. Thank you, Officer. She won't speak to you again. Maybe not to me either. But she's home.

optionen.text: Stays a while.

events.lage: The boathouse is dark. Petru is sitting in it anyway. Somebody from the village has already told him about Totò's boat.

zeilen.text: Get out of my workshop.

optionen.text: Stays a while.

events.lage: Petru listens without a word. When you get to Sunday, he puts the net down.

zeilen.text: Sunday. Hm. I'll make the fish pie.

optionen.text: Stays a while.

events.lage: Ghjuvan leans his shotgun against the fold and talks without looking at you, as if he had said it to the sheep too many times already.

zeilen.text: Five generations on this pasture. My grandfather, my father, me. We never sold a metre.
Then the bank. Then the men in black suits, twice, with a pen and a very good price. And now a bear. There are no bears on Corsica. Every night, one sheep.
Ten more and I sign. Kill it. Please. I have my father's knife and forty sheep. That's everything.

optionen.text: “Show me where it comes from.”

zeile.text: Along the goat path. You'll see. You'll wish you hadn't.

optionen.text: “I'll come back for it. I promise.”

zeile.text: Everybody promises. The bear comes anyway.

events.lage: Ghjuvan is counting again. Thirty-eight. He doesn't say anything. He just looks at you.

zeilen.text: Two more last week. Go, Officer. Please go.

optionen.text: Takes the goat path.
Not today, Ghjuvan.

events.lage: Three goats lie along the path, a few steps apart. They are torn open and not eaten. Something killed them for nothing. Two feral dogs have found them first and they don't want to share.

optionen.text: Drives the dogs off the path.

events.lage: Ghjuvan has come up after you with a pot of soup. He sits by the fire with the shotgun across his knees and talks to the flames.

zeilen.text: My wife used to sing up here. Badly. The sheep loved it. Since she died they don't come when I call.
If I sign, the men in black put a fence round it and the pasture is gone. Five generations, and I'm the one who ends it.

optionen.text: Eats the soup and listens.

events.fund: Ghjuvan's summer hut. A bed, a stove, a calendar from a feed merchant in Corte, every day crossed out in red. Under the calendar is a letter from the bank, folded so often it is falling apart.

events.lage: A high, thin squeal from the alders. Then it steps out: a bear cub, fat and clumsy, with a blinking red collar of its own. It stares at you. A second little face peers out of the bushes behind it.

optionen.text: Freezes.

events.lage: The den smells of wet fur and old bones. She is enormous and grey at the muzzle, and the collar has cut so deep into her neck that the fur has grown over the light. Somewhere behind her, the cubs are crying.

optionen.text: Plants Le Large in the ground. “Come on, then.”

events.lage: Old Grey lies on her side and breathes like a bellows. The red light blinks under her fur. The cubs have crawled up against her belly and are shaking. She is still trying to get up between you and them.

optionen.text: Ends it, quickly, for Ghjuvan.
Takes out his knife. “Hold still.” Cuts the chip out of her neck.

events.lage: Ghjuvan listens to it all and then sits down in the grass among his sheep. He takes his father's knife off his belt and holds it out to you, handle first.

zeilen.text: You saved five generations today. Take it. My father would want it in a hand that did something.
…The little ones. Will they make it, without her?

optionen.text: Doesn't answer. Takes the knife.

events.lage: Ghjuvan stares at the chip in your hand, then at you.

zeilen.text: She has cubs. I understand. I have sheep. Do you understand that?
She will be hungry and she will have three mouths. You know where she'll come.

optionen.text: “Without the chip she'll stay in the mountains. I'm sure of it.”

zeile.text: You're sure. Good. Then I'll sleep tonight.

events.lage: You go back to Old Grey's den once more. You don't know why. The two cubs are lying in front of it, curled up against each other in the sun. One of them lifts its head when you come. The other one doesn't.

optionen.text: Stays until the light goes.

events.lage: Ghjuvan's fold is empty. A new fence runs across the pasture, and on the gate hangs a white sign with a small logo. A.V. Estates. Private property. On the doorstep of the farmhouse lies a shepherd's crook nobody picked up.

optionen.text: Walks back down.

events.lage: Inside, the hut is all herbs and candles. Dumenica pours you something bitter in a cup without a handle and sits down so close that her knees touch yours.

zeilen.text: I hunt when I sleep, my son. Every night. And the beast I kill in the dream always has a face.
Last night it was black, with yellow eyes. And it had the face of Petru's girl.
Kill the beast while you are awake, and the dream breaks. That is the only way. I'm too old to do it.

optionen.text: “Where is it?”

zeile.text: Up on the ridge, at night, you'll see the lights. Follow the lights.

optionen.text: “I don't believe in dreams. But I'll look.”

zeile.text: Nobody believes. Then they come back to me, afterwards. Go.

events.lage: The candle is burning in the window again. Dumenica opens the door before you knock.

zeilen.text: I dreamed the black beast again. Closer.

optionen.text: Goes up to the ridge.
Not tonight.

events.lage: Night. Red lights move along the ridge in the fog, slow, in a line. Not torches. Infrared lamps. Two men in black, and one of them is holding a grey handset with a dial, turning it like a radio.

optionen.text: Moves in before they can call anyone.

events.lage: The handset is still warm. On its little screen a dot is moving, further up the mountain. Next to the dot it says PANTHERA 02 and a percentage, falling. They weren't hunting the beast. They were steering it, like a dog, to sniff out Adrien.

optionen.text: Pockets the controller.

events.lage: A hut on the way to the dot, and nobody has lived in it for a long time. A little wooden dog stands on the table, the only thing without dust. When you come back out, Dumenica is standing in the dark by the door. She must have followed you up the whole way.

zeilen.text: My son's. Twenty years ago I dreamed his face. I told him. He laughed. A week later the mountain kept him.
I dust his dog every Sunday. Only the dog. I can't touch the rest.

optionen.text: Puts a hand on her shoulder. Then keeps going.

events.fund: The hut has been empty for twenty years and nobody has touched it. Dust on the table, a cup turned upside down, and in the middle a small dog carved out of chestnut wood. A child's toy. Someone has dusted the dog. Only the dog.

events.lage: Barking ahead, wild and close. A pack of feral dogs has the black beast's scent and is hunting it up the ravine, and you are standing in their way.

optionen.text: Stands his ground.

events.lage: In a crack in the rock lies a panther, black, thin to the bone. The collar has been burned into its fur. It doesn't hide. It drags itself out to meet you like something that only wants it to be over.

optionen.text: Lifts his weapon.

events.lage: The panther lies at your feet. Behind it, deep in the crack, something hangs from a red thread: a crescent of boar tusk with raven feathers and a pale moonstone. Somebody hung it there long before the collar, and you take it. The controller in your pocket is buzzing. On its screen there are three more dots now, up on the ridge, coming down towards the bergerie. The agents. And one dial that would turn the beast around and send it at them.

optionen.text: Ends it, here, awake, the way Dumenica asked.
Turns the dial. Sends the beast at its masters.

events.lage: Dumenica cries without making a sound. Then she takes a little silver hand off her own neck and puts it round yours.

zeilen.text: It's broken. I feel it. The girl will live. Wear this, so you always wake up.
…But something is still looking for her. I can feel that too.

optionen.text: Thanks her. Doesn't tell her about the three dots on the screen.

events.lage: The panther gets up as if someone had pulled it on a string, and runs. A minute later the screaming starts on the ridge, men's voices, three of them, then fewer. Then the beast itself screams, high and long, as the chip burns out. Then nothing. When you come down, Dumenica is standing at the lake with a candle.

zeilen.text: I heard it die. In the dark. Screaming. Exactly as I dreamed it.
Then the dream is true. The girl will die. I have to tell Petru. I have to tell him now.

optionen.text: “Dumenica, wait. It doesn't mean…”

zeile.text: It always means. That is the curse, my son. It always means.

events.lage: The switchbacks are quieter now. Something still rustles under the chestnuts, and the tower is still up there.

optionen.text: Hunts along the ridge for collars.
Climbs up to the bergerie.
Just walks, and turns back at the clearing.

events.lage: Adrien is splitting wood with one arm. He lifts the axe in greeting.

zeilen.text: The dead man says hello. Coffee? It's terrible. Laetitia says it's the best on the mountain.

optionen.text: Has the terrible coffee.

events.lage: Laetitia lowers the rifle when she sees it's you. Adrien is pale and sweating. Outside, the light is going.

zeilen.text: You came back. Good. They'll come tonight, I can feel it.

optionen.text: Checks his weapon and waits by the door.
Goes back down for now.

events.lage: The way down always takes longer than the way up.

optionen.text: Heads back to the boat.

events.lage: When you come to, Adrien is already in cuffs. Wolff is sitting on the wall with the camera on his knees. He hasn't looked at it. He won't now.

zeilen.text: You fought well. It changes nothing. I am taking him down.
Get out. Get out of here.

optionen.text: Goes.

events.lage: Petru calls. He never calls. Behind him you can hear the radio, turned off, and the harbour.

zeilen.text: Ghjuvan Santucci. The shepherd. They found him this morning on his pasture.
The bear you let live came down in the night with her young. He went out with the shotgun for his last sheep. Hm. Forty sheep.
The men in black were at the funeral. With flowers. And a pen.

optionen.text: Says nothing for a long time. Then: “Thank you for telling me.”
“That's on me, Petru.”

zeile.text: On you, on the bear, on the bank. On the men with the pen. Mostly on them.

events.lage: Petru, short of breath, as if he'd run to the phone.

zeilen.text: The old woman's hut by the lake burned down last night. Dumenica. They found her sitting outside in the grass, holding a little wooden dog.
She said men in black were looking for someone and didn't find him. So they found her hut. She is alive. She says she didn't dream it. That's what frightens her.

optionen.text: “Bring her to the village. I'll pay for whatever she needs.”

zeile.text: Hm. She can have Laetitia's room. Until.

optionen.text: Tells him to keep her safe.

events.lage: Totò catches you on the quay and presses a postcard into your hand. On the front, a town you don't know, flat as a plate. On the back, in biro, a blue boat on trestles, and one line: “Papa – the sea is different here. Not better. – L.”

zeilen.text: From our two runaways, Comandante, Laetitia and her soldier. It came to my cousin in Bastia. It's not for me. And I don't think it's for you either.

optionen.text: Takes it to Petru.
Keeps it for now.

events.lage: The boathouse is dark again. You put Laetitia's postcard on the workbench, next to the net. Petru reads it. Then he reads it again.

zeilen.text: Twelve years she wanted to leave. Twelve years I said nothing.
She drew the boat. She still knows where the keel goes.
Take this. I wore it the night Marie, my wife, said yes. I was strong then, and stupid. Like you.

optionen.text: Takes the coat.
Takes the coat, and switches the radio on for him.

events.nachklang_text: He puts the net down and switches the radio back on. Corsican football. He doesn't look up, but he turns it a little louder.

events.lage: Evening. The radio is off. Petru has pulled the old sea chest out from under the workbench. His splinted hand rests on the lid. Totò sits on a crate by the door and pretends not to listen.

zeilen.text: When I was twenty, I could lift the mooring stone at the end of the quay. Alone. The whole village came to watch.
I wore this that winter. On the tuna boats out of Bastia. Six weeks, and the sea never got through it.
This hand can't hold a net now. Hm. The coat still holds. Take it.

optionen.text: Puts the coat on.
Puts the coat on, and lifts the chest back under the bench for him.

events.nachklang_text: It fits. Petru looks at you for a long moment. “Hm.” This one means yes.

events.lage: A coat lies folded on the workbench when you come in. Navy wool, old brass buttons. Petru doesn't put the net down. Outside on the quay, Totò mends a fender and doesn't come in.

zeilen.text: I wore this when I was young and strong. Twenty years at sea in it. It bought me my first boat.
You brought my daughter home. Take it. We are even.

optionen.text: Takes the coat.
“She'll come round, Petru.”

zeile.text: Hm. The sea doesn't hurry.

events.nachklang_text: He goes back to the net. The radio stays off.

events.lage: The first morning after the hearing. Lola has laid the table the way she always does, and then taken one plate away again, the plate of the one who was fired at the hearing. Nobody mentions the empty chair. Everybody looks at it.

zeilen.text: I made pancakes. I made one too many. I'll eat it. It's fine. I'm fine.
Mr. Maximum has seen many teams lose a player. The team that talks about it wins.
Comandante, one question. Is it over now, or is this only the start?

optionen.text: “It was the right call. It still hurts. Both things are true.”

zeile.text: Both things. Okay. I can hold two things. I'm a chef.

optionen.text: “It's the start, Totò. We're going to find out who's really behind all this.”

zeile.text: Then I want more coffee. A lot more coffee.

events.lage: The first morning after the hearing. Somebody has hung a bedsheet over the mess door with GOOD MORNING EDEN on it in ketchup. Lola is singing. The coffee is strong enough to stand a spoon in.

zeilen.text: We survived the hearing and nobody went to prison! I made the celebration pancakes, and they're shaped like Megan. Eat her face.
Mr. Maximum would like to say a few words. Twenty-five words. Maybe thirty.
One euro says Maxwell needs a hundred. Who's in?

optionen.text: Puts a euro on the table. “A hundred and twenty.”

zeile.text: Ha! A man of the people!

optionen.text: Lets Maxwell talk. All hundred and forty words.

zeile.text: …and that, brothers and sisters, is why we are a team. Thank you. Mr. Maximum is crying.

events.lage: The first morning after the hearing. Breakfast is on the table, but nobody talks while you're in the room. When you sit down, two people find a reason to get up.

zeilen.text: Coffee's there. Pancakes are there. I'm… there. Over there.
Comandante, nobody knows what really happened the night of the fire. That's the problem, everybody guesses.

optionen.text: “Then let's stop guessing. Whatever it takes, I'll find out.”

zeile.text: Okay. Prove it. I'll believe it when I see it.

optionen.text: Eats in silence. Some mornings you just eat.

events.titel: A Red Eye in the Dark
events.lage: Evening. A noise comes up from the generator room that Unit-01, Rosi's old diesel, has never made. Not a cough, not a purr. A grinding, like teeth. When you open the door, the old diesel turns its head towards you. Its eye is not amber any more. It's red.

zeilen.text: Brother. Unit-01 is looking at us like Mr. Maximum looks at a buffet.
She's never done that. Thirty-one years, two owners, one explosion, and she's never done that.

optionen.text: Steps in and closes the door behind him. “Easy, old girl. Easy.”

zeile.text: Mr. Maximum is right behind you. Quite far behind you.

optionen.text: Pulls the fuel line first, then goes in. “Sorry, old girl.”

zeile.text: She'll forgive you. She's a diesel, and diesels forgive everything.

events.lage: Midnight in the workshop. Unit-01 is lying on the bench like a patient, purring again, amber again. Rosi has her control board open and is holding something up to the lamp with tweezers. Her hands are shaking, and Rosi's hands never shake.

zeilen.text: This isn't ours, and it isn't anybody's on this boat. Somebody soldered it into her, and it's neat work. Better than mine.
It listens, and when it hears the right signal it gives orders. Like the collars on those animals in the harbour. Somebody can make my Unit-01 bite.
Then somebody was on board who shouldn't have been. Mr. Maximum will say nothing. Mr. Maximum is a vault.

optionen.text: Takes the little black module and turns it in the light. There's a stamped code. And a tiny white logo.

zeile.text: I know that logo from somewhere, but I don't know where, and I hate that.

optionen.text: “Can you make it talk? Find out who it was listening to?”

zeile.text: Give me a week and a very large coffee. And don't tell Unit-01 I said she got hacked. She's sensitive.

events.lage: Midnight in the workshop. Without Rosi it's just a room. Maxwell has Unit-01's control board open on the bench and a phone torch in his teeth, following a video tutorial with the volume turned down.

zeilen.text: Mr. Maximum is no engineer. But Mr. Maximum knows what doesn't belong. This doesn't belong.
Rosi would have known in one second. Rosi isn't here.

optionen.text: Takes the little black module. A stamped code. A tiny white logo.
“Rosi should see this. Wherever she is.”

zeile.text: I'll send her a photo. She'll swear. That's how we know she still cares.

events.lage: You sent Megan a photo of the little black module from Unit-01 at three in the morning. At seven she calls back. She has not slept either.

zeilen.text: That logo. A.V. Estates. I sat across a table from them in Monaco a year ago. They wanted to buy the bay for a resort.
A.V. Estates belongs to Alon Varenne. The man behind those collars in the harbour. The man who owns the mountain.
Somebody put his hardware into my generator. On my ship. Find out who, First Officer. Quietly.

optionen.text: “Quietly. Understood.”

zeile.text: And Duc? Lock your cabin. I mean it.

optionen.text: “Quietly is how they got on board in the first place.”

zeile.text: Fair. Then loudly. But carefully loudly.

events.lage: Yamamoto-san is cleaning his long lens on the aft deck. He waves you over and scrolls through his camera with the solemn joy of a man about to show a stranger four hundred pictures of a cormorant.

zeilen.text: Bird photography. Very relaxing. Very… ah. This one is not a bird. Mm.
Thursday night, harbour. The cook… no. The trader. Totò-san. With a man from a dinghy. Big moustache. Gold tooth. They are arguing. Then the moustache goes out to sea. Towards the cliffs.
I am a banker. In my experience, two men arguing at night about a dinghy is always about money.

optionen.text: “Send me that one, please.”

zeile.text: Of course. I send you also the cormorant. As a gift.

optionen.text: “Delete it. Totò's business is Totò's business.”

zeile.text: Deleted. Mm. Loyalty. Also very relaxing.

events.lage: Totò hasn't touched his coffee. That has never happened before. He waits until the mess is empty, then sits down opposite you and puts his phone on the table between you, face up. No new messages.

zeilen.text: My cousin Gennaro, from Bastia, owes money to some people. The wrong people. The worst people.
Thursday he went into the grotto under Punta d'Orsu to fetch a crate for them. Three hours, he said. It's Monday, boss.
I can't go to the police. If I go to the police, they find out what's in my locker. And Gennaro has a little girl. Giulia. Seven years old. Please.

optionen.text: “When's low tide?”

zeile.text: Today. Tomorrow. Every day, twice. I have a boat. I always have a boat.

optionen.text: “You should have told me on Thursday.”

zeile.text: On Thursday I thought he was just drunk somewhere. He's usually just drunk somewhere.

events.lage: Lea and Sophia are sitting on the swim platform with Lea's battered chart book open between them, comparing her grandfather's pencil marks with a nautical chart. Then a shadow, a scream, a rush of wings. Kevin, the fat seagull who steals everything on this boat. And page forty goes up into the sky in his beak.

zeilen.text: NO! No no no no. That's Grandad's page! That's the only one with the cross on it!
He's flying towards the village, to the bell tower. That gull has a nest up there, everybody knows.
Officer. I've never asked you for anything. I'm asking now. Get that bird.

optionen.text: Already pulling off his shoes. “The bell tower. Got it.”

zeile.text: Not now! Low tide, the grotto, Totò's cousin… whenever. Just before Sunday. Please.

optionen.text: “It's a page, Lea. You know it by heart.”

zeile.text: I know it by heart. I don't know HIS HANDWRITING by heart.

events.lage: Sunday evening. Nobody planned it, and everybody came. Lola grills sardines, Maxwell grills Lola's sardines again because Mr. Maximum likes them burnt, Totò plays something sad on a phone speaker. Two weeks ago you were strangers stranded on a broken yacht. Now you're strangers stranded on a broken yacht together.

zeilen.text: To week two! Nobody died, though some people nearly did, and I made a cake shaped like a gull!
Mr. Maximum would like to say thirty words. Fifty. A hundred. It's Sunday.
To my cousin Gennaro. Wherever he is.

optionen.text: Raises his glass to all of it.
Sits next to Totò and doesn't say anything.

events.lage: Past midnight. A knock, three short, one long. Lea is standing in your doorway in a hoodie, hair still wet, the page Kevin stole in one hand and Sophia's tablet in the other. Behind her, over the bay, something small is humming in the dark. A drone. No lights.

zeilen.text: Sophia worked it out. Grandad's cross and the old chart and the sonar. It fits. It all fits.
Forty metres down, off Punta d'Orsu. Grandad's schooner. The one he looked for his whole life.
Do you hear that? That hum? It's been there since you climbed the bell tower after Kevin. I think somebody else knows too.

optionen.text: Pulls her inside and closes the door. “Then we dive first.”

zeile.text: We dive first. Week three. Oh God. I need a bigger tank.

optionen.text: Looks out at the drone. “Then we dive fast. And we tell nobody.”

zeile.text: Nobody. Not even Sophia? …Sophia already knows. Sophia did the maths.

events.lage: Past midnight. A knock. Lea is standing in your doorway with a pencil behind her ear and a sheet of paper covered in rubbed-out lines. Behind her, over the bay, something small is humming in the dark. A drone. No lights.

zeilen.text: Kevin's nest on the bell tower is empty. Grandad's page is gone. Sea, rain, I don't know. So I drew it. From memory.
It's close. It's not Grandad's. I don't know if it's close enough.
And that hum. It's been there since the day Kevin stole the page. I think somebody else is looking too.

optionen.text: “Close is a start. We'll dive anyway.”

zeile.text: Anyway. Okay. Week three. We dive anyway.

optionen.text: “I should have climbed that bell tower for your page. I'm sorry, Lea.”

zeile.text: You had Totò's cousin to save and a grotto full of… stuff. I know. I'm just sad. Let me be sad.

betroffen.was: came to see what the noise is

events.lage: The workshop smells of hot metal. Two long shapes lie on the bench under a sheet. Mr. Maximum has been looking for his mop since last night, and he has checked your cabin twice.

zeilen.text: Number One, Mr. Maximum reports a crime. The old wooden mop is gone. On day two you laughed at it, brother, and it taught you to parry anyway. Now somebody has stolen it in the night.
I stole it. Stop crying and help me with the sheet.

optionen.text: Takes one corner of the sheet.
Takes one corner of the sheet. “That mop hit me in the ear on day two. I won't miss it.”

events.lage: Under the sheet is a long steel pipe with a steel cube on the end, as big as a beer crate. Just under the cube, a thick ring of white bristles sits around the pipe. You know those bristles.

zeilen.text: Those are… eish. Those are the bristles.

You would have cried if I threw them out, so they stay. The block held Unit-01 down for longer than I've been alive, so don't you dare dent it. It's called a Steel Mop, because I couldn't think of anything that would make you happier.

optionen.text: Steps back and gives him room.
“Can anybody even lift that?”

events.lage: He lifts it with both hands. The sleeves of his shirt tear at the shoulders, one and then the other, and everybody hears it.

zeilen.text: That shirt was a uniform. Sleeves: zero. Arms: nine, and I'm not happy about it. The bow tie stays, Mr. Ndlovu, or I call your Gogo.
Mr. Maximum keeps the bow tie. Mr. Maximum is a professional. Parry the dirt, Number One! Only now the dirt has to be very brave.

optionen.text: Looks at the second shape on the bench.
Picks up one torn sleeve and hands it to Chiara.

events.lage: Rosi puts the second shape into Chiara's hands, a short grey rifle with a thick wire coiled under the barrel.

zeilen.text: The other one is yours, Mole. It's a taser rifle. It reaches further than you can throw a napkin swan, and whoever it hits stops moving for a while. Robots don't care, so don't waste it on them.
Balance: eight. Colour: two. Who chose grey?
The capacitor is the best one we had, and that's all I'm going to say about it. Well, Officer? Will they do?

optionen.text: Looks at both of them. “They'll do. Nobody on that beach is ready for him.”

zeile.text: Nobody on this boat is either. Now get out of my workshop.

optionen.text: “And what did you build for me?”

zeile.text: Terremoto, Officer, on the worst day of my life, and you've dented it twice. I'm writing that on the board.

events.lage: Low tide. Totò rows you round the point in a dinghy that smells of diesel and fish. Under the cliff, where the sea has pulled back, there are steps cut into the rock, slippery with weed. They lead down into the dark. Something squeaks in there. A lot of somethings.

zeilen.text: My cousin Gennaro went in on Thursday. He said three hours, in and out. He always says three hours.
I wait here with the boat. When the water reaches the third step, I have to go. Okay? I'm sorry. Bring him out, boss.

optionen.text: Steps off the dinghy onto the weed. “Third step. Got it.”

zeile.text: And boss? Whatever he did, he's not a bad man. He's just Gennaro.

optionen.text: “Not today, Totò.”

zeile.text: Okay. Okay. Tomorrow. The tide comes back tomorrow too.

events.lage: Behind the entrance the grotto opens into a beach the sun has never seen. Grey sand, driftwood, a smell of salt and old smoke. Someone made a fire here not long ago. Then, from a crack in the rock to the left, a woman's voice, very far away and very scared.

zeilen.text: Au secours! Is somebody there? Please! Help!

optionen.text: Follows the voice into the crack.
Gennaro first. Takes the tunnel deeper into the rock.

events.fund: A cheap plastic lighter, half buried in the wet sand, with a sticker of a cartoon pony on it. Next to it, folded small and nearly dry, a child's drawing: a man with a big moustache in a boat, and underneath, in crooked letters, PAPÀ.

events.lage: A tunnel, too straight to be natural. Old iron rings in the walls where lanterns used to hang, a rail for carts, rusted to lace. Something long and patient is lying across the rail, enjoying the last of the warmth.

optionen.text: Steps over the rail very slowly.

events.lage: A hall full of crates. Cigarettes, whisky, a jet ski still in its plastic. And at the back, on its own, a heavy grey crate with a stamped code and a small white logo. You know that crate. You saw it in the hangar in Antibes, the night before all this began. Two men are playing cards on it.

optionen.text: Walks up to the card game. “Deal me in.”
Waits in the dark until one of them goes for a piss.

events.lage: A pool, black and perfectly still. Then it isn't. A boy surfaces in a torn wetsuit, a net bag full of packages on his belt. He sees you and nearly goes under again. He can't be more than nineteen. Somewhere under the rock, very faint, something is humming.

zeilen.text: You're not one of them. They don't come down here, they're scared of the water.
I'm Matteu. Pinelli, from the village. I dive for them. They pay. And…
My brother Ghjacumu drowned down here last year. They said if I dive for them long enough, they'll tell me where. So I can bring him home to our mother.

optionen.text: “Show me where you've already looked.”

zeile.text: There's a gallery behind the pool. They told me never to go there. That's why I think it's there.

optionen.text: “I'm looking for a man called Gennaro. Where do they keep people?”

zeile.text: Past the torches. Be careful. The old man is coming back with the tide. He always does.

events.lage: Torches in iron rings, freshly lit. Somebody is expecting company. A man with a torch in one hand and a cutlass in the other steps out of a niche and grins with three teeth.

optionen.text: Grins back with all of his.

events.lage: A dry cave above the waterline. A man with a gold tooth and a big moustache is chained to a ring bolt by one ankle. He has a black eye and a split lip, and when he sees you he starts talking before you've said a word.

zeilen.text: Who are you? No. Wait. Totò sent you. Of course he did. Totò sends people. Holy Mother.
It's not my crate. Okay? I only carry. Three nights, a thousand euros, no questions. Then the old man in Bastia says the debt has doubled. Doubled!
Here. They didn't find this. My grandfather's. He fished out of Bastia for fifty years with it, and nobody ever heard him coming. They called it Sussurro. The whisper.
It whispered me out of worse places than this. Take it. You'll need it more than me, when he comes.

optionen.text: Takes the knife. Weighs it. Cuts the rope that holds the chain. “Let's go home.”

zeile.text: Not yet. Listen. Do you hear the water? That's him. He comes with the tide.

events.fund: Scratched into the rock beside the ring bolt: a row of little lines, and a name, GIULIA. His daughter. He counted the tides for her.

events.lage: A dry cave above the waterline. A man with a gold tooth and a big moustache is chained to a ring bolt by one ankle. He is sitting very still with his hands in his lap. They are swollen and blue. Someone has taken his fingers one at a time, and taken his time.

zeilen.text: Totò sent you. Of course. You're late, my friend. Only a little. An hour.
He asked me for the money, very politely, and every time I said I don't have it, he took a finger. Very politely.
My grandfather's knife. They didn't find it. Sussurro, the whisper. Take it out of my boot. I can't close my hand around it anymore.

optionen.text: Takes the knife from his boot. Says nothing. Cuts the rope.

zeile.text: Don't tell Totò about the hands. Not yet. Listen. That's him. He comes with the tide.

events.lage: The water comes in over the sand without a sound. With it comes a boat, and in the boat sits an old man in a linen suit gone yellow at the cuffs, peeling an orange. Two men with torches stand behind him. He steps out onto the rock as if onto a carpet.

zeilen.text: Sit down, signore. I'm in no hurry. The tide is always in a hurry. I never am.
That man owes me money. And that knife in your hand is his, so it is mine. Shall we talk like civilised people?

optionen.text: “I'm not here to talk.” Steps between him and Gennaro.

zeile.text: Pity. Nobody wants to talk any more. Everybody wants to bleed.

events.lage: The water comes in over the sand without a sound. With it comes a boat, and in the boat sits an old man in a linen suit gone yellow at the cuffs, peeling an orange. Two men with torches stand behind him. He steps out onto the rock as if onto a carpet.

zeilen.text: Sit down, signore. I'm in no hurry. The tide is always in a hurry. I never am.
That man owes me money. And that knife in your hand is his, so it is mine. Shall we talk like civilised people?

optionen.text: “I'm not here to talk.” Steps between him and Gennaro.

zeile.text: Pity. Nobody wants to talk any more. Everybody wants to bleed.

events.lage: The water comes in over the sand without a sound. With it comes a boat, and in the boat sits an old man in a linen suit gone yellow at the cuffs, peeling an orange. Two men with torches stand behind him. He steps out onto the rock as if onto a carpet. Before he can say another word, Matteu comes out of the pool behind him, Ghjacumu's medal round his neck and a diving knife in his fist.

zeilen.text: You locked him in! Eighteen days! He scratched the days into the wall!
Ah. The little brother. I told your brother too: the sea keeps what it's given.

optionen.text: Goes for the old man before the torches reach the boy.

zeile.text: For Ghjacumu…

events.lage: The water comes in over the sand without a sound. With it comes a boat, and in the boat sits an old man in a linen suit gone yellow at the cuffs, peeling an orange. Two men with torches stand behind him. He steps out onto the rock as if onto a carpet. Before he can say another word, Matteu comes out of the pool behind him, Ghjacumu's medal round his neck and a diving knife in his fist.

zeilen.text: You locked him in! Eighteen days! He scratched the days into the wall!
Ah. The little brother. I told your brother too: the sea keeps what it's given.

optionen.text: Goes for the old man before the torches reach the boy.

zeile.text: For Ghjacumu…

events.lage: The old man sits against a crate with his hands in his lap, breathing through his nose. His men are gone. The water is at your ankles. Gennaro limps to the grey crate and puts his hand on it like on an animal.

zeilen.text: Take the crate to my boat, and Gennaro's debt is paid. All of it. My word. I am many things, but I keep my word.
Forty collars, a box of chips. The same ones they put on the dogs in the harbour. On the goat.
If you take it, you can show the world what Alon Varenne does. And I… I go on owing the old man. Forever. You decide. I already decided enough stupid things this year.

optionen.text: Pushes the crate into the old man's boat. “His debt is paid. Then we're done.”

zeile.text: Done. You are an honest man, signore. That is rarer than you think, and more expensive.

optionen.text: Puts his hand on the crate. “This goes with me. It's proof.”

zeile.text: Proof. How nice. Proof keeps nobody warm, signore. Ask Gennaro in a week.

events.lage: The old man's boat slides out with the tide, the crate in the bow like a coffin. Gennaro watches it go. Then he sits down in the water and laughs until he cries, or the other way round.

zeilen.text: Free. I'm free. Giulia. I can go home to Giulia.
Forty collars, though. Forty dogs. Forty goats. Somewhere. I'll think about that tomorrow. Today I just want to breathe.

optionen.text: Helps him up. “Come on. Totò's waiting at the third step.”

events.lage: The old man's boat slides out with the tide, empty. He doesn't look back. He doesn't need to. Gennaro stares at the crate between your feet as if it were a bomb.

zeilen.text: You did the right thing. You did. For the dogs, for the goats, for everybody.
Only… the old man doesn't forget. He'll come to Bastia. Giulia's school is in Bastia.

optionen.text: Lifts the crate. It's heavier than it looks. “We'll keep you safe.”

zeile.text: You'll keep me safe. Sure. Like you kept the boat safe.

events.lage: The water is lapping at the third step. Totò is standing up in the dinghy, waving both arms. When he sees Gennaro, he stops waving and just stands there.

zeilen.text: Gennà. You stupid, stupid… Come here.
Boss. I don't know what to say. Me, Totò, I don't know what to say. Thank you.

optionen.text: Climbs into the dinghy. Lets the two of them hug it out.

events.lage: On the way back you pass the crack in the rock. You said you'd come back. You came back. The passage is full of black water now, up to the roof. Bastien was under those stones. Chloé is sitting on a rock above the waterline, quite still, a velvet box in her hands.

zeilen.text: He was talking until the end. About Marseille. About a restaurant by the old port.
Here. He was going to give it to me when we found the strongbox. Give it to someone who gets the chance.

optionen.text: Takes the box. Stays with her a moment. Then takes her with him to the boat.

zeile.text: Don't. Don't say sorry. You chose your friend. I would have chosen mine.

events.lage: Behind the pool a gallery runs down into the rock, half flooded. Matteu swims ahead with a dive lamp. On a ledge above the water something thick and dark uncoils, slowly, the way only things that have never been afraid uncoil.

zeilen.text: There. On the ledge. Don't let it get between us and the air.

optionen.text: Puts himself between the boy and the ledge.

events.lage: A dome of rock with air in it, and a shelf just above the high-water mark. Matteu pulls himself up next to you, shivering. Then he holds the lamp to the wall and stops shivering.

zeilen.text: Lines. Somebody counted. That's… that's how Ghjacumu counted. Fives, with a line through. He did it on the wall of our room, for the days until the summer.
He was here. He was alive here.

optionen.text: Puts a hand on his shoulder. “Let's see where this goes.”

events.fund: Tally marks on the wall of the air pocket, scratched with a knife. Seven groups of five, and two more. Thirty-seven tides. Somebody lived down here for eighteen days.

events.lage: At the end of the air pocket a narrow passage leads back towards the smugglers' tunnel. It is closed by an iron grate, and the grate is padlocked. From your side there is no keyhole. The lock is on the other side, where the smugglers walk. Rats come out of the dark when the lamp swings round.

optionen.text: Kicks the rats back into the dark.

events.lage: Matteu is still at the tally marks with the lamp. He hasn't seen the grate. You have. Behind the bars, on the other side, is a little green string with a tin medal on it, chewed through. Somebody pushed his hand through these bars for a long time. Somebody else locked them, and came back with the tide, and didn't open them.

zeilen.text: What's there? What do you see? Is it him?

optionen.text: Tells him the truth. “Someone locked him in, Matteu. From the outside.”

zeile.text: …The old man. He always comes with the tide. He comes with the tide.

optionen.text: Lies. “Just rats. He drowned, Matteu. It was quick. He didn't suffer.”

zeile.text: Quick. Okay. Okay. Thank you. That's… I can tell my mother that.

events.lage: The crack opens into a passage where the roof has come down. Under the rubble a man is lying on his back, pale and grinning with pain, one leg buried to the hip. A woman is kneeling next to him, pulling at the stones with bleeding fingers. Behind her, two men are going through a rucksack. They look up.

zeilen.text: Thank God! These two came with the tide, they took our lamps, our water…

optionen.text: “Put the bag down, gentlemen.”

events.lage: Their camp is a ledge with two sleeping bags, a winch, a laptop wrapped in cling film and a wall of photos: an old schooner, a strongbox, a map of the bay with a red circle. On the laptop there's a sticker: a small white logo you have seen before.

zeilen.text: Chloé. Chloé Marchal. That's Bastien under the rocks. We're looking for a strongbox, from a schooner that went down in 1924.
Yes, A.V. Estates pays for the expedition. Yes, we report every find to them. Everybody needs money, okay? Treasure hunting doesn't feed anyone.
The winch. With the winch we can lift the stone. But the tide… in twenty minutes the passage is under water.

optionen.text: Shoulders the winch. “Show me.”

events.fund: A little velvet box at the bottom of Bastien's rucksack, under the spare batteries. Inside, a ring with a tiny blue stone. The receipt is still in the box. He bought it in Marseille in March.

events.lage: Back at the rubble the water is already round Bastien's shoulders. Freeing him will take every minute the tide has left. Somewhere deeper in the rock Totò's cousin is waiting, and so is a man who comes with the tide.

zeilen.text: Please. I'll give you everything. Our notes, the map, the circle on the map. Everything.
Please don't leave him here.

optionen.text: Sets the winch against the stone and starts cranking.

zeile.text: Thank you. Thank you, thank you…

optionen.text: “I'll come back for him. I promise.” Goes for Gennaro.

zeile.text: You'll come back. Yes. Of course. Go. GO!

events.lage: The stone comes up a finger's width, then a hand. Bastien screams, and then he is out, and Chloé is holding his head above the water. His leg is bent in the wrong place. He's laughing anyway. It's taken almost an hour. The tide hasn't waited for anybody.

zeilen.text: Here. Our notes. The circle on the map. Take them, give them to whoever you want. Just not to A.V. Estates. Never again.

optionen.text: Takes the notes, and goes deeper, fast.

events.lage: Low tide again. Totò doesn't come with you this time. The steps are as slippery as before, and the rats have forgotten you already.

optionen.text: Goes down to the hall of crates and hunts for leftovers.
Sits on the drowned beach for a while.

events.lage: The fire pit is cold. The sea breathes in and out at the mouth of the grotto.

optionen.text: Goes back up before the third step.

events.lage: The village from above: terracotta roofs, washing lines, TV aerials. On the highest roof, by the bell tower, a big white gull is standing on one leg with a page of paper in its beak, looking at you the way a cat looks at a dog behind a fence.

zeilen.text: That's him. That's Kevin. That's Grandad's page. That's forty years of Grandad.
I'll take the left. You take the… oh, there are pigeons. Of course there are pigeons.

optionen.text: Climbs out of Alva's attic window onto the roof.

events.lage: Up the drainpipe, over the gutter, onto the bell tower. Kevin is waiting at the top on a nest made of fishing line, chip papers and, apparently, everything this crew has lost in two weeks. He drops the page into the nest, spreads his wings and screams.

zeilen.text: Don't hurt him! Just… hurt him a little.

optionen.text: Spreads his arms too and screams back.

events.lage: Kevin sulks on the weathervane. The nest is a museum: Totò's lighter, Megan's fountain pen, Holm's spare sunglasses, a fork from the galley, a sock nobody will ever claim. And, a little wet, page forty.

zeilen.text: Grandad's handwriting. The bay, the cross. 1924. It's all still there.
You climbed a bell tower for me. Nobody's ever climbed anything for me. Ever.

optionen.text: Gives her the page, and keeps Megan's pen for himself.

zeile.text: You're keeping Megan's pen. I didn't see that. I saw nothing.

optionen.text: Gives her the page, and puts everything else back. “He collected it fair and square.”

zeile.text: You're the only person on this island who respects that gull. That's weird. I like it.

events.lage: Getting down is harder than getting up. It always is. Kevin watches you go with one eye, already planning the next theft.

optionen.text: Climbs back in through Alva's window.

events.lage: Night, and the tide is in. Totò wouldn't bring you, so you rowed yourself and tied the dinghy to an iron ring in the cliff. The water stands well over the third step now. Everything that lives down here has climbed up to where you are.

optionen.text: Climbs out onto the wet rock.
Unties the dinghy again. Not tonight.

events.lage: The rail is under water. You wade along it up to your knees, torch in your teeth. Then you notice the ceiling. It isn't rock. It's moving, very slightly, and all of it at once.

optionen.text: Keeps very still, and keeps walking.

events.lage: The gallery behind the black pool is a canal now. You have to swim the last stretch, holding the torch high. Something long brushes past your leg, turns, and comes back to have another look.

optionen.text: Swims faster.

events.lage: The high tide floats a boat right into the hall. Men with head torches are unloading new grey crates, each with the same small white logo. So that's what high tide is for. One of them turns around.

optionen.text: Steps into the light before he can shout.
Gets a look into an open crate first.

events.lage: Moonlight falls through a crack in the roof and lies on the black pool like a coin. The humming you heard at low tide the first time is louder now. It has words in it. Then a woman draws herself up onto the rock at the water's edge, wet honey-blonde hair clinging to her like weed, a long fish tail sliding out of the pool behind her. She looks at you as if she has been waiting.

zeilen.text: Well now. A man who comes down at high tide, on purpose. Either very brave, or very lost.
Most of them run when they hear me. The rest of them stay. Forever, mind. Which are you, sailor?

optionen.text: Puts the weapon away. “Neither. I came to talk.”

zeile.text: Talk? Go on, then. Make it good. I've heard every word the sea ever drowned.

optionen.text: Backs away, very slowly.

zeile.text: Another night, then. I'm not going anywhere. I never do.

events.lage: She rests her arms on the edge of the pool like a girl on a windowsill. When she speaks again, the song has gone out of her voice, and she just sounds old.

zeilen.text: There's a boat at the bottom of the bay. An old sailing ship. She went down in a storm a hundred years ago, and I sang her crew to sleep. That's what I do.
But she's not resting. Men come with lamps and machines now. They want something she's carrying. And there's a blade down there that was never meant for them.
Here. This fell off her when she sank. It's been waiting for its blade ever since. You'll find it. And when you dive, I'll be close. Don't go the way the lamps go.

optionen.text: Takes the stone. It is warm, which makes no sense at all.

zeile.text: Go on, sailor. The tide doesn't wait for anybody. Not even for me.

events.lage: The pool is black and still. No one rises out of it. Only once, very far away, under the rock, someone hums two notes, as if to say: I know you're there.

optionen.text: Sits a while. Then goes back.

events.lage: The dinghy is still there, knocking against the rock. The moon is out over the point. Behind you the grotto breathes in and out with the sea.

optionen.text: Rows home.

events.lage: Totò calls from the harbour. You can hear gulls and his breathing. He doesn't say hello.

zeilen.text: The coast guard found Gennaro's boat this morning. Off Cap Corse. Empty. The engine was still warm.
Giulia's mother called me. She asks where her husband is. What do I tell her, boss? That there's a crate in the tender garage, and it's proof?

optionen.text: “I'm sorry, Totò. I'm so sorry.”

zeile.text: Yeah. Me too. I'll be at work tomorrow. Don't talk to me for a few days.

optionen.text: “We'll make it count. I promise you, that crate will bring Alon down.”

versprechen.text: Make the crate count against Alon

zeile.text: Make it count. Okay. Do that. Then at least it was worth something.

events.lage: Alva calls from behind the bar. Music, laughter, glasses. She has to shout a little.

zeilen.text: Your little diver from the grotto is here. Matteu Pinelli. New watch, new wetsuit, buying everyone a round.
He says the men from Bastia are like family now. That the old man came to his mother's house with flowers for the dead brother. Isn't that sweet? Why do I want to throw up?

optionen.text: Says nothing. Hangs up after a while.
“Tell him to go home, Alva. Please.”

zeile.text: I did. He laughed. He said he's never been happier.

events.lage: A photo from Chiara: a little grey-blue plush dolphin with a navy ribbon, sitting on your folded jacket.

zeilen.text: found it in my locker. had it since my first season. it's been to every port i ever worked 🐬
it's yours now. don't make it a big thing. it's a dolphin, not a ring

optionen.text: Hangs it on the jacket straight away.

zeile.text: you hung it up already?? …okay. it looks good there. shut up 😤

optionen.text: “I'll take good care of it, Chief.”

zeile.text: you'd better. it has more sea miles than you ⚓

events.lage: A photo from Chiara: a little grey-blue plush dolphin with a navy ribbon, sitting on your folded jacket.

zeilen.text: found it in my locker. had it since my first season. it's been to every port i ever worked 🐬

events.lage: A green bottle knocks against the swim platform. Inside is a strip of wet paper in a slanting old hand. You read it, and somehow you hear it.

zeilen.text: Sailor. The girl's box has stopped giving pictures. It clicks and gives me nothing, and I've shaken it, and I've asked it nicely.
I'd ask her, but she says nobody is to know about me, and I've been very good about it. Bring what it eats. Leave it on the third step at dusk.

optionen.text: Asks Lea for a spare film pack without saying why. “It's for a friend.”

zeile.text: It eats squares! It gave me the moon, sailor, and the moon looks like a thumbprint. Bring more whenever you like.

zeile_fehlschlag.text: You've brought me squares for some other box. They don't fit. I gave them to the crabs.

optionen.text: Buys film in the village and seals it in a jar with candle wax. “Waterproof enough.”

zeile.text: Wax and a jar. That's how my sailors kept their tobacco dry. It works, and it smells of the church.

zeile_fehlschlag.text: The jar leaked, sailor. Now I have a box of wet squares and one very clean crab.

optionen.text: Leaves the bottle where it is. “Not my problem.”

zeile.text: Then I'll go on shaking it. I have plenty of time, you know.

events.lage: Another bottle, this one smelling of diesel. The paper has been folded very small.

zeilen.text: There's a net on the old mooring past the point. Nobody fishes it, sailor. It just goes on catching, and it has had three turtles from me this week.
I can't cut it. Your steel doesn't like me, and I don't like your steel. You could do it, in daylight, while I'm away.

optionen.text: Dives on it with a knife at slack water. “Twenty seconds, tops.”

zeile.text: The turtles came back this morning, and they were very rude about it. I've taken their picture.

zeile_fehlschlag.text: You cut half of it, and half a net still drowns things. But you went down, sailor. I saw you.

optionen.text: Tells Petru where it is and lets him think it was his idea. “Someone ought to.”

zeile.text: The old man came out in his boat and swore at it for an hour. It was a lovely sound, and the net is gone.

zeile_fehlschlag.text: He says that net was his grandfather's and it can stay where it is. Men and their nets.

optionen.text: Puts the bottle in the recycling. “Tell a fisherman.”

zeile.text: I did tell one, sailor. Some time ago. He's still asleep.

events.lage: The third bottle has the camera's strap tied round its neck, and a very small square of film.

zeilen.text: I've listened to your village bell for longer than I'd like to say, and I've never seen what's ringing it. The hill is a long way up for me.
Would you take a picture of it? From the top, with the sea behind. I'd like to know how it looks from up there, looking down at me.

optionen.text: Climbs the bell tower at dawn with the square in his pocket. “Hold still, bell.”

zeile.text: So that's it. It's so small, sailor. All those years, and it's no bigger than a boy.

zeile_fehlschlag.text: You sent me your thumb. It's a very nice thumb, and behind it there's a bit of bell.

optionen.text: Asks Nonna Fiora for the key to the tower. “It's for someone who can't come up.”

zeile.text: She held it up to the window for you, didn't she? I can see her thumb. Tell her it's a good bell.

zeile_fehlschlag.text: She asked who it was for, and now she has lit a candle for me. No picture, though. How very like her.

optionen.text: Leaves the square on the rail for the gulls. “Some other time.”

zeile.text: Yes. There's always some other time. I'm the one who'd know.

events.titel: For the Girl with the Box
events.lage: One last bottle. Inside are two Polaroids, curled from the damp, each with a line in the same slanting hand. You take them down to the pool at dusk.

zeilen.text: Now you've seen where I sleep, sailor, and that makes two of you. Show the girl. Tell her six metres is very shallow.

optionen.text: Holds up the second one. “The same octopus?”

zeile.text: A different one. The first one talks too much.

optionen.text: Looks at the first one for a long time.

zeile.text: Don't stare, sailor. It's only the light.

events.lage: A water taxi from Ajaccio bumps against the hull. Marit Holm comes up the gangway slowly, one hand on the rail and the other pressed against her side. The crew comes out one by one, and nobody knows whether to salute her or hug her. Then someone hugs her, and she lets it happen. That's new. She counts heads, and you can see her lips move.

zeilen.text: Megan called me every evening. She reads your reports out loud, like a charge sheet. So I know what you have been doing, Frankfurt.

You took a deserter out by sea, and it cost you Petru. I'd fix that before the twenty-first.

The mountains you have left alone so far, and they won't stay quiet for you.
