optionen.text: Touches one of the stars on her sleeve and goes to work.

events.lage: There's a plate at your place, with a cheese toastie on it, and it isn't burnt. Last night in the galley you stayed with Lola until the pan was cold. She is very busy with something on the other side of the room, and she's whistling badly.

zeilen.text: Don't tell anyone I told you, Boss, but someone on this boat got the good one. No idea who. Mostly the cheese.

optionen.text: Eats every bit of it.

zeile.text: You legend. Right, heaps to do. Get out of my galley, and come back in one piece.

optionen.text: “Sunday. We'll find you a signal, for Nan.”

zeile.text: …Yeah. Yeah, you'd better, or she'll send a boat. Ta, mate.

events.lage: Alva is on the quay with a coffee for you, and she takes the money for it. Last night she danced for you out here in the dark, once, and told you that you were never there. She counts your change very carefully.

zeilen.text: You look tired, o figliolu. I can't think why. That's one euro fifty, and I'm writing down the rest. Do you want to know what you owe me?

optionen.text: “Tell me when this is over.”

zeile.text: That's what they all say. Mind you come and pay it. Alva remembers.

optionen.text: Drinks the coffee and says nothing about any dancing.

zeile.text: Good. What dancing?

events.lage: Bibi found the marks by the road this morning. A dog has been sleeping under the same bush for a week, and it has gone for everyone who stopped. Now it stands in the middle of the road, ribs showing, teeth showing. A small steel box is bolted to its old collar, and the light on it never stops.

zeilen.text: That box is ARK's. They took strays, because nobody asks about strays. It keeps firing, and it drives them out of their heads. So tire it out, then throw Rosi's grenade. And when it's nearly down, stop hitting it. Please.

optionen.text: Gets ready, and hates it.
Turns back. “Not today.”

events.lage: The road is empty. There's a little blood on it, and Bibi looks at that for a while.

zeilen.text: It'll be back at the bush tomorrow, or the day after. It's got nowhere else. Next time stop one hit sooner, okay?

optionen.text: Walks back with her.

events.lage: Bibi has marked a new place on her map. It's another Biscuit, she says, with the same red light on its neck, and this one has nobody yet.

zeilen.text: That one's got the same nose, nearly. Tire it out, then the grenade, and don't tell Biscuit.

optionen.text: Gets ready, and hates it.
Turns back. “Not today.”

events.lage: You can hear it from the top of the gorge. It sounds like someone laughing at a joke they don't understand, over and over. Bibi has gone very quiet.

zeilen.text: That's one of mine. Seven one one four. Every time the collar fires, she laughs. It has been firing for three weeks. I know how that sounds. Tire her out, then the grenade. I can't do this part. I'm sorry.

optionen.text: Walks down into the gorge, and says nothing funny.
Turns back. “Not today.”

events.lage: The laughing comes down from somewhere above you. Then it stops, and that's worse.

zeilen.text: I know that place she's in. You can't chase someone out of it. We come back, and we're boring, and we come back again.

optionen.text: Walks back with her.

events.lage: Bibi has marked a new place on her map. It's another Sorry, she says, with the same red light on its neck, and this one has nobody yet.

zeilen.text: There's a second one. Nobody's told this one it's funny yet. You know how this goes.

optionen.text: Walks down into the gorge, and says nothing funny.
Turns back. “Not today.”

events.lage: Black trunks and ash. You've met her before, and you still have the bruise. She stands on the burnt road with the steel plates bolted to her shoulders and the collar blinking under them, and she hits whatever comes near.

zeilen.text: Eleven months I fed her. I thought the plates were for a broken shoulder, and they told me it was a brace. Nobody could make her do anything, so they gave her the collar, and they bolted it on while she was asleep. Now we have to put her to sleep too. I know.

optionen.text: Walks straight towards her and doesn't look away.
Turns back. “Not today.”

events.lage: She walks away through the trunks at her own speed. Nothing on this island has ever made her hurry.

zeilen.text: Yeah, that's her. She'll be back on this road tomorrow, and the collar will still be on. Stop one hit sooner, okay?

optionen.text: Walks back with her.

events.lage: Three of Petru's spanners have gone missing, and one came back clean. Bibi has followed a line of very small, very careful footprints to the foot of the cliff. A stone drops next to you. It isn't an accident. Then the collar blinks up there, and something starts screaming.

zeilen.text: He solved the feeding puzzle in a week, and it took me two to notice. For a minute he's the cleverest one here. Then the collar fires, and he isn't anybody. He'll watch the grenade all the way, so wear him out first.

optionen.text: Puts down your lunch and gets ready.
Turns back. “Not today.”

events.lage: He's up on the cliff again. He holds up one of Petru's spanners, so you can see it. Then the collar blinks, and he drops it, and he's gone.

zeilen.text: He'll be back. He always comes back for the tools. Next time stop one hit sooner, okay? He's got nothing left by then.

optionen.text: Walks back with her.

events.lage: Bibi has marked a new place on her map. It's another Monsieur, she says, with the same red light on its neck, and this one has nobody yet.

zeilen.text: This one's watching how you hold the grenade. Wear him out before he learns it.

optionen.text: Puts down your lunch and gets ready.
Turns back. “Not today.”

events.lage: High grass and a lot of wind. The wolf stands by herself at the far end of the pasture, with a collar blinking on her neck. The others you fought on this mountain ran as a pack. Nothing runs with this one. The collar has seen to that.

zeilen.text: I won't lie to you, this one could really kill you. The collar pulls hardest on the strong ones, and she's the strongest I ever had. She'll shake off that grenade until she can hardly stand. So wait for it.

optionen.text: Walks out into the open grass, alone, and stops.
Turns back. “Not today.”

events.lage: Nothing on the pasture now but the wind. Bibi picks up a clump of grey fur and puts it in her pocket.

zeilen.text: She'll let us try again. She's the only one of them who's fair. Next time stop one hit sooner, okay? Just one.

optionen.text: Walks back with her.

events.lage: The shepherds up here say a cat has been killing their dogs. You don't believe them, until you see it on the roof of the hut. It's grey and round and it doesn't look like much. Then the collar blinks, and it screams at you.

zeilen.text: That's Madame. She lived on Julien's desk. He called all of them subjects, but not her. He put the collar on her himself, in front of us, to show it was safe. So. Tire her out, then the grenade. Mind the hands.

optionen.text: Takes a step back, then remembers that it's a cat.
Turns back. “Not today.”

events.lage: Something moves around under the floor of the hut, and then it stops. Bibi leaves a saucer by the door.

zeilen.text: She'll come back for the saucer. She's got standards.

optionen.text: Walks back with her.

events.lage: There's something red in the top of a chestnut tree, and it's making a noise like a very small, very angry door. Bibi stares up at it. You've seen many things on this island, but you haven't seen this.

zeilen.text: He came in a crate, with a ribbon on it. There were rich people who sent us animals as gifts. The collar is too big for him, so they used tape. He can't reach it, and he's been up there for days, and he won't stop.

optionen.text: Shakes the tree. Feels bad about it right away.
Turns back. “Not today.”

events.lage: A flash of red, far off between the trees. Then there's only the noise, and then not even that.

zeilen.text: He'll get tired before we do. He's got tiny legs.

optionen.text: Walks back with her.

events.lage: Something big has been going through the fences along the creek. It looks like a huge wet guinea pig. It doesn't look angry. It looks as if it has no idea why its body keeps doing this, and the collar on its neck blinks and blinks.

zeilen.text: You know what they're famous for? Nothing bothers them. Birds sit on them. That's why ARK wanted one. They wanted to see how long it would take. It took four days. I timed it. I wrote it down.

optionen.text: Wades into the creek. It's colder than it looks.
Turns back. “Not today.”

events.lage: The fence is down again, further along. There's a wet track up the bank. Bibi looks at it and doesn't say anything for a bit.

zeilen.text: He doesn't even want to fight. That's the worst part.

optionen.text: Walks back with her.

events.lage: Bibi has marked a new place on her map. It's another Monday, she says, with the same red light on its neck, and this one has nobody yet.

zeilen.text: Another one. Birds on him and everything. It took them four days with him too. Be nice.

optionen.text: Wades into the creek. It's colder than it looks.
Turns back. “Not today.”

events.lage: You've fought one of these on the monastery bridge. This one is bigger, and it has rooted up half the ravine. It keeps slamming its head against the rocks, on the side where the collar sits.

zeilen.text: That's a local one. ARK wanted animals from the island for the field tests, so if anyone found one, nobody would ask. The one on your bridge was his sister, I think. Bring the grenade, and don't stand in front of him.

optionen.text: Stands in front of him anyway. There's nowhere else to stand.
Turns back. “Not today.”

events.lage: The whole ravine is torn up, and the sound of it is going away. Bibi kicks a stone back into its hole, for no reason.

zeilen.text: He'll be back. They don't leave their ground.

optionen.text: Walks back with her.

events.lage: Bibi has marked a new place on her map. It's another Truffle, she says, with the same red light on its neck, and this one has nobody yet.

zeilen.text: That's his other sister. There are a lot of them, and they all hate you. Same plan.

optionen.text: Stands in front of him anyway. There's nowhere else to stand.
Turns back. “Not today.”

events.lage: You've heard this squeal before, up in the alders on the mountain. It's Old Grey's smallest, the fat clumsy one, and it has come all the way down here alone. The red light on its neck is still blinking, and it's hitting the air with its paws.

zeilen.text: They only made the collar in one size. You saw what that did to the mother. It's going to grow into the neck, and then I can't take it off. So it has to be now. I know it's a baby. Don't hit it hard. Just... you know how little it takes.

optionen.text: Crouches down. “Come on, then. You and me.”
Turns back. “Not today.”

events.lage: The alders are moving, and then they aren't. Bibi stays there for a long time, calling something quietly.

zeilen.text: It'll stay near. It doesn't know where else to go. Next time, please, just one hit less.

optionen.text: Walks back with her.

events.lage: Bibi has marked a new place on her map. It's another Pudding, she says, with the same red light on its neck, and this one has nobody yet.

zeilen.text: It's the other little one. It's so light, so please, only the smallest hits you've got.

optionen.text: Crouches down. “Come on, then. You and me.”
Turns back. “Not today.”

events.lage: A very old tortoise is standing in the middle of the path, with a 12 painted on its shell. Its neck is stretched out, its mouth is open, and it is coming at you. It's coming very slowly. You have time to take this in.

zeilen.text: Twelve of forty. It was a battery test: how long does a collar last, on something that lives this long? Nobody expected the battery to go first. The others... I don't know. She's still looking for them, I think. Don't laugh. She bites like a door.

optionen.text: Tries not to laugh, and stays out of reach.
Turns back. “Not today.”

events.lage: The path is empty. You don't understand how. You only looked away for a moment.

zeilen.text: Yes, I know. Don't look at me. She'll be a little further on tomorrow. Stop one hit sooner, okay?

optionen.text: Walks back with her.

events.lage: Bibi has marked a new place on her map. It's another Twelve, she says, with the same red light on its neck, and this one has nobody yet.

zeilen.text: That's Nineteen! She found one! Slowly, please. They've got all day.

optionen.text: Tries not to laugh, and stays out of reach.
Turns back. “Not today.”

events.lage: Something huge is circling in the fog above the ridge, and there's a small red light going round with it. A bone drops out of the sky and breaks on the rocks next to you. Then the shape folds its wings.

zeilen.text: He's a wild one. He only came over the fence because of the food bins. They needed a bird for the range test, so they kept him. He can't land for long. Every time he does, it fires, and up he goes. When he comes down at you, that's your chance.

optionen.text: Looks up, and keeps looking up.
Turns back. “Not today.”

events.lage: Only fog now, and the small red light going away in it. Then not even that.

zeilen.text: He'll be back over the ridge. He can't help it.

optionen.text: Walks back with her.

events.lage: Bibi has marked a new place on her map. It's another Bones, she says, with the same red light on its neck, and this one has nobody yet.

zeilen.text: That's his friend, and it's stolen my lunch. Wait until it lands, then the grenade.

optionen.text: Looks up, and keeps looking up.
Turns back. “Not today.”

events.lage: For three days Bibi has found nothing but prints, on walls, on roofs, and on your boat once. Now she's found a dead goat high on a rock, and she has gone pale. You look up. There's nothing there. You look up again.

zeilen.text: From somebody's private zoo. She cost more than this whole bay. She lived in a cage the size of your cabin, and now she's got a mountain and that thing on her neck. You won't see her come. She fights the grenade like nothing else. So wait.

optionen.text: Puts his back against the rock.
Turns back. “Not today.”

events.lage: There's a print on the rock, and it's still wet. It's higher than your head. You don't remember her leaving.

zeilen.text: She let you live. Don't feel too good about it.

optionen.text: Walks back with her.

events.lage: A long grey shape lies on the warm stones of the gorge, and two of the village's goats are lying near it, not moving. It lifts its flat head and looks at you. It doesn't get up. It has plenty of time. The collar blinks slowly, and it looks like it belongs there.

zeilen.text: A rich man's collection. It came with a certificate. Charly named him back at the lab, because he's cold, he's never in a hurry, and he lies on everything he owns. Mr. V. Don't tell anyone I laughed. One bite is enough, so don't let him start the clock.

optionen.text: Walks down into the gorge. He watches you all the way.
Turns back. “Not today.”

events.lage: He has gone. You don't know when. There's a long smooth track in the dust, going away, and he wasn't hurrying at all.

zeilen.text: He doesn't mind. He's got all the time in the world, and he knows it.

optionen.text: Walks back with her.

events.lage: Bibi has marked a new place on her map. It's another Mr. V., she says, with the same red light on its neck, and this one has nobody yet.

zeilen.text: I didn't know there were two. Charly's going to want a name for this. Don't let it start the clock.

optionen.text: Walks down into the gorge. He watches you all the way.
Turns back. “Not today.”

events.lage: Bibi stops you on the quay and holds out a shoebox. Rosi stands behind her, wiping her hands on a rag. In the box are small grey grenades with blue tape around them.

zeilen.text: The collars make them crazy. You've seen it. I can't get near them to cut one off. So I asked Rosi for something that doesn't kill them.
It's a vet's sedative in a soft shell. The collar fights it. As long as the animal has strength, the collar wins. Under one in ten, it can't. Above that, you're just making it wet.
So you have to fight them first. I know. I hate it too. And when one is nearly down, stop hitting it, or it runs, and we start again.

optionen.text: Takes the box.
“Does it hurt them?”

zeile.text: Less than the collar does. Now take the box. I have an engine in pieces.

events.lage: Bibi puts a shoebox on the quay in front of Elsa and takes off the lid. Inside there are steel collars, cut open, each with a lab number. Elsa looks into the box for a long time without touching it.

zeilen.text: Every number in there was an animal. I can tell you what each of them weighs. I fed them. I signed for them.
A statement can be called a lie, Miss Bibi. A number on a steel collar is much harder to call a lie. Who else has seen these?

optionen.text: “Only us.”
“Keep them away from the town hall.”

zeile.text: I didn't ask for advice, First Officer. ...I have a safe at home. It's a very old safe.

events.lage: Two men from the commission in Ajaccio have set up a folding table on the quay, with a clerk and a lot of paper. They have been very polite to everyone. Elsa puts a shoebox on the table and takes off the lid. It's the box Bibi brought to the quay weeks ago: steel collars, cut open, each with a lab number.

zeilen.text: These have been in the safe at my home since the day I got them. That is my seal, and nobody has broken it. Please check it. I would like you to check it.

I logged these at the town hall, as the rules say. Then they were gone for a while. When I found them again, my seal was broken. I still have every number, and I'm telling you this before their lawyers do.
Every number in that box has a name now. I can tell you what each of them weighs. You can write that down too.
The gentleman wants to know who cut them off, First Officer. Will you tell him?

optionen.text: Points at Bibi. “She did. Every one of them.”
Steps up to the table. “We did. Put my name next to hers.”

zeile.text: You don't have to do that. ...All right. Spell it for him.

events.lage: Bibi has been up since before light. She has cleaned every pen at Mochi's, which makes no sense, because nobody is going to need them. Now she stands at the first gate with the field book under one arm and the key in her hand. She has been standing there for a while.

zeilen.text: They're fat, they're bored, and they have started looking at the hills. That's what healthy looks like. I wrote that in my notes weeks ago, and then I didn't do anything about it.
I pressed my best waistcoat for this. Yes, for the animals. A farewell is a farewell, and somebody here should be dressed for it.
They were never mine, you know. I signed for them once, and look how that went. So today I'm not signing for anything. I'm only going to open the gates, one at a time. Will you stay for it?

optionen.text: Takes the key from her hand. “I'll do the first one.”
Stays next to her. “Of course I'll stay.”

events.lage: Biscuit looks back once at the gate, then runs. By the evening a fisherman is feeding a dog at the harbour, and says it isn't his.

zeilen.text: Twenty-one kilos. I said twenty, and you went over, you big biscuit. I'm not sorry. Go on, go!

optionen.text: Watches him go.

events.lage: She walks out of the gate, sits down outside it, and looks back at you. A week later she has an old fisherman, a chair and all of his sardines.

zeilen.text: Seven and a half kilos, exactly the same as the day she came. I fed her for weeks, and it made no difference at all. Try not to frighten anyone, Madame.

optionen.text: Watches her go.

events.lage: She stops at the edge of the macchia and laughs once, not very loud. It's the first time it has sounded like a joke.

zeilen.text: Forty-eight kilos. Ha. Did you hear that? That one was real. She meant it. ...Sorry. I do that.

optionen.text: Watches her go.

events.lage: She goes up the ridge at her own speed and doesn't look back. Duchesses don't. Danzel watches until she is very small.

zeilen.text: Fifty-four kilos, and now all of it is her. There's no steel left on her. I won't tell you to look back, Your Grace. You never do.

optionen.text: Watches her go.

events.lage: He takes one spanner with him. Next week you find a clean spanner on the rail of the yacht, and nobody saw who left it.

zeilen.text: Thirty-seven kilos. Yes, that's Petru's spanner. No, let him have it. He'll bring it back when he has finished with it.

optionen.text: Watches him go.

events.lage: That night there are two voices up on the ridge. Bibi stands at the gate with her coffee and listens until it goes cold.

zeilen.text: Forty-one kilos. She never took food from my hand, not once in all these weeks. I think that's the best thing about her.

optionen.text: Watches her go.

events.lage: There are no red pandas on Corsica. There is one now. The village argues about it, and the children leave out eggs.

zeilen.text: Six kilos. He raised both arms at me this morning, to scare me. I was very scared, Rusty. Go on, you terrible animal.

optionen.text: Watches him go.

events.lage: He gets as far as the creek and stops. A month later there are ducks on him. He has never looked happier, as far as anyone can tell.

zeilen.text: Sixty kilos. There's no rush, Monday. You can take all day. ...You're going to take all day, aren't you?

optionen.text: Watches him go.

events.lage: He trots into the macchia without looking back. Every autumn after that, someone finds a neat pile of truffles by the gate.

zeilen.text: A hundred and thirty-one kilos, and I'm not going to ask how many of those were truffles. Go on. Go and dig.

optionen.text: Watches him go.

events.lage: Bibi drives it up to the high pasture herself. It looks back twice. Up in the alders, something big makes a sound, or maybe that's only the wind.

zeilen.text: Forty kilos, and it's still mostly paws. It won't remember any of this. That was the whole idea. Go on, Pudding. Go on. ...Please go on.

optionen.text: Watches it go.

events.lage: Bibi opens the gate on a Monday. On Thursday Twelve is at the bend in the road. In the spring someone sees her up on the hill, still going, and still furious.

zeilen.text: Nine kilos, the same as ever. She's still looking for the other thirty-nine, you know. I hope she finds a few of them.

optionen.text: Watches her go.

events.lage: He goes up in three slow circles and doesn't come back. But now and then a bone drops onto the quay, from very high up. The fishermen have stopped looking up.

zeilen.text: Six kilos, still. He looked at my skeleton one last time this morning. Go on, you horrible bird. I'll miss you.

optionen.text: Watches him go.

events.lage: Nobody sees her leave. That winter a shepherd comes down from the top of Monte Cinto, and he won't say what he saw in the snow, but he's smiling.

zeilen.text: I never did find out what she weighs. I left her gate open last night, and this morning she had gone. Well. Goodbye, Ghost, I suppose.

optionen.text: Watches her go.

events.lage: It takes him all day to reach the gate, and he doesn't thank anyone. Three weeks later a very expensive villa reports a very large lizard in the pool.

zeilen.text: Ninety-one kilos. That's one whole kilo, in all this time. It's a very big island, Mr. V. Please don't eat anyone important.

optionen.text: Watches him go.

events.lage: The last gate stands open. The pens are very quiet now, and the evening light lies on all that clean straw. Bibi sits down on the wall, opens the field book at the first page and looks at it. Then she closes it.

zeilen.text: That's all of them, every page. I never finished anything before in my life. I don't know what you're supposed to do after.
There are still some out there with the light on. I know where they sleep. I'll go up tomorrow, and the day after, and I'll be boring about it.
And him? He never needed a gate. Somebody should tell him he has a very nice sign.
I'm still going to put his food out tonight. I know. Don't say anything.

optionen.text: Sits down on the wall next to her.

events.lage: A voice message from Madame Casanova, 07:10. Church bells and a lot of pigeons.

zeilen.text: Monsieur, it is Madame Casanova. Still no word from San Martinu. No herbs, no cheese, no brothers.
You said you would climb the macchia and look for them. The path is still there, Monsieur. And the brothers too, I hope.

optionen.text: Texts back: “Going up soon.”
Plays it again. Then checks his bat.

events.lage: A voice message from Petru. Eleven seconds long. The radio in his boathouse is off.

zeilen.text: Hm. Petru. Laetitia is still up in the mountains. Nobody has seen her come down.
The path to the Genoese tower is long. Go up when you can. I am waiting.

optionen.text: Texts back: “I haven't forgotten her.”
Listens to the silence at the end of it.

events.lage: A voice message from Totò. He is whispering, and the harbour is very loud.

zeilen.text: Comandante. Gennaro is still down in the grotto under Punta d'Orsu. Three hours, he said. Three hours!
Low tide is in the day. The boat is ready. I am always ready. Madonna, I am never ready.

optionen.text: Texts back: “Keep the boat ready.”
Sends him a thumbs up and finishes his coffee.

events.lage: A voice message from Lea. Fast, a bit out of breath, and a lot of gulls.

zeilen.text: Okay, don't panic. But Kevin gets bored of his treasures. Then he drops them in the sea.
Page forty of Grandad's chart book. The bay, the cross, 1924. Today, maybe? Please?

optionen.text: Texts back: “Today.”
Puts his shoes on.

events.lage: A voice message from Totò, sent at 06:40. He sounds like he didn't sleep.

zeilen.text: Comandante. At high tide the grotto is humming again. I heard it from the boat, all night.
I am not rowing out there at night. Not for money, not for you. If you want to know, go yourself. In the evening, when the tide is in.

optionen.text: Texts back: “Then I go alone.”
Leaves him on read.

events.lage: Totò again. This time he isn't joking.

zeilen.text: Comandante. One more evening, maybe two, and then we have bigger problems than a humming rock.
If you still want to know what hums in the grotto, go tonight. When the tide is in.

optionen.text: Texts back: “Tonight.”
Deletes it. Some things can stay a mystery.

events.lage: Mina comes across the square with a small parcel. Inside: an old iron key with a ribbon from a crate of seedlings, and a letter in Nonna's hand.

zeilen.text: From Nonna. She says you didn't come, so the mountain comes to you. That's what she said. I don't know what it means.
The letter says: It's the cellar door of the Casanova house. Pascal left it for me. I don't want it. Do you?

optionen.text: Takes the key.

zeile.text: Signed and delivered. That's my job.

optionen.text: “Give it back to her. I'll find another way in.”

zeile.text: Okay. Up the mountain again. My legs hate you.

events.lage: Holm is sitting on the mole with a stick next to her and a row of empty bottles on the wall. Petru is putting up the last one.

zeilen.text: Frankfurt. You still have my rifle. I want it back, so we shoot for it. At the stand, whenever you're ready.
It pulls left. Like the day you won it from me.
And one more thing. That night in the siege, you said nobody goes to the north road, Pascal has it. I should have gone myself. That's mine, not yours.
The sea doesn't hurry. Neither do bottles. Again.

optionen.text: “Tomorrow. And I'm keeping it.”

zeile.text: Faen. We'll see, Frankfurt.

optionen.text: Sits down next to her on the mole first.

zeile.text: My hands are fine now. My head isn't, yet. Takk.

betroffen.was: is standing at the church door

events.lage: Day 24. The village spent the night in the church, and nobody slept much. Smoke still hangs over the square. The church door is open. The door to the back room behind the altar is shut. You are holding two cups of coffee. On someone's phone, Alon's video is playing again, and a man near the fountain asks it out loud: Did you know?

zeilen.text: Sorry, Yacht. I don't know what to say to you today.

zeile.text: For the festa. ...That is a terrible reason. Yes.

optionen.text: Leaves it for today and goes to someone else.

events.lage: The board says: Petru · wood · a table for the whole village. At the back of the workshop, on blocks, lies a small blue boat with a name on the bow: Stella. There is dust on her seats. In front of the workshop: a pile of black beams from the burned houses.

zeilen.text: Stella was Marie's boat. She went out with her every morning, for thirty years. Since Marie died, Stella hasn't touched the water. My own boat is the green one at the quay.
Five years on blocks, Frankfurt. A boat that doesn't swim is only a cupboard.
Maybe it's time she held something again. Or the beams from the fire. Which one?

optionen.text: “Stella. Let her hold the whole village.”

zeile.text: Marie would like that. She always fed too many people.

optionen.text: “The burned beams. Let the fire turn into a table.”

zeile.text: Black wood makes a good table. Stella stays on her blocks. For now.

optionen.text: Leaves this one for another day.

events.lage: The board says: Buenaventura · carrying stones · a stage. Forty pirates wait with their hats in their hands.

zeilen.text: Señor, where do we build it? Where the fire was, or where the people are?

optionen.text: “In front of the post office. Where the fire was.”

zeile.text: Where the fire was. Yes. That is right.

optionen.text: “In front of the church. Where the people are.”

zeile.text: Where the people are! A pirate likes an audience.

optionen.text: Leaves this one for another day.

events.lage: The board says: Bà Tư · cooking too much · the big pot. Bà Tư already has the biggest pot in Corsica on the fire.

zeilen.text: For the festa I cook too much. Like always, but bigger. My way, or your mother's way, con?

optionen.text: “Your way. Always your way.”

zeile.text: Smart boy. My way.

optionen.text: “My mother's way. I'll tell you how she made it.”

zeile.text: Tell me. We cook it together. For her.

optionen.text: Leaves this one for another day.

events.lage: The board says: Lola · cooking · the grill. Lola has written a menu on her arm because she ran out of paper.

zeilen.text: I've been in every kitchen in this village, Boss. Mostly for the biscuits. Who tastes it first?
Boss! The festa menu. Who tastes it first?

optionen.text: “Bà Tư. If she says yes, it's perfect.”

zeile.text: Scary. Good. Scary good.

optionen.text: “Madame Casanova. It's her festa.”

zeile.text: She'll give it a speech. A long one.

optionen.text: “Me. Right now.”

zeile.text: Open wide, Boss. It's hot. Sorry!

optionen.text: Leaves this one for another day.

events.lage: The board says: Buenaventura's men · fishing · the grill at the harbour. The Eventually is ready to go out.

zeilen.text: Señor. The reef, with many small fish? Or the open sea, with one big fish, if you can catch it?

optionen.text: “The reef. Enough for everyone.”

zeile.text: Many small fish. Like my crew.

optionen.text: “The open sea. I'll catch the big one myself.”

zeile.text: Ha! The Señor fishes! I want to see this.

optionen.text: Leaves this one for another day.

events.lage: The board says: Alva · the bar · a drink for every table.

zeilen.text: Papa's recipe, with myrtle? Or a new one? If it's new, you give it a name.

optionen.text: “Papa's recipe.”

zeile.text: Papa's. He'd like that. Don't watch me while I make it.

optionen.text: “A new one. We call it 'The Eventually'.”

zeile.text: The pirates will cry. Good.

optionen.text: “A new one. We call it 'Fresh Bread'.”

zeile.text: Fresh Bread. ...Sandru will know why. Fine.

optionen.text: Leaves this one for another day.

events.lage: The board says: Mina · letters · a garland over the street. Mina has a box of post that nobody can deliver.

zeilen.text: Letters for people who moved away. Or who aren't here any more. Shall I hang them up over the street?

optionen.text: “Yes. All of them.”

zeile.text: All of them. Even the ones from Monaco in the careful hand. Let them hang.

optionen.text: “Yes, but not Pascal's post.”

zeile.text: Okay. His stay in the box.

optionen.text: “No. Flowers. Letters are for reading.”

zeile.text: Flowers. You sound like my mother.

optionen.text: Leaves this one for another day.

events.lage: The board says: Don · the bell · ringing for the dance. The bell is cracked and rings in the wrong rhythm. Don has a pack of cards.

zeilen.text: You let me stay sober once already, at the church door, the night of the siege. Twice is a habit. Cards instead of wine, my son. Shall I win tonight, or will you?
Cards instead of wine, my son. We play until the bell is fixed. Shall I win tonight, or will you?

optionen.text: Plays to win.

zeile.text: You cheat like a fisherman. I like it.

optionen.text: Lets him win.

zeile.text: You let me win. I saw it. Thank you.

optionen.text: “Nobody wins. We play until the bell is fixed.”

zeile.text: Then we play all night. Good.

optionen.text: Leaves this one for another day.

events.lage: The board says: Rosi · machines · lights over the square. Rosi has a box of cables and the steel from the scrap field.

zeilen.text: What goes in the switch, Officer? One of your chips, or a piece of Alon's collars?
Rosi says on the video: one of your chips, or a piece of Alon's collars? Mr. Maximum holds the screwdriver.

optionen.text: Gives her one of his own chips.

zeile.text: Your chip? ...White light. Thank you, Officer.

optionen.text: “A piece of the collars. Let his light shine for us.”

zeile.text: Amber, like Unit-01's eye. I love it.

optionen.text: Leaves this one for another day.

events.lage: The board says: Sandru · his mother's recipes · a table of sweets. Sandru has a tin box with gazelle horns and chebakia.

zeilen.text: Ha. My mother's tin. Do I sell these at the market, under Alon's sign, or only at the festa?

optionen.text: “At the market. Let them see what's not in their system.”

zeile.text: Not in the system. Ha. They'll count it.

optionen.text: “Only at the festa. These are for us.”

zeile.text: For us. Yes. Better.

optionen.text: Leaves this one for another day.

events.lage: The board says: Nonna and Isabelle · the garden · herbs for the tables. Isabelle has already filled three baskets.

zeilen.text: Who gets the first basket? Tell me, before Isabelle gives them all away.

optionen.text: “The long table.”

zeile.text: For everyone. Good answer.

optionen.text: “Bà Tư's pot.”

zeile.text: Ah. She'll say it's too much. It's never too much.

optionen.text: “Frederico. He carries everything.”

zeile.text: Frederico! He'll eat it on the way.

optionen.text: Leaves this one for another day.

events.lage: The board says: Danzel · sewing · the festa dresses. Danzel stands in his shop with pins in his mouth.

zeilen.text: Chiara's dress is finished already! So, whose dress next? I can only finish one more in time!
Whose dress first? I can only finish one in time!

optionen.text: “One of the women from the crew. You choose who.”

zeile.text: I choose. Good. I always choose right.

optionen.text: “Madame Casanova. She wears the same dress every year.”

zeile.text: The mayor! Red. It has to be red.

optionen.text: Leaves this one for another day.

events.lage: The board says: Jana · the children · pictures for the festa. Jana has a pile of drawings from behind the church door.

zeilen.text: Sir, the children made these for the festa. Where do I hang them?

optionen.text: “On the church door.”

zeile.text: On the door they hid behind. That's nice.

optionen.text: “On the stage. Everybody should see them.”

zeile.text: Everybody! They'll be so proud.

optionen.text: Leaves this one for another day.

events.lage: Holm holds the other end of the saw. Halfway through, she stops and looks at the sea through the open door.

zeilen.text: Frankfurt. Thirty-four years at sea. Eleven seasons on the Eden Rise. My mother in Ålesund is old. And I sleep well here. Better than on any bridge.
Since the night before Bergen I have said everything only once. So listen. These four stripes on my shoulders. Do I keep them, or do they go in the table?

optionen.text: “Put them in the table. You can stay.”

zeile.text: Faen. ...Takk. Petru, give me a nail.

optionen.text: “Keep them. One more season, then decide.”

zeile.text: One more. Then we see. That's an honest answer, Frankfurt.

optionen.text: “Don't ask me. Ask Petru.”

zeile.text: Stay.

events.lage: You walk back past the board. Madame Casanova crosses one more name off with a red pencil.

zeilen.text: Good. Who's next, Monsieur? Or is that enough for today?

optionen.text: Walks on to the next name on the board.
“That's enough for today.”

events.lage: The sun is lower now. The board is still there, and so are the names.

zeilen.text: Tomorrow, then. The festa doesn't build itself. ...Mostly it does, but don't tell anyone.

optionen.text: Goes home.

events.lage: Bibi comes across the square with a goat on a rope. The goat is wearing a flower crown and eating it.

zeilen.text: Capra wants to come to the festa. Do we let her?
A goat. At my festa.

optionen.text: “Yes. She's family now.”

zeile.text: Hear that, Capra? Family. Don't eat the dresses.

optionen.text: “No. She'll eat Danzel's dresses.”

zeile.text: Fine. But she'll be sad, and so will I.

events.lage: Bibi sits at the gate of her animal station with her field book. On one page there are forty little lines. Buenaventura has come up to see her, hat in hand.

zeilen.text: So he's got forty men, a boat and nothing to do? And they know every rock in that bay? Doudou. Doudou, come here. I need you to do some numbers.
People pay me to watch a capybara sleep. They'll pay double to see a pirate who's sorry.
Tourists? On my ship? Why would a pirate do that, Señorita?

optionen.text: “Because a pirate with tourists can pay his debts.”
“Because you'd be the head of something.”
“Ask Bibi. It's her idea.”

events.lage: Lea sits at the harbour with her grandfather's chart and draws in the rocks with a pencil. Buenaventura looks over her shoulder.

zeilen.text: Did you know a protected bay needs people who know every rock? Proper people, with boats. And they've got forty!
The wreck is gone, but the bay isn't. Somebody has to show people what's still here.
Tourists? On my ship? Why would a pirate do that?

optionen.text: “Because a pirate with tourists can pay his debts.”
“Because you'd be the head of something.”
“Ask Lea. It's her idea.”

events.lage: Buenaventura takes off his hat and looks at it for a long time.

zeilen.text: The head of... ...I would need a hat.
I'll make you one. Out of an old feeding bucket. Don't ask.
Did you know some sea captains wore two? Probably.
But the grotto belongs to the old man with the oranges. And I owe him everything already.

optionen.text: “Then we go and ask him. Together.”
“Leave the old man to me.”

events.lage: The grotto at low tide. An old man in a linen suit, yellow at the cuffs, sits by the water and peels an orange. Everybody on this coast owes him money. Buenaventura stands behind you with his hat in his hands.

zeilen.text: Last time you came with a knife. Today you came with a captain. Better.
I want to show tourists your grotto. I pay you from every ticket.
Eventually.
...Eventually.
A man in prison pays nobody. A man with tourists pays me every day, a little. I prefer every day. But you want something too, I think. The commission. Why should I come and open my book for you?

optionen.text: “Because Alon paid Buenaventura through you. It's in your book.”

zeile.text: Clever. Not kind. Clever.

optionen.text: “Because nobody pays you if Alon gets the bay.”

zeile.text: Yes. That is the reason. Not kindness.

optionen.text: Says nothing and looks at the empty water where Gennaro's boat used to come in.

zeile.text: Totò's cousin. ...He should hate me. Fine. I'll come.

events.lage: The tide goes out. A flat rock comes up out of the water. Buenaventura climbs onto it and plants his purple flag.

zeilen.text: It is an island. Twice a day.
Here. Your first payment.

optionen.text: Watches the old man hand the pirate a piece of orange.
Takes a piece of orange too.

events.lage: Maxwell stands on the quay with a cool box in his arms, like a baby. A taxi to the airport in Bastia is waiting.

zeilen.text: Number One. Mr. Maximum is going to fly. In an aeroplane. Gogo needs this medicine in Durban, and the post is too slow.
I kept the bandage from the siege, brother. For luck.
Bibi says a plane has no bad temper. Mr. Maximum fed Bones. Mr. Maximum can sit in a plane.
Number One. What does a big man do when he's scared of the sky?

optionen.text: “He takes the window seat and looks anyway.”

zeile.text: The window! Eish. ...Okay. Okay.

optionen.text: Puts a hand on the cool box. “He carries it. Like he always does.”

zeile.text: Like always. Thank you, brother.

optionen.text: “He holds Jana's hand. She's coming to the airport.”

zeile.text: Coach, I'll hold your hand the whole way to Bastia. And I'm not sorry.

events.lage: Early morning. A taxi stops on the square. Maxwell gets out with an empty cool box and a face like a man who has seen the clouds from above.

zeilen.text: Mr. Maximum has flown. We will never speak of it.
Gogo says thank you. And she says you are too thin.

optionen.text: “Welcome back, Maxwell.”
Hugs him, cool box and all.

zeile.text: Eish! Careful, brother. Mr. Maximum is still a bit airsick.

events.lage: Yamamoto has a printout from her bank. She holds it out to Rosi with both hands, like a gift she is ashamed of.

zeilen.text: So sorry, Rosi-san. I read A.V.'s property lists for my bank. There is a street in Catania. Lot 14. A workshop, closed three years ago.
...The press in that workshop was older than Papa. It had a crack in the left side. He called it Old Lady.
Officer. If he goes down, can I buy it back? Tell me the truth.

optionen.text: “If he goes down, yes. So let's make him go down.”

zeile.text: Okay. Then that's the plan. My plan.

optionen.text: “I don't know. But I'll help you try.”

zeile.text: Honest. Annoying. Thank you.

optionen.text: Sits down on the toolbox next to her and waits.

zeile.text: I will wait too. So sorry. I am bad at waiting.

events.lage: Up on the ridge, between the cistus and the rocks, lie the white machines from the siege. Grass grows through their joints. One of them still turns its head when you come closer.

optionen.text: Goes closer, slowly.
Goes back down. Not today.

events.lage: Behind the next rock, two more. They wake up at the same time.

optionen.text: Stands his ground.
Takes the steel he has and goes home.

events.lage: It is quiet now. You fill your bag with good steel. From up here you can see the villa on the other side of the bay.

optionen.text: Carries the steel down to the village.
Looks at the villa for a long time first.

events.lage: Megan has put her laptop on the table. She is wearing her boardroom clothes. On the screen: a dark room in Monaco and one man.

zeilen.text: Officer-san. So sorry. I have stopped the loan to A.V. I did not ask permission. Very rude of me.
Stay out of the picture, First Officer. And don't breathe so loudly.

optionen.text: Stands next to the screen, out of the picture.
Gives her a glass of water first.

events.lage: The man in Monaco listens with his chin in his hand.

zeilen.text: I have names, people who will sign in front of a commission. And papers he can't buy.
It's about a bay that's worth more protected than sold. ...He wants to talk to you, Duc. Is this village worth more than what A.V. pays him?

optionen.text: Steps into the picture. “The numbers are hers. The names are the village's. I just carried the letters.”

zeile.text: That's the first argument I've won that I actually believe in. It's uncomfortable.

optionen.text: “Sell them the bay, and you sell them me with it.”

zeile.text: Bold. He hates bold. It worked.

events.lage: The man in Monaco says: Bring me something better than a fishing village, Megan. The screen goes black.

zeilen.text: How... delightful.

optionen.text: “We still have the commission.”

zeile.text: We have the commission. And we have you. God help us.

optionen.text: Closes the laptop for her.

events.lage: Mina comes running: The market. It's Sandru. In the A.V. Market, Sandru is sitting on the floor between the white shelves. The braces on his legs are quiet. You never noticed the sound until it stopped. A small screen on his knee says: Device paused. The user broke the rules of service. Thank you for your understanding.

zeilen.text: Ha. They switched me off. Like a lamp.
You heard them hum, the first day you came in here. Now listen.
They found the tin. My mother's recipes, under his sign.
And now the screen says I can walk again if I don't talk to the commission. He wants my mouth for my legs.
Duc. The door. Can you hold the door?

optionen.text: Holds the door.
Takes his other arm.
Steps back and lets Alva do it.

events.lage: Alva has not stepped into her mother's old shop since her mother left for Seville. Today she carries her brother out of it, across the street, and up the stairs.

zeilen.text: You're my little brother, you idiot. I've carried you since you were six.
I know. That's the whole problem.

optionen.text: Walks behind them up the stairs.
Waits at the bottom of the stairs, so they can be alone.

events.lage: Sandru sits on a chair in Alva's bar. On his legs: the same braces, with a new box on the side, painted in Rosi's colours.

zeilen.text: Same motors. Same chips. I only took out the part that talks to his computers. The leash, Officer. Like with the collars. That sound is mine now. Don't let them tell you otherwise.
Rosi says which way on the video, I hold the screwdriver. Teamwork, brother.
A.V. gave me six years of walking. You gave me a speech. ...And her. You gave me her. So what do I do now, Duc? Walk over there and say what?

optionen.text: “Say thank you. Then say nothing.”

zeile.text: Ha. One thing at a time, Duc.

optionen.text: “Go and stand in front of Alva. Straight.”

zeile.text: Straight. Okay. ...She's going to cry. I'm going to cry.

optionen.text: Shrugs. “You gave yourself the speech. I just listened.”

zeile.text: Then I'll give it to the men from Ajaccio too. The whole thing.

events.lage: In the morning Sandru walks across the square again. The braces hum. He doesn't look at you.

zeilen.text: I said yes to the screen, Duc. Legs for a quiet mouth. Don't look at me like that. Nobody else offered.

optionen.text: “I should have offered. I'm sorry.”

zeile.text: Yeah. Me too.

optionen.text: Lets him walk past.

events.lage: Mina hands you an envelope made of very good paper. Your name is on it, in a careful hand.

zeilen.text: This one's for you, Yacht. The good paper. From the house on the hill.
It says: Dinner. Tomorrow at eight. Just you. A.V. ...Yacht, that's the hand from the name sheet you picked up at the gate. And from the letters on the church steps.
It says: Dinner. Tomorrow at eight. Just you. A.V.
Are you going?

optionen.text: “Yes.”
“Yes. But not alone.”
“I don't know yet.”

events.lage: The evening before the villa. The festa is the day after tomorrow, and everybody already knows: after midnight, the mole belongs to whoever is standing there with you. Tonight, people come to ask.

zeilen.text: Yacht. Everybody's asking who you'll be with after midnight. I'm not asking. I just know you'll have to answer.

optionen.text: Waits on the quay.

events.lage: She finds you before you find her.

zeilen.text: First Officer. I'll ask you once, and if you laugh, it's a two. After midnight, on the mole. Will you come?

optionen.text: “Yes.”
“Not this time. I'm sorry.”

zeile.text: Okay. That's a three. ...For the night, not for you.

events.lage: She finds you before you find her.

zeilen.text: After my dance, Duc, I close the bar for one hour. Will you be on the quay?

optionen.text: “Yes.”
“Not this time. I'm sorry.”

zeile.text: Fine. I'll close the bar for nobody, then. Nobody is good company.

events.lage: She finds you before you find her.

zeilen.text: After midnight, on the mole. Will you come? Proper come?

optionen.text: “Yes.”
“Not this time. I'm sorry.”

zeile.text: Okay. Did you know octopuses hide when they're sad? I'm going to hide a bit.

events.lage: She finds you before you find her.

zeilen.text: Ten euros says you'll come down to the mole after midnight. ...Oh. Have I just lost?

optionen.text: “Yes.”
“Not this time. I'm sorry.”

zeile.text: Then I keep my ten euros. It's not much comfort, darling.

optionen.text: “Yes.”
“Not this time. I'm sorry.”

zeile.text: Okay. The dress comes off anyway. For me.

zeilen.text: Boss. When the cooking's done. One song, just us, on the mole. Mostly one song. Yes?

optionen.text: “Yes.”
“Not this time. I'm sorry.”

zeile.text: Oh. No worries, Boss. Mostly no worries.

zeilen.text: No camera after midnight. Will you meet me by the water?

optionen.text: “Yes.”
“Not this time. I'm sorry.”

zeile.text: Okay. Thank you for saying it to my face. Nobody does that.

zeilen.text: The gates open on Sunday afternoon, and I'll be a mess. After midnight, will you come anyway?

optionen.text: “Yes.”
“Not this time. I'm sorry.”

zeile.text: Then I'll sit with the animals. They never say no.

optionen.text: “Yes.”
“Not this time. I'm sorry.”

zeile.text: Noted, First Officer. We never spoke of it. That part is easy.

zeilen.text: Good night, Yacht. Don't be late on Sunday. Midnight comes fast at a festa.

optionen.text: Goes to bed.

events.lage: The quay is quiet again. Nobody waits for you after midnight, and that's fine. The festa is for everyone.

zeilen.text: Nobody? Then you dance with me. Once. Badly.

optionen.text: “Deal, Mina.”

events.lage: The morning of the dinner. Holm, Rosi and Madame Casanova stand at the end of the quay. Up on the hill, the villa shines in the sun.

zeilen.text: You're invited, Frankfurt. That's better than a search warrant.
A cellar door nobody locks properly. Old iron. My favourite kind of door.
I know the cellar. I hid there from my father when I was seven. I'll take you.
Who goes down with you, Frankfurt?

optionen.text: Nods at Rosi. “You and me.”

events.lage: Petru sits in front of his workshop and mends a net. It is the same net as every afternoon, and it is not broken. The radio on the workbench plays Corsican football, very quietly.
